sentences.zh: 志第十七五行昔得《河圖》、《洛書》六十五字，治水有功，因而寶之。

translations.literal: Treatise 17, Five Phases: In antiquity Yu received the River Chart and Luo Writ of sixty-five characters; because he had merit in controlling the waters, he therefore treasured them.
translations.idiomatic: Treatise 17, on the Five Phases. In antiquity, when Yu received the sixty-five characters of the River Chart and Luo Writ, he had merit in controlling the floods and therefore treasured them.

sentences.zh: 殷太師箕子入周，武王訪其事，乃陳《洪範》九疇之法，其一曰五行。

translations.literal: The Grand Master of Yin, Jizi, entered Zhou; King Wu inquired of him about these matters, and he then set forth the method of the Nine Categories of the Great Plan, the first of which is called the Five Phases.
translations.idiomatic: Jizi, Grand Master of Yin, came to Zhou; King Wu questioned him about these matters, and he presented the method of the Nine Categories of the Hong Fan, the first of which concerns the Five Phases.

sentences.zh: 漢興，董仲舒、劉向治《春秋》，論災異，乃引九疇之說，附於二百四十二年行事，一推咎徵天人之變。

translations.literal: When Han arose, Dong Zhongshu and Liu Xiang studied the Spring and Autumn Annals and discussed portents and anomalies; they drew on the theory of the Nine Categories and attached it to the events of the 242 years, tracing in each case the signs of blame and the transformations between Heaven and humanity.
translations.idiomatic: When the Han dynasty rose, Dong Zhongshu and Liu Xiang studied the Spring and Autumn Annals and discussed portents and anomalies. They drew on the doctrine of the Nine Categories and applied it to the events of the 242 years, tracing in each case the signs of culpability and the transformations between Heaven and humankind.

sentences.zh: 班固敘漢史，采其說《五行志》。

translations.literal: Ban Gu narrated Han history and adopted their theory in the Treatise on the Five Phases.
translations.idiomatic: In narrating Han history, Ban Gu adopted their theories in the Treatise on the Five Phases.

sentences.zh: 綿代史官，因而纘之。

translations.literal: Generation after generation of historiographers have continued and compiled it thereafter.
translations.idiomatic: Successive generations of court historians have continued and compiled it in turn.

sentences.zh: 今略舉大端，以明變怪之本。

translations.literal: Now I briefly set forth the main points to clarify the root of omens and anomalies.
translations.idiomatic: Here I briefly set forth the main points to clarify the foundation of portents and anomalies.

sentences.zh: 《經》曰：「水曰潤下，火曰炎上，木曰曲直，金曰從革，土爰稼穡。

translations.literal: The Classic says: "Water is called soaking downward, fire is called blazing upward, wood is called bending and straightening, metal is called yielding and reforming, earth is for sowing and reaping.
translations.idiomatic: The Classic says: "Water moistens downward, fire blazes upward, wood bends and straightens, metal yields to reforming, and earth is for sowing and reaping.

sentences.zh: 」又曰：「建用皇極。

translations.literal: " It also says: "Establish and employ the sovereign standard.
translations.idiomatic: " It also says: "Establish and employ the sovereign standard.

sentences.zh: 」《傳》曰：「畋獵不時，飲食不享，出入不節，奪民農時，及有奸謀，則木不曲直。

translations.literal: " The Tradition says: "When hunting is untimely, food and drink are not offered in sacrifice, comings and goings lack restraint, the people's farming seasons are seized, and there are treacherous plots, then wood does not bend and straighten.
translations.idiomatic: " The Tradition says: "When hunting is untimely, food and drink are not ritually offered, comings and goings lack restraint, the people's farming seasons are seized, and there are treacherous plots, then wood does not bend and straighten.

sentences.zh: 棄法律，逐功臣，殺太子，以妾為妻，則火不炎上。

translations.literal: When laws are abandoned, meritorious ministers are driven off, the heir apparent is killed, and a concubine is made wife, then fire does not blaze upward.
translations.idiomatic: When laws are abandoned, meritorious ministers are driven away, the heir apparent is killed, and a concubine is made wife, then fire does not blaze upward.

sentences.zh: 好治宮室，飾臺榭，內淫亂，犯親戚，侮父兄，則稼穡不成。

translations.literal: When one delights in building palaces, adorning terraces and pavilions, indulges in licentiousness within, violates kin, and insults fathers and elder brothers, then sowing and reaping do not succeed.
translations.idiomatic: When a ruler delights in building palaces and adorning terraces and pavilions, indulges in licentious conduct within the palace, violates kin, and insults fathers and elder brothers, then sowing and reaping do not succeed.

sentences.zh: 好戰功，輕百姓，飾城郭，侵邊境，則金不從革。

translations.literal: When one delights in military achievement, treats the common people lightly, adorns walls and ramparts, and encroaches on borderlands, then metal does not yield and reform.
translations.idiomatic: When a ruler delights in military achievement, treats the common people lightly, adorns walls and ramparts, and encroaches on the borderlands, then metal does not yield to reforming.

sentences.zh: 簡宗廟，不禱祠，廢祭祀，逆天時，則水不潤下。

translations.literal: When ancestral temples are neglected, prayers and sacrifices are omitted, sacrifices are abolished, and heavenly seasons are violated, then water does not soak downward.
translations.idiomatic: When ancestral temples are neglected, prayers and sacrifices are omitted, rites are abolished, and the seasons of Heaven are violated, then water does not moisten downward.

sentences.zh: 」《經》曰「敬用五事」，謂「貌曰恭，言曰從，視曰明，聽曰聰，思曰睿。

translations.literal: " The Classic says "Reverently employ the five matters," meaning "bearing is called respectful, speech is called compliant, sight is called discerning, hearing is called acute, thought is called perceptive.
translations.idiomatic: " The Classic says, "Reverently employ the five matters," meaning "bearing is called respectful, speech is called compliant, sight is called discerning, hearing is called acute, and thought is called perceptive.

sentences.zh: 恭作肅，從作乂，明作哲，聰作謀，睿作聖。

translations.literal: Respectfulness becomes solemnity, compliance becomes governance, discernment becomes wisdom, acuteness becomes counsel, perceptiveness becomes sagacity.
translations.idiomatic: Respectfulness becomes solemnity, compliance becomes good governance, discernment becomes wisdom, acuteness becomes counsel, and perceptiveness becomes sagacity.

sentences.zh: 」又曰「建用皇極」，「皇建其有極」。

translations.literal: " It also says "Establish and employ the sovereign standard," "The sovereign establishes that standard."
translations.idiomatic: " It also says, "Establish and employ the sovereign standard," and "The sovereign establishes that standard."

sentences.zh: 《傳》曰「貌之不恭，是謂不肅，厥咎狂，厥罰恆雨，厥極凶。

translations.literal: The Tradition says: "When bearing is not respectful, this is called lack of solemnity; its blame is frenzy, its punishment is constant rain, its utmost is misfortune.
translations.idiomatic: The Tradition says: "When bearing is not respectful, this is called lack of solemnity; the blame is frenzy, the punishment is constant rain, and the utmost consequence is misfortune.

sentences.zh: 時則有服妖，時則有龜孽，時則有雞禍，時則有下體生上之屙，時則有青眚青祥。

translations.literal: At such times there are garment omens, at such times turtle prodigies, at such times chicken calamities, at such times prodigies of the lower body generating upon the upper, at such times green calamities and green auspices.
translations.idiomatic: At such times there are garment omens, turtle prodigies, chicken calamities, prodigies in which the lower body generates upon the upper, and green calamities and green auspices.

sentences.zh: 凡草木之類謂之妖，蟲豸之類謂之孽，六畜謂之禍，及人謂之屙，甚則異物生謂之眚，身外而來謂之祥也。

translations.literal: All among plants and trees are called ya, among insects and vermin are called nie, the six domestic animals are called huo, involving humans is called e, when severe and strange things are born it is called sheng, what comes from outside the body is called xiang.
translations.idiomatic: Anomalies among plants and trees are called ya; among insects and vermin, nie; among the six domestic animals, huo; those involving humans, prodigies; when strange things are born in extreme form, this is called sheng; what comes from outside is called an auspice.

sentences.zh: 言之不從，是謂不乂，厥咎僭，厥罰恆暘，厥極憂。

translations.literal: When speech is not compliant, this is called lack of governance; its blame is overstepping, its punishment is constant drought, its utmost is sorrow.
translations.idiomatic: When speech is not compliant, this is called lack of good governance; the blame is overstepping, the punishment is constant drought, and the utmost consequence is sorrow.

sentences.zh: 時則有詩妖，時則有介蟲之孽，時則有犬禍，時則有口舌之屙，時則有白眚白祥。

translations.literal: At such times there are poetic omens, at such times shell-bearing insect prodigies, at such times canine calamities, at such times oral prodigies, at such times white calamities and white auspices.
translations.idiomatic: At such times there are poetic omens, shell-bearing insect prodigies, canine calamities, oral prodigies, and white calamities and white auspices.

sentences.zh: 視之不明，是謂不哲，厥咎豫，厥罰恆燠，厥極疾。

translations.literal: When sight is not discerning, this is called lack of wisdom; its blame is complacency, its punishment is constant heat, its utmost is illness.
translations.idiomatic: When sight is not discerning, this is called lack of wisdom; the blame is complacency, the punishment is constant heat, and the utmost consequence is illness.

sentences.zh: 時則有草妖，時則有臝蟲之孽，時則有羊禍，時則有目屙，時則有赤眚赤祥。

translations.literal: At such times there are grass omens, at such times naked insect prodigies, at such times sheep calamities, at such times eye prodigies, at such times red calamities and red auspices.
translations.idiomatic: At such times there are grass omens, naked insect prodigies, sheep calamities, eye prodigies, and red calamities and red auspices.

sentences.zh: 聽之不聰，是謂不謀，厥咎急，厥罰恆寒，厥極貧。

translations.literal: When hearing is not acute, this is called lack of counsel; its blame is haste, its punishment is constant cold, its utmost is poverty.
translations.idiomatic: When hearing is not acute, this is called lack of counsel; the blame is haste, the punishment is constant cold, and the utmost consequence is poverty.

sentences.zh: 時則有鼓妖，時則有魚孽，時則有豕禍，時則有耳屙，時則有黑眚黑祥。

translations.literal: At such times there are drum omens, at such times fish prodigies, at such times swine calamities, at such times ear prodigies, at such times black calamities and black auspices.
translations.idiomatic: At such times there are drum omens, fish prodigies, swine calamities, ear prodigies, and black calamities and black auspices.

sentences.zh: 思之不睿，是謂不聖，厥咎蒙，厥罰恆風，厥極凶短折。

translations.literal: When thought is not perceptive, this is called lack of sagacity; its blame is obscurity, its punishment is constant wind, its utmost is misfortune, brevity, and broken life.
translations.idiomatic: When thought is not perceptive, this is called lack of sagacity; the blame is obscurity, the punishment is constant wind, and the utmost consequence is misfortune, brevity, and untimely death.

sentences.zh: 時則有脂夜之妖，時則有華孽，時則有牛禍，時則有心腹之屙，時則有黃眚黃祥。

translations.literal: At such times there are grease-and-night omens, at such times flower prodigies, at such times bovine calamities, at such times heart-and-belly prodigies, at such times yellow calamities and yellow auspices.
translations.idiomatic: At such times there are grease-and-night omens, flower prodigies, bovine calamities, heart-and-belly prodigies, and yellow calamities and yellow auspices.

sentences.zh: 皇之不極，是謂不建，厥咎眊，厥罰恆陰，厥極弱。

translations.literal: When the sovereign lacks the utmost standard, this is called failure to establish; its blame is dim-sightedness, its punishment is constant overcast, its utmost is weakness.
translations.idiomatic: When the sovereign lacks the utmost standard, this is called failure to establish it; the blame is dim-sightedness, the punishment is constant overcast skies, and the utmost consequence is weakness.

sentences.zh: 時則有射妖，時則有龍蛇之孽，時則有馬禍，時則有下體代上之屙，時則有日月亂行、星辰逆行。

translations.literal: At such times there are archery omens, at such times dragon-and-serpent prodigies, at such times equine calamities, at such times prodigies of the lower replacing the upper, at such times the sun and moon run in disorder and the stars move retrograde.
translations.idiomatic: At such times there are archery omens, dragon-and-serpent prodigies, equine calamities, prodigies in which the lower replaces the upper, and the sun and moon run in disorder while the stars move retrograde.

sentences.zh: 」九疇名數十五，其要五行、皇極之說，前賢所以窮治亂之變，談天人之際，蓋本於斯。

translations.literal: " The Nine Categories number fifteen in name; their essentials are the doctrines of the Five Phases and the sovereign standard. Former sages therefore exhaustively traced the transformations of order and disorder and discussed the juncture between Heaven and humanity—this is fundamentally based on these.
translations.idiomatic: " The Nine Categories comprise fifteen names in all; their essentials are the doctrines of the Five Phases and the sovereign standard. Former sages traced the transformations of order and disorder and discussed the relationship between Heaven and humankind on this foundation.

sentences.zh: 故先錄其言，以傳於事。

translations.literal: Therefore I first record their words to transmit them in connection with events.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore their words are recorded first, to be transmitted together with the events they explain.

sentences.zh: 京房《易傳》曰：「臣事雖正，專必地震。

translations.literal: Jing Fang's Commentary on the Changes says: "Although a minister's conduct may be correct, if he is autocratic there will surely be an earthquake.
translations.idiomatic: Jing Fang's Commentary on the Changes says: "Although a minister's conduct may be correct, if he acts autocratically there will surely be an earthquake.

sentences.zh: 其震，于水則波，於木則搖，於屋則瓦落，大經在辟而易臣，茲謂陰動。

translations.literal: When it quakes, in water there are waves, in wood there is swaying, in houses tiles fall; the great norm lies in the sovereign while the Changes speak of ministers—this is called yin stirring.
translations.idiomatic: When it quakes, water forms waves, wood sways, and roof tiles fall from houses. The great norm rests with the sovereign while the Changes speak of ministers—this is called the stirring of yin.

sentences.zh: 」又曰：「小人剝廬，厥妖山崩，茲謂陰乘陽，弱勝強。

translations.literal: " It also says: "When petty men strip the hut, its omen is mountains collapsing—this is called yin riding upon yang, the weak overcoming the strong.
translations.idiomatic: " It also says: "When petty men strip the hut, the omen is mountains collapsing—this means yin riding upon yang, the weak overcoming the strong.

sentences.zh: 」劉向曰：「金木水沴土，地所以震。

translations.literal: " Liu Xiang said: "Metal, wood, and water harm earth—therefore the ground quakes.
translations.idiomatic: " Liu Xiang said: "When metal, wood, and water harm earth, the ground quakes.

sentences.zh: 」《春秋》災異，先書地震、日蝕，惡陰盈也。

translations.literal: " In the Spring and Autumn Annals, among portents and anomalies earthquakes and solar eclipses are recorded first, because yin's fullness is detested.
translations.idiomatic: " In the Spring and Autumn Annals, among portents and anomalies earthquakes and solar eclipses are recorded first, because the fullness of yin is regarded with detestation.

sentences.zh: 正月二十二日，松、叢二州地震，壞人廬舍。

translations.literal: On the twenty-second day of the first month, Song and Cong prefectures suffered an earthquake that destroyed people's dwellings.
translations.idiomatic: On the twenty-second day of the first month, Song and Cong prefectures were struck by an earthquake that destroyed people's homes.

sentences.zh: 二十年九月十五日，靈州地震，有聲如雷。

translations.literal: On the fifteenth day of the ninth month in the twentieth year, Ling Prefecture suffered an earthquake with a sound like thunder.
translations.idiomatic: On the fifteenth day of the ninth month in the twentieth year, Ling Prefecture was struck by an earthquake with a sound like thunder.

sentences.zh: 二十三年八月一日，晉州地震，壞人廬舍，壓死者五十餘人。

translations.literal: On the first day of the eighth month in the twenty-third year, Jin Prefecture suffered an earthquake that destroyed people's dwellings; more than fifty were crushed to death.
translations.idiomatic: On the first day of the eighth month in the twenty-third year, Jin Prefecture was struck by an earthquake that destroyed people's homes, and more than fifty were crushed to death.

sentences.zh: 三日，又震。

translations.literal: On the third day it quaked again.
translations.idiomatic: On the third day there was another quake.

sentences.zh: 十一月五日，又震。

translations.literal: On the fifth day of the eleventh month it quaked again.
translations.idiomatic: On the fifth day of the eleventh month there was another quake.

sentences.zh: 四月一日，又震。

translations.literal: On the first day of the fourth month it quaked again.
translations.idiomatic: On the first day of the fourth month there was another quake.

sentences.zh: 六月十二日，又震。

translations.literal: On the twelfth day of the sixth month it quaked again.
translations.idiomatic: On the twelfth day of the sixth month there was another quake.

sentences.zh: 高宗顧謂侍臣曰：「朕政教不明，使晉州之地，屢有震動。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozong turned to his attendant ministers and said: "My governance and instruction are unclear, causing the region of Jin Prefecture to quake repeatedly.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozong turned to his attendant ministers and said, "My governance and instruction are unclear, and this has caused the region of Jin Prefecture to quake again and again.

sentences.zh: 」侍中張行成曰：「天，陽也；

translations.literal: " Chief Minister Zhang Xingcheng said: "Heaven is yang;
translations.idiomatic: " Chief Minister Zhang Xingcheng said, "Heaven is yang;

sentences.zh: 地，陰也。

translations.literal: earth is yin.
translations.idiomatic: earth is yin.

sentences.zh: 陽，君象；

translations.literal: Yang is the image of the ruler;
translations.idiomatic: Yang is the image of the ruler;

sentences.zh: 陰，臣象。

translations.literal: yin is the image of the minister.
translations.idiomatic: yin is the image of the minister.

sentences.zh: 君宜轉動，臣宜安靜。

translations.literal: The ruler ought to move and turn; ministers ought to be still and quiet.
translations.idiomatic: The ruler ought to be active and responsive; ministers ought to remain still and steady.

sentences.zh: 今晉州地震，彌旬不休，臣將恐女謁用事，大臣陰謀。

translations.literal: Now Jin Prefecture has quaked for more than ten days without cease; your servant fears that women favorites will hold power and great ministers will plot in secret.
translations.idiomatic: Now Jin Prefecture has quaked for more than ten days without cease. Your servant fears that women favorites will wield power and great ministers are plotting in secret.

sentences.zh: 且晉州，陛下本封，今地屢震，尤彰其應。

translations.literal: Moreover Jin Prefecture was Your Majesty's original enfeoffment; that the land now quakes repeatedly makes the correspondence especially clear.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, Jin Prefecture was Your Majesty's original fief, and that the land now quakes repeatedly makes the omen especially clear.

sentences.zh: 伏願深思遠慮，以杜其萌。

translations.literal: I humbly hope Your Majesty will ponder deeply and take far-reaching counsel to cut off these beginnings.
translations.idiomatic: I humbly hope Your Majesty will ponder deeply and take far-reaching counsel to cut off these troubles at the root.

sentences.zh: 」帝深然之。

translations.literal: " The emperor deeply approved of this.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor strongly agreed.

sentences.zh: 二月十八日，秦州地震。

translations.literal: On the eighteenth day of the second month, Qin Prefecture suffered an earthquake.
translations.idiomatic: On the eighteenth day of the second month, Qin Prefecture was struck by an earthquake.

sentences.zh: 先是，秦州百姓聞州西北地下殷殷有聲，俄而地震，壞廨宇及居人廬舍數千間，地拆而復合，震經時不定，壓死百餘人。

translations.literal: Earlier, the people of Qin Prefecture heard a deep rumbling underground northwest of the prefecture; presently an earthquake came, destroying several thousand government offices and private dwellings, the ground splitting open and closing again, the quaking continuing for a long time without settling, and more than a hundred were crushed to death.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, the people of Qin Prefecture had heard a deep rumbling underground to the northwest of the prefectural seat. Soon an earthquake struck, destroying several thousand government offices and private homes. The ground split open and closed again, and the shaking continued for a long time without abating. More than a hundred people were crushed to death.

sentences.zh: 玄宗令右丞相蕭嵩致祭山川，又遣倉部員外郎韋伯陽往宣慰，存恤所損之家。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuanzong ordered Right Chancellor Xiao Song to offer sacrifices to mountains and rivers, and also sent Wei Boyang, an outer-office director in the Ministry of Revenue, to proclaim consolation and provide relief to the households that had suffered damage.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuanzong ordered Right Chancellor Xiao Song to offer sacrifices to the mountains and rivers, and also sent Wei Boyang of the Ministry of Revenue to proclaim consolation and provide relief to the households that had suffered damage.

sentences.zh: 十一月辛亥朔，河西地震有聲，地裂陷，壞廬舍，張掖、酒泉尤甚。

translations.literal: On the first day of the eleventh month, xinhai, Hexi suffered an earthquake with sound; the ground split and sank, dwellings were destroyed, and Zhangye and Jiuquan were especially hard hit.
translations.idiomatic: On the first day of the eleventh month, on a xinhai day, Hexi was struck by an earthquake with a rumbling sound. The ground split and sank, dwellings were destroyed, and Zhangye and Jiuquan suffered especially severe damage.

sentences.zh: 至二載六月始止。

translations.literal: It did not cease until the sixth month of the second year.
translations.idiomatic: The quakes did not cease until the sixth month of the second year.

sentences.zh: 十一月壬申，京師地震，有聲自東北來，如雷者三。

translations.literal: On renshen day of the eleventh month, the capital suffered an earthquake; a sound came from the northeast like thunder three times.
translations.idiomatic: On a renshen day in the eleventh month, the capital was struck by an earthquake. A sound came from the northeast like thunder three times.

sentences.zh: 四年二月丙辰夜，京師地震，有聲如雷者三。

translations.literal: On the night of bingchen day in the second month of the fourth year, the capital suffered an earthquake with a sound like thunder three times.
translations.idiomatic: On the night of a bingchen day in the second month of the fourth year, the capital was struck by an earthquake with a sound like thunder three times.

sentences.zh: 十一月己卯夜，京師地震，是夕者三，巢鳥皆驚，人多去室。

translations.literal: On the night of jimao day in the eleventh month, the capital suffered an earthquake; that night there were three, nesting birds were all startled, and many people left their rooms.
translations.idiomatic: On the night of a jimao day in the eleventh month, the capital was struck by an earthquake three times that night. Nesting birds were all startled, and many people fled their rooms.

sentences.zh: 東都、蒲、陝亦然。

translations.literal: The Eastern Capital, Pu, and Shan were the same.
translations.idiomatic: The Eastern Capital, Pu, and Shan were affected as well.

sentences.zh: 四年正月朔日，德宗御含元殿受朝賀。

translations.literal: On the first day of the first month in the fourth year, Emperor Dezong took the Hall of Encompassing Primacy to receive court congratulations.
translations.idiomatic: On New Year's Day in the fourth year, Emperor Dezong took the Hall of Encompassing Primacy to receive the court's New Year congratulations.

sentences.zh: 是日質明，殿階及欄檻三十餘間，無故自壞，甲士死者十餘人。

translations.literal: That day at dawn, more than thirty sections of the hall steps and balustrades collapsed for no apparent reason, and more than ten armored soldiers died.
translations.idiomatic: That day at dawn, more than thirty sections of the hall steps and balustrades collapsed for no apparent reason, and more than ten armored guards were killed.

sentences.zh: 其夜，京師地震。

translations.literal: That night the capital suffered an earthquake.
translations.idiomatic: That night the capital was struck by an earthquake.

sentences.zh: 二日又震，三日又震，十八日又震，十九日又震，二十日又震。

translations.literal: On the second day it quaked again, on the third again, on the eighteenth again, on the nineteenth again, and on the twentieth again.
translations.idiomatic: It quaked again on the second day, again on the third, again on the eighteenth, again on the nineteenth, and again on the twentieth.

sentences.zh: 帝謂宰臣曰：「蓋朕寡德，屢致後土震驚，但當修政，以答天譴耳。

translations.literal: The emperor said to his chief ministers: "Surely I lack virtue and have repeatedly caused the earth below to tremble in alarm; I need only reform government to answer Heaven's reproof."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said to his chief ministers, "Surely I lack virtue and have repeatedly caused the earth to tremble in alarm. I need only reform government to answer Heaven's reproof."

sentences.zh: 」二十三日又震，二十四日又震，二十五日又震，時金、房州尤甚，江溢山裂，屋宇多壞，人皆露處。

translations.literal: " On the twenty-third it quaked again, on the twenty-fourth again, on the twenty-fifth again; at that time Jin and Fang prefectures were especially severe—rivers overflowed, mountains split, many buildings were destroyed, and people all slept in the open.
translations.idiomatic: " It quaked again on the twenty-third, again on the twenty-fourth, and again on the twenty-fifth. At that time Jin and Fang prefectures were especially hard hit: rivers overflowed, mountains split open, many buildings were destroyed, and people were forced to sleep in the open.

sentences.zh: 至二月三日壬午，又震，甲申又震，乙酉又震，丙申又震。

translations.literal: Until the third day of the second month, renwu, it quaked again; on jiashen again, on yiyou again, on bingshen again.
translations.idiomatic: By the third day of the second month, on a renwu day, it quaked again; then again on a jiashen day, again on a yiyou day, and again on a bingshen day.

sentences.zh: 三月甲寅，已震，己未又震，庚午又震，辛未又震。

translations.literal: On jiayin day in the third month it had already quaked; on jiwei it quaked again, on gengwu again, on xinwei again.
translations.idiomatic: On a jiayin day in the third month it had already quaked; it quaked again on a jiwei day, again on a gengwu day, and again on a xinwei day.

sentences.zh: 京師地生毛，或白或黃，有長尺餘者。

translations.literal: In the capital the ground produced hair, white or yellow, some more than a foot long.
translations.idiomatic: In the capital the ground sprouted hair, white or yellow, some more than a foot in length.

sentences.zh: 五月丁卯，又震。

translations.literal: On dingmao day in the fifth month it quaked again.
translations.idiomatic: On a dingmao day in the fifth month there was another quake.

sentences.zh: 八月甲辰，又震，其聲如雷。

translations.literal: On jiachen day in the eighth month it quaked again, its sound like thunder.
translations.idiomatic: On a jiachen day in the eighth month there was another quake, with a sound like thunder.

sentences.zh: 九年四月辛酉，京師又震，有聲如雷。

translations.literal: On xinyou day in the fourth month of the ninth year, the capital quaked again with a sound like thunder.
translations.idiomatic: On a xinyou day in the fourth month of the ninth year, the capital was struck by another earthquake with a sound like thunder.

sentences.zh: 河中尤甚，壞城壘廬舍，地裂水湧。

translations.literal: Hezhong was especially severe: city walls and ramparts and dwellings were destroyed, the ground split and water gushed forth.
translations.idiomatic: Hezhong was especially hard hit: city walls, ramparts, and dwellings were destroyed, the ground split open, and water gushed forth.

sentences.zh: 十年四月戊申，又震。

translations.literal: On wushen day in the fourth month of the tenth year it quaked again.
translations.idiomatic: On a wushen day in the fourth month of the tenth year there was another quake.

sentences.zh: 十三年十月乙未日午時，震從東來，須臾而止。

translations.literal: At the noon hour on yiwei day in the tenth month of the thirteenth year, the quake came from the east and ceased after a moment.
translations.idiomatic: At noon on a yiwei day in the tenth month of the thirteenth year, the quake came from the east and ceased after a moment.

sentences.zh: 八月，京師地震。

translations.literal: In the eighth month the capital suffered an earthquake.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month the capital was struck by an earthquake.

sentences.zh: 憲宗謂侍臣曰：「昨地震，草樹皆搖，何祥異也？

translations.literal: Emperor Xianzong said to his attendant ministers: "Yesterday there was an earthquake and grass and trees all swayed—what omen or anomaly is this?
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xianzong said to his attendant ministers, "Yesterday there was an earthquake and grass and trees all swayed. What kind of omen is this?

sentences.zh: 」宰臣李絳曰：「昔周時地震，三川竭，太史伯陽甫謂周君曰：『天地之氣，不過其序。

translations.literal: " Chief Minister Li Jiang said: "In antiquity during Zhou there was an earthquake and the three rivers dried up; Grand Astrologer Boyang Fu said to the Zhou ruler: 'The qi of Heaven and Earth do not exceed their proper order.
translations.idiomatic: " Chief Minister Li Jiang said, "In antiquity, during the Zhou, there was an earthquake and the three rivers dried up. Grand Astrologer Boyang Fu said to the Zhou ruler, 'The qi of Heaven and Earth do not exceed their proper order.

sentences.zh: 若過其序，人亂也。

translations.literal: If they exceed their order, humanity is in disorder.
translations.idiomatic: If they exceed their order, humanity is in disorder.

sentences.zh: 人政乖錯，則上感陰陽之氣，陽伏而不能出，陰迫而不能升，於是有地震。

translations.literal: When human government is perverse and mistaken, above it moves the qi of yin and yang; yang lies hidden and cannot emerge, yin presses and cannot rise—thereupon there is an earthquake.
translations.idiomatic: When human government is perverse and mistaken, it stirs the qi of yin and yang above. Yang lies hidden and cannot emerge, yin presses down and cannot rise—and then there is an earthquake.

sentences.zh: 』又孔子修《春秋》，所紀災異，先地震、日蝕，蓋地載萬物，日君象，政有感傷，天地見眚，書之示戒，用儆後王。

translations.literal: ' Moreover when Confucius compiled the Spring and Autumn Annals, among the portents and anomalies he recorded, earthquakes and solar eclipses came first—for earth bears all things, the sun is the image of the ruler; when government suffers injury, Heaven and Earth display calamities; recording them shows warning, to admonish later kings.
translations.idiomatic: ' Moreover, when Confucius compiled the Spring and Autumn Annals, among the portents and anomalies he recorded, earthquakes and solar eclipses came first—for earth bears all things and the sun is the image of the ruler. When government suffers injury, Heaven and Earth display calamities. Recording them serves as a warning to admonish later kings.

sentences.zh: 伏願陛下體勵虔恭之誠，動以利萬物、綏萬方為念，則變異自消，休征可致。

translations.literal: I humbly hope Your Majesty will embody and encourage sincere reverence, and in every action keep in mind benefiting the myriad things and bringing peace to the myriad regions—then anomalies will vanish of themselves and auspicious signs may be attained.
translations.idiomatic: I humbly hope Your Majesty will embody sincere reverence and keep in mind, in every action, benefiting all things and bringing peace to the realm—then anomalies will vanish of themselves and auspicious signs may be attained.

sentences.zh: 」九年三月丙辰，巂州地震，晝夜八十震方止，壓死者百餘人。

translations.literal: " On bingchen day in the third month of the ninth year, Xi Prefecture suffered an earthquake; for day and night there were eighty quakes before it ceased, and more than a hundred were crushed to death.
translations.idiomatic: " On a bingchen day in the third month of the ninth year, Xi Prefecture was struck by an earthquake. For a full day and night there were eighty quakes before it ceased, and more than a hundred people were crushed to death.

sentences.zh: 三月乙卯，京師地震。

translations.literal: On yimao day in the third month the capital suffered an earthquake.
translations.idiomatic: On a yimao day in the third month the capital was struck by an earthquake.

sentences.zh: 二月乙亥夜四更，京師地震，屋瓦皆墜，戶牖之間有聲。

translations.literal: On the night of yihai day in the second month, at the fourth watch, the capital suffered an earthquake; roof tiles all fell, and there was sound between doors and windows.
translations.idiomatic: On the night of a yihai day in the second month, during the fourth watch, the capital was struck by an earthquake. Roof tiles all fell, and there was a rumbling sound between doors and windows.

sentences.zh: 二年十一月乙丑夜，地南北微震。

translations.literal: On the night of yichou day in the eleventh month of the second year, the ground quaked slightly from south to north.
translations.idiomatic: On the night of a yichou day in the eleventh month of the second year, the ground quaked slightly from south to north.

sentences.zh: 十月，京師地震，振武、天德、靈武、鹽、夏等州皆震，壞軍鎮廬舍。

translations.literal: In the tenth month the capital suffered an earthquake; Zhenwu, Tiande, Lingwu, Yan, Xia, and other prefectures all quaked, destroying army posts and dwellings.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month the capital was struck by an earthquake. Zhenwu, Tiande, Lingwu, Yan, Xia, and other prefectures all quaked, destroying military posts and dwellings.

sentences.zh: 七月二十日，巂州山崩，川水咽流。

translations.literal: On the twentieth day of the seventh month, mountains in Xi Prefecture collapsed and river waters were choked in their flow.
translations.idiomatic: On the twentieth day of the seventh month, mountains in Xi Prefecture collapsed and river waters were choked in their course.

sentences.zh: 七月七日，隴右山崩，大蛇屢見。

translations.literal: On the seventh day of the seventh month, mountains in Longyou collapsed and great serpents were repeatedly seen.
translations.idiomatic: On the seventh day of the seventh month, mountains in Longyou collapsed and great serpents were repeatedly sighted.

sentences.zh: 太宗問秘書監虞世南曰：「是何災異？

translations.literal: Emperor Taizong asked Director of the Palace Library Yu Shinan: "What portent or anomaly is this?
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taizong asked Director of the Palace Library Yu Shinan, "What kind of portent is this?

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「春秋時梁山崩，晉侯召伯宗而問焉。

translations.literal: " He replied: "In Spring and Autumn times Mount Liang collapsed; the Marquis of Jin summoned Bo Zong and questioned him.
translations.idiomatic: " He replied, "In Spring and Autumn times Mount Liang collapsed, and the Marquis of Jin summoned Bo Zong to question him about it.

sentences.zh: 對曰：『國主山川，故山崩川竭，君為之不舉，降服出次，祝幣以禮焉。

translations.literal: He answered: 'The state is master of mountains and rivers; therefore when mountains collapse and rivers dry up, the ruler for this does not raise music, lowers his garments and goes out to a temporary lodging, and offers prayer silks according to ritual.
translations.idiomatic: He answered, 'The state is master of the mountains and rivers. Therefore when mountains collapse and rivers dry up, the ruler should suspend music, don mourning garments and move to a temporary lodging, and offer prayer silks according to ritual.

sentences.zh: 』晉侯從之，卒亦無害。

translations.literal: ' The Marquis of Jin followed this, and in the end suffered no harm.
translations.idiomatic: ' The Marquis of Jin followed this advice, and in the end suffered no harm.

sentences.zh: 漢文帝九年，齊、楚地二十九山同日崩。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Emperor Wen of Han, twenty-nine mountains in Qi and Chu lands collapsed on the same day.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year of Emperor Wen of Han, twenty-nine mountains in the Qi and Chu regions collapsed on the same day.

sentences.zh: 文帝出令，郡國無來獻，施惠於天下，遠近歡洽，亦不為災。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen issued an edict that commanderies and kingdoms should not come with tribute offerings, and extended favor throughout the realm; near and far were harmonious, and it likewise did not become a disaster.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen issued an edict that the commanderies and kingdoms should not come bearing tribute, and extended favor throughout the realm. Near and far were harmonious, and no disaster followed.

sentences.zh: 後漢靈帝時，青蛇見御座。

translations.literal: In the time of Emperor Ling of Later Han, a green serpent appeared at the imperial seat.
translations.idiomatic: During the reign of Emperor Ling of Later Han, a green serpent appeared at the imperial throne.

sentences.zh: 晉惠帝時，大蛇長三百步，經市入廟。

translations.literal: In the time of Emperor Hui of Jin, a great serpent three hundred paces long passed through the market and entered a temple.
translations.idiomatic: During the reign of Emperor Hui of Jin, a great serpent three hundred paces long passed through the market and entered a temple.

sentences.zh: 今蛇見山澤，蓋深山大澤，實生龍蛇，亦不足怪也。

translations.literal: Now that serpents are seen in mountains and marshes, surely deep mountains and great marshes truly produce dragons and serpents—this is not enough to be considered strange.
translations.idiomatic: As for serpents now being seen in mountains and marshes, deep mountains and great marshes truly do produce dragons and serpents—this is hardly strange enough to count as a portent.

sentences.zh: 唯修德可以消變。

translations.literal: Only cultivating virtue can dispel such transformations.
translations.idiomatic: Only by cultivating virtue can such portents be dispelled.

sentences.zh: 」上然之。

translations.literal: " The emperor approved of this.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 十七年八月四日，涼州昌松縣鴻池谷有石五，青質白文，成字曰「高皇海出多子李元王八十年太平天子李世民千年太子李治書燕山人士樂太國主尚汪譚獎文仁邁千古大王五王六王七王十鳳毛才子七佛八菩薩及上果佛田天子文武貞觀昌大聖延四方上下治示孝仙戈入為善。

translations.literal: On the fourth day of the eighth month in the seventeenth year, at Hongchi Valley in Changsong County, Liang Prefecture, there were five stones of green substance with white writing, forming characters that read: "Supreme Emperor, the sea brings forth many sons; King Li Yuan; eighty years; Son of Heaven of great peace Li Shimin; a thousand years; Crown Prince Li Zhi; book; Yanshan; men of the realm rejoice; supreme lord of the great state; Shang Wang Tan; award; Wen; benevolence surpassing a thousand ages; great king; five kings; six kings; seven kings; ten; phoenix-haired talents; seven Buddhas; eight bodhisattvas; and supreme fruit; Buddha field; Son of Heaven; civil and martial; Zhenguan; flourishing greatness; sage extending; four quarters above and below; governed; showing filial piety; immortal; Ge; entering; acting for good."
translations.idiomatic: On the fourth day of the eighth month in the seventeenth year, at Hongchi Valley in Changsong County, Liang Prefecture, five stones of green substance bearing white inscriptions appeared, forming characters that read: "Supreme Emperor, the sea brings forth many sons; King Li Yuan; eighty years; Son of Heaven of great peace Li Shimin; a thousand years; Crown Prince Li Zhi," and continuing through a long prophetic inscription naming rulers, heirs, sage-kings, Buddhas and bodhisattvas, the Zhenguan reign, universal governance, filial piety, and the blessing of goodness.

sentences.zh: 」涼州奏。

translations.literal: " Liang Prefecture reported this.
translations.idiomatic: " Liang Prefecture reported the discovery.

sentences.zh: 其年十一月三日，遣使祭之，曰：「嗣天子某，祚繼鴻業，君臨宇縣，夙興旰食，無忘於政，導德齊禮，愧于前修。

translations.literal: On the third day of the eleventh month that year, envoys were sent to offer sacrifice, saying: "The succeeding Son of Heaven, so-and-so, his throne continuing the great enterprise, ruling the realm, rising early and eating late, never forgetting governance, guiding virtue and equalizing ritual—yet ashamed before former exemplars.
translations.idiomatic: On the third day of the eleventh month that year, envoys were sent to offer sacrifice with this declaration: "The succeeding Son of Heaven, bearing the great enterprise forward and ruling the realm, rises early and retires late, never neglecting government, guiding virtue and harmonizing ritual—yet remains ashamed before the achievements of former sages.

sentences.zh: 天有成命，表瑞貞石，文字昭然，歷數唯永。

translations.literal: Heaven has a fulfilled mandate; the steadfast stone displays the auspice, the characters clear and bright, the succession destined for eternity.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven has fulfilled its mandate; the steadfast stone displays this auspice, its characters clear and bright, and the dynastic succession destined to endure.

sentences.zh: 既旌高廟之業，又錫眇身之祚。

translations.literal: It honors the achievement of the High Temple and also bestows fortune upon this insignificant person.
translations.idiomatic: It honors the achievement of the imperial ancestors and also bestows fortune upon my humble person.

sentences.zh: 迨于皇太子治，亦降貞符，具紀姓氏，列于石言。

translations.literal: As for the Crown Prince Zhi, he too has received the true talisman; surnames are fully recorded and set forth in the stone's words.
translations.idiomatic: As for Crown Prince Zhi, he too has received the true talisman; our surnames are fully recorded and inscribed in the stone's words.

sentences.zh: 仰瞻睿漢，空銘大造，甫惟寡薄，彌增寅懼。

translations.literal: Gazing up at the wise Milky Way, I can only inscribe the great creation; I am but slight and thin, which only increases my reverent fear.
translations.idiomatic: Gazing up at Heaven's wisdom, I can only inscribe my gratitude for the great creation; I am but slight and unworthy, which only deepens my reverent awe.

sentences.zh: 敢因大禮，重薦玉帛，上謝明靈之貺，以申祗慄之誠。

translations.literal: I venture, through the great rites, again to offer jade and silk, above to thank the bright spirits' bestowal, and below to express reverent awe.
translations.idiomatic: I venture, through these great rites, again to offer jade and silk, to thank the bright spirits for their blessing and to express my reverent devotion.

sentences.zh: 八月二十日，隕石十八于同州馮翊縣，光曜，有聲如雷。

translations.literal: On the twentieth day of the eighth month, eighteen meteorites fell in Fuyi County, Tong Prefecture, shining brightly with a sound like thunder.
translations.idiomatic: On the twentieth day of the eighth month, eighteen meteorites fell in Fuyi County, Tong Prefecture, shining brightly with a sound like thunder.

sentences.zh: 上問于志寧曰：「此何祥也？

translations.literal: The emperor asked Yu Zhining: "What omen is this?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked Yu Zhining, "What kind of omen is this?

sentences.zh: 當由朕政之有闕。

translations.literal: It must be due to faults in my governance.
translations.idiomatic: It must be due to faults in my governance.

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「按《春秋》，隕石于宋五，內史過曰：『是陰陽之事，非吉凶所生。

translations.literal: " He replied: "According to the Spring and Autumn Annals, five meteorites fell in Song; Inner Scribe Guo said: 'This is a matter of yin and yang, not something from which fortune and misfortune arise.
translations.idiomatic: " He replied, "According to the Spring and Autumn Annals, five meteorites fell in Song. Inner Scribe Guo said, 'This is a matter of yin and yang, not something from which fortune and misfortune arise.

sentences.zh: 』自古災變，杳不可測，但恐物之自爾，未必關於人事。

translations.literal: ' Since antiquity calamities and transformations have been obscure and beyond measure; I only fear things follow their own course and are not necessarily connected to human affairs.
translations.idiomatic: ' Since antiquity calamities and transformations have been obscure and beyond prediction. I only fear that things follow their own course and are not necessarily connected to human affairs.

sentences.zh: 陛下發書誡懼，責躬自省，未必不為福矣。

translations.literal: Your Majesty issues edicts of warning and fear, blames yourself and examines your conduct—this may well turn into blessing.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty issues edicts of warning, blames yourself, and examines your conduct—this may well turn misfortune into blessing.

sentences.zh: 」永昌中，華州敷水店西南坡，白晝飛四五里，直抵赤水，其坡上樹木禾黍，宛然無損。

translations.literal: " During the Yongchang era, on the southwest slope of Fushui post station in Hua Prefecture, [the ground] flew four or five li in broad daylight, reaching straight to Chishui; the trees and grain on that slope remained entirely undamaged.
translations.idiomatic: " During the Yongchang era, the southwest slope of Fushui post station in Hua Prefecture flew four or five li in broad daylight, reaching straight to the Chishui River. The trees and grain on that slope remained entirely undamaged.

sentences.zh: 則天時，新豐縣東南露臺鄉，因大風雨雹震，有山踴出，高二百尺，有池週三頃，池中有龍鳳之形、禾麥之異。

translations.literal: In the time of Empress Wu, at Loutai township southeast of Xinfeng County, because of great wind, rain, hail, and quaking, a mountain surged forth two hundred feet high, with a pool three qing in circumference; in the pool were forms of dragons and phoenixes and strange grain and wheat.
translations.idiomatic: During the reign of Empress Wu, at Loutai township southeast of Xinfeng County, a great windstorm with rain, hail, and quaking caused a mountain to surge forth two hundred feet high, with a pool three qing in circumference. In the pool appeared forms of dragons and phoenixes and strange grain and wheat.

sentences.zh: 則天以為休征，名為慶山。

translations.literal: Empress Wu regarded it as an auspicious sign and named it Mount Qing.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Wu regarded it as an auspicious sign and named it Mount of Celebration.

sentences.zh: 荊州人俞文俊詣闕上書曰：「臣聞天氣不和而寒暑隔，人氣不和而疣贅生，地氣不和而堆阜出。

translations.literal: Yu Wenjun of Jing Prefecture came to the palace gate and submitted a memorial saying: "Your servant has heard that when heavenly qi is not harmonious, cold and heat are separated; when human qi is not harmonious, warts and excrescences grow; when earthly qi is not harmonious, mounds and knolls emerge.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Wenjun of Jing Prefecture came to the palace and submitted a memorial saying, "Your servant has heard that when heavenly qi is not harmonious, cold and heat fall out of balance; when human qi is not harmonious, warts and excrescences grow; when earthly qi is not harmonious, mounds and knolls emerge.

sentences.zh: 今陛下以女主居陽位，反易剛柔，故地氣隔塞，山變為災。

translations.literal: Now Your Majesty, a woman ruler occupying the yang position, has reversed hard and soft; therefore earthly qi is blocked and mountains turn into calamity.
translations.idiomatic: Now Your Majesty, a woman ruler occupying the yang position, has reversed hard and soft. Therefore earthly qi is blocked and mountains become calamities.

sentences.zh: 陛下以為慶山，臣以為非慶也。

translations.literal: Your Majesty regards it as Mount of Celebration; your servant believes it is not celebration.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty regards it as the Mount of Celebration, but your servant believes it is no cause for celebration.

sentences.zh: 誠宜側身修德，以答天譴。

translations.literal: You truly ought to restrain yourself and cultivate virtue to answer Heaven's reproof.
translations.idiomatic: You truly ought to restrain yourself and cultivate virtue to answer Heaven's reproof.

sentences.zh: 不然，恐災禍至。

translations.literal: Otherwise, I fear calamity will come.
translations.idiomatic: Otherwise, I fear calamity will follow.

sentences.zh: 」則天怒，流於嶺南。

translations.literal: " Empress Wu was enraged and exiled him to Lingnan.
translations.idiomatic: " Empress Wu was enraged and exiled him to Lingnan.

sentences.zh: 四月五日，大風震電，藍田山開百餘步。

translations.literal: On the fifth day of the fourth month, great wind, quaking, and lightning split open Lantian Mountain for more than a hundred paces.
translations.idiomatic: On the fifth day of the fourth month, a great windstorm with quaking and lightning split open Lantian Mountain for more than a hundred paces.

sentences.zh: 六月，虢州閺鄉縣界黃河內女媧墓，天寶十三載因大雨晦冥，失其所在，至今年六月一日夜，河濱人家忽聞風雨聲，曉見其墓踴出，上有雙柳樹，下有巨石二，柳各長丈餘。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, at the tomb of Nüwa within the Yellow River on the border of Min township, Guo Prefecture—in the thirteenth year of Tianbao, because of great rain and darkness, its location was lost—until the night of the first day of the sixth month this year, households along the river suddenly heard the sound of wind and rain; at dawn they saw the tomb surge forth, with a pair of willow trees above and two great stones below, each willow more than a zhang in height.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, at the tomb of Nüwa within the Yellow River on the border of Min township, Guo Prefecture—in the thirteenth year of Tianbao, great rain and darkness had caused its location to be lost—until the night of the first day of the sixth month this year, when households along the river suddenly heard wind and rain. At dawn they saw the tomb surge forth, topped by a pair of willow trees and supported below by two great stones, each willow more than a zhang in height.

sentences.zh: 郡守圖畫以聞，今號風陵堆。

translations.literal: The prefectural governor drew it and reported; it is now called Fengling Mound.
translations.idiomatic: The prefectural governor drew a record and reported it; the site is now called Fengling Mound.

sentences.zh: ，郴州黃芩山崩震，壓殺數百人。

translations.literal: In Chen Prefecture, Huangqin Mountain collapsed in a quake and crushed several hundred people to death.
translations.idiomatic: In Chen Prefecture, Huangqin Mountain collapsed in a quake, crushing several hundred people to death.

sentences.zh: 建中初，魏州魏縣西四十里，忽然土長四五尺數畝，里人駭異之。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Jianzhong era, forty li west of Wei County, Wei Prefecture, earth suddenly rose four or five feet over several mu; the villagers were alarmed and astonished.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Jianzhong era, forty li west of Wei County in Wei Prefecture, the earth suddenly rose four or five feet over several mu of ground, and the local people were alarmed and astonished.

sentences.zh: 明年，魏博田悅反，德宗命河東馬燧、潞州李抱真討之，營於陘山。

translations.literal: The next year Tian Yue of Weibo rebelled; Emperor Dezong ordered Ma Sui of Hedong and Li Baozhen of Lu Prefecture to campaign against him, encamping at Xing Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: The following year Tian Yue of Weibo rebelled. Emperor Dezong ordered Ma Sui of Hedong and Li Baozhen of Lu Prefecture to campaign against him, and they encamped at Xing Mountain.

sentences.zh: 幽州朱滔、恆州王武俊帥兵救田悅，王師退保魏縣西。

translations.literal: Zhu Tao of You Prefecture and Wang Wujun of Heng Prefecture led troops to rescue Tian Yue; the imperial army withdrew to defend west of Wei County.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Tao of You Prefecture and Wang Wujun of Heng Prefecture led troops to rescue Tian Yue, and the imperial army withdrew to defend west of Wei County.

sentences.zh: 朱滔、武俊、田悅引軍與王師對壘。

translations.literal: Zhu Tao, Wang Wujun, and Tian Yue led their armies to face the imperial forces in camp.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Tao, Wang Wujun, and Tian Yue led their armies to face the imperial forces in opposing camps.

sentences.zh: 三年十一月，朱滔僭稱冀王，武俊稱趙王，田悅稱魏王。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of the third year, Zhu Tao presumptuously styled himself King of Ji, Wang Wujun King of Zhao, and Tian Yue King of Wei.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of the third year, Zhu Tao presumptuously styled himself King of Ji, Wang Wujun King of Zhao, and Tian Yue King of Wei.

sentences.zh: 悅時壘正當土長之所，及僭署告天，乃因其長土為壇以祭。

translations.literal: Yue's camp at the time lay right where the earth had risen; when he presumptuously took office and announced it to Heaven, he used the risen earth as an altar for sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: Yue's camp at the time lay exactly where the earth had risen. When he presumptuously assumed royal title and announced it to Heaven, he used the risen earth as an altar for sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 魏州功曹韋稔為《益土頌》以媚悅。

translations.literal: Wei Mi, records officer of Wei Prefecture, composed an "Ode on the Increased Earth" to flatter Yue.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Mi, records officer of Wei Prefecture, composed an "Ode on the Increased Earth" to flatter Yue.

sentences.zh: 馬燧聞之，笑曰：「田悅異常賊也。

translations.literal: When Ma Sui heard of this, he laughed and said: "Tian Yue is an extraordinary rebel.
translations.idiomatic: When Ma Sui heard of this, he laughed and said, "Tian Yue is an extraordinary rebel.

sentences.zh: 七月一日，黃氣竟天，大雨，谷水溢，入洛陽宮，深四尺，壞左掖門，毀宮寺一十九；

translations.literal: On the first day of the seventh month, yellow qi filled the sky; great rain fell, the Gu River overflowed and entered the Luoyang palace to a depth of four feet, destroying the Left Flank Gate and ruining nineteen palace temples;
translations.idiomatic: On the first day of the seventh month, yellow qi filled the sky. Great rain fell, the Gu River overflowed and entered the Luoyang palace to a depth of four feet, destroying the Left Flank Gate and ruining nineteen palace temples;

sentences.zh: 洛水暴漲，漂六百餘家。

translations.literal: the Luo River rose violently and swept away more than six hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: the Luo River rose violently and swept away more than six hundred households.

sentences.zh: 帝引咎，令群臣直言政之得失。

translations.literal: The emperor blamed himself and ordered the ministers to speak frankly of the gains and losses in government.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor blamed himself and ordered his ministers to speak frankly about the strengths and failings of government.

sentences.zh: 中書侍郎岑文本曰：「伏唯陛下覽古今之事，察安危之機，上以社稷為重，下以億兆為念。

translations.literal: Zhongshu Vice Minister Cen Wenben said: "I humbly hope Your Majesty will survey affairs ancient and modern and discern the mechanisms of security and danger, above taking the altars of soil and grain as weighty, below keeping the hundred millions in mind.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongshu Vice Minister Cen Wenben said, "I humbly hope Your Majesty will survey affairs ancient and modern and discern what brings security and danger, taking the state as your highest concern and keeping the welfare of the people in mind.

sentences.zh: 明選舉，慎賞罰，進賢才，退不肖。

translations.literal: Make clear appointments, be careful in rewards and punishments, advance the worthy and talented, and dismiss the unworthy.
translations.idiomatic: Make appointments wisely, be careful in rewards and punishments, advance the worthy and talented, and dismiss the unworthy.

sentences.zh: 聞過即改，從諫如流。

translations.literal: When you hear of faults, reform at once; follow remonstrance as water flows.
translations.idiomatic: When you hear of faults, reform at once; follow remonstrance as readily as flowing water.

sentences.zh: 為善在於不疑，出令期於必信。

translations.literal: Doing good lies in not doubting; issuing orders expects certain faith.
translations.idiomatic: Doing good requires steadfast resolve; issuing orders requires that they be surely believed.

sentences.zh: 頤神養性，省畋遊之娛；

translations.literal: Nourish the spirit and cultivate nature, reducing the pleasures of hunting;
translations.idiomatic: Nourish your spirit and cultivate your nature, reducing the pleasures of the hunt;

sentences.zh: 去奢從儉，減工役之費。

translations.literal: discard extravagance and follow frugality, reducing the costs of labor and corvée.
translations.idiomatic: discard extravagance and follow frugality, reducing the costs of labor and corvée.

sentences.zh: 務靜方內，不求辟土；

translations.literal: devote effort to tranquillity within the realm, not seeking to open new territory;
translations.idiomatic: Devote effort to tranquillity within the realm, not seeking to open new territory;

sentences.zh: 載橐弓矢，而無忘武備。

translations.literal: put bow and arrows in the case, yet do not forget military preparedness.
translations.idiomatic: sheath bow and arrows, yet do not forget military preparedness.

sentences.zh: 凡此數者，願陛下行之不怠，必當轉禍為福，化咎為祥。

translations.literal: Of all these several points, I hope Your Majesty will practice them without slackening; you will surely turn misfortune into blessing and transform blame into auspice.
translations.idiomatic: In all these matters, I hope Your Majesty will practice them without slackening; you will surely turn misfortune into blessing and transform blame into auspice.

sentences.zh: 況水之為患，陰陽常理，豈可謂之天譴而系聖心哉！

translations.literal: Moreover, that water becomes a calamity is the regular principle of yin and yang—how can it be called Heaven's reproof and bind the sage heart!
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, floods are a regular manifestation of yin and yang—how can they be called Heaven's reproof and weigh upon Your Majesty's heart!

sentences.zh: 」十三日，詔曰：「暴雨為災，大水泛溢，靜思厥咎，朕甚懼焉。

translations.literal: " On the thirteenth day an edict said: "Violent rain has become a calamity and great waters have overflowed; pondering the blame in silence, We are greatly afraid.
translations.idiomatic: " On the thirteenth day an edict proclaimed: "Violent rain has become a calamity and great waters have overflowed. Pondering where the blame lies, We are deeply afraid.

sentences.zh: 文武百僚，各上封事，極言朕過，無有所諱。

translations.literal: Civil and military officials of every rank, each submit sealed memorials, speaking to the utmost of Our faults, concealing nothing.
translations.idiomatic: Let civil and military officials of every rank submit sealed memorials, speaking frankly of Our faults without concealment.

sentences.zh: 諸司供進，悉令減省。

translations.literal: All departments' tribute offerings are altogether ordered reduced.
translations.idiomatic: All departments' tribute offerings are to be reduced.

sentences.zh: 凡所力役，量事停廢。

translations.literal: All corvée labor is to be halted or abolished according to circumstances.
translations.idiomatic: All corvée labor is to be halted or abolished as circumstances require.

sentences.zh: 遭水之家，賜帛有差。

translations.literal: Households that suffered flooding are granted silk in varying amounts.
translations.idiomatic: Households that suffered flooding are to receive grants of silk in varying amounts.

sentences.zh: 」二十日，詔廢明德宮及飛山宮之玄圃院，分給河南、洛陽遭水戶。

translations.literal: " On the twentieth day an edict abolished Mingde Palace and the Mystic Garden court of Feishan Palace, distributing them to flood-stricken households in Henan and Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: " On the twentieth day an edict abolished Mingde Palace and the Mystic Garden court of Feishan Palace, distributing the land to flood-stricken households in Henan and Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 九月，黃河氾濫，壞陝州河北縣及太原倉，毀河陽中潬，太宗幸白馬阪以觀之。

translations.literal: In the ninth month the Yellow River overflowed, destroying Hebei County in Shan Prefecture and the Taiyuan granary, ruining the central ford of Heyang; Emperor Taizong visited Baima Slope to observe it.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month the Yellow River overflowed, destroying Hebei County in Shan Prefecture and the Taiyuan granary and ruining the central ford of Heyang. Emperor Taizong visited Baima Slope to observe the flood.

sentences.zh: 六月，恆州大雨，自二日至七日。

translations.literal: In the sixth month Heng Prefecture had great rain from the second to the seventh day.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month Heng Prefecture had heavy rain from the second to the seventh day.

sentences.zh: 滹沱河水泛溢，損五千三百家。

translations.literal: The Hutuo River overflowed, damaging five thousand three hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: The Hutuo River overflowed, damaging five thousand three hundred households.

sentences.zh: 七月，冀州奏：六月十三日夜降雨，至二十日，水深五尺，其夜暴水深一丈已上，壞屋一萬四千三百九十區，害田四千四百九十六頃。

translations.literal: In the seventh month Ji Prefecture reported: from the night of the thirteenth day of the sixth month rain fell until the twentieth; water was five feet deep, and that night violent water was more than a zhang deep, destroying fourteen thousand three hundred ninety dwellings and harming four thousand four hundred ninety-six qing of fields.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month Ji Prefecture reported that from the night of the thirteenth day of the sixth month rain fell until the twentieth. The water reached five feet in depth, and that night a sudden flood exceeded a zhang in depth, destroying fourteen thousand three hundred ninety dwellings and damaging four thousand four hundred ninety-six qing of fields.

sentences.zh: 九月十八日，括州暴風雨，海水翻上，壞永嘉、安固二縣城百姓廬舍六千八百四十三區，殺人九千七十、牛五百頭，損田苗四千一百五十頃。

translations.literal: On the eighteenth day of the ninth month, Kuozhou had a violent windstorm and rain; seawater surged upward, destroying six thousand eight hundred forty-three dwellings of common people in the cities of Yongjia and Angu counties, killing nine thousand seventy persons and five hundred cattle, and damaging four thousand one hundred fifty qing of seedling fields.
translations.idiomatic: On the eighteenth day of the ninth month, Kuozhou suffered a violent windstorm and rain. Seawater surged inland, destroying six thousand eight hundred forty-three dwellings in the cities of Yongjia and Angu counties, killing nine thousand seventy people and five hundred cattle, and damaging four thousand one hundred fifty qing of seedling fields.

sentences.zh: 五月十四日，連日澍雨，山水溢，溺死五千餘人。

translations.literal: On the fourteenth day of the fifth month, for successive days there was soaking rain; mountains and rivers overflowed, and more than five thousand drowned.
translations.idiomatic: On the fourteenth day of the fifth month, soaking rain fell for successive days. Mountains and rivers overflowed, and more than five thousand people drowned.

sentences.zh: 六月十二日，連日大雨，至二十三日，洛水大漲，漂損河南立德弘敬、洛陽景行等坊二百餘家，壞天津橋及中橋，斷人行累日。

translations.literal: On the twelfth day of the sixth month, for successive days there was great rain until the twenty-third; the Luo River rose greatly, sweeping and damaging more than two hundred households in the Lide, Hongjing, and Jingxing wards of Henan and Luoyang, destroying the Tianjin Bridge and Central Bridge and cutting off travel for many days.
translations.idiomatic: On the twelfth day of the sixth month, heavy rain fell for successive days until the twenty-third. The Luo River rose sharply, sweeping away more than two hundred households in the Lide, Hongjing, and Jingxing wards of Henan and Luoyang, destroying the Tianjin Bridge and Central Bridge and cutting off travel for many days.

sentences.zh: 先是，頓降大雨，沃若懸流，至是而泛溢衝突焉。

translations.literal: Earlier, heavy rain had fallen in bursts, pouring down like a hanging torrent; by this time it overflowed and clashed.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, heavy rain had fallen in bursts like a hanging torrent; by this time the waters overflowed and surged in conflict.

sentences.zh: 西京平地水深四尺已上，麥一束止得一二升，米一斗二百二十文，布一端止得一百文。

translations.literal: In the Western Capital the level ground had water more than four feet deep; a bundle of wheat yielded only one or two sheng, rice was two hundred twenty cash per dou, and a bolt of cloth only one hundred cash.
translations.idiomatic: In the Western Capital the level ground stood more than four feet deep in water. A bundle of wheat yielded only one or two sheng, rice sold for two hundred twenty cash per dou, and a bolt of cloth for only one hundred cash.

sentences.zh: 國中大饑，蒲、同等州沒徙家口並逐糧，饑餒相仍，加以疾疫，自陝至洛，死者不可勝數。

translations.literal: Throughout the realm there was great famine; in Pu, Tong, and other prefectures submerged migrants' households all pursued grain; hunger followed hunger, and pestilence was added besides; from Shan to Luo the dead were beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: Throughout the realm there was great famine. In Pu, Tong, and other prefectures displaced households all pursued grain wherever they could find it. Hunger followed upon hunger, and pestilence was added besides. From Shan to Luo the dead were beyond counting.

sentences.zh: 西京米鬥三百已下。

translations.literal: In the Western Capital rice fell below three hundred cash per dou.
translations.idiomatic: In the Western Capital the price of rice fell below three hundred cash per dou.

sentences.zh: 二年三月，洛州黃河水溺河陽縣城，水面高於城內五六尺。

translations.literal: In the third month of the second year, the Yellow River in Luozhou inundated Heyang county city; the water surface was five or six feet higher than within the city.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the second year, the Yellow River in Luozhou inundated Heyang county city, and the water surface stood five or six feet higher than the ground within the city.

sentences.zh: 自鹽坎已下至縣十里石灰，並平流，津橋南北道無不碎破。

translations.literal: From Yankan down to the county for ten li, lime and stone were all swept level; ferry bridges and roads north and south were all shattered.
translations.idiomatic: From Yankan down to the county for ten li, lime and stone were all swept level. Ferry bridges and roads north and south were all shattered.

sentences.zh: 七月，溫州大水，漂流四千餘家。

translations.literal: In the seventh month Wen Prefecture had great flooding that swept away more than four thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month Wen Prefecture suffered great flooding that swept away more than four thousand households.

sentences.zh: ，寧州大霖雨，山水暴漲，漂流二千餘家，溺死者千餘人，流屍東下。

translations.literal: In Ning Prefecture there was great prolonged rain; mountains and rivers rose violently, sweeping away more than two thousand households; more than a thousand drowned, and corpses floated eastward downstream.
translations.idiomatic: In Ning Prefecture prolonged heavy rain caused mountains and rivers to rise violently, sweeping away more than two thousand households. More than a thousand people drowned, and corpses floated eastward downstream.

sentences.zh: 十七日，京師大雨雹，人有凍死者。

translations.literal: On the seventeenth day the capital had great rain and hail; some people froze to death.
translations.idiomatic: On the seventeenth day the capital suffered heavy rain and hail, and some people froze to death.

sentences.zh: 四年，自九月至十月，晝夜陰晦，大雨雪。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, from the ninth to the tenth month, day and night were dim and overcast with great rain and snow.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year, from the ninth to the tenth month, day and night were dim and overcast with heavy rain and snow.

sentences.zh: 都中人畜，有餓凍死者。

translations.literal: Among people and livestock in the capital, some died of hunger and cold.
translations.idiomatic: Among people and livestock in the capital, some died of hunger and cold.

sentences.zh: 令開倉賑恤。

translations.literal: An order was issued to open granaries for relief.
translations.idiomatic: An order was issued to open the granaries for relief.

sentences.zh: 七月二十七日，洛水漲，壞百姓廬舍二千餘家。

translations.literal: On the twenty-seventh day of the seventh month the Luo River rose and destroyed more than two thousand common people's dwellings.
translations.idiomatic: On the twenty-seventh day of the seventh month the Luo River rose and destroyed more than two thousand common people's dwellings.

sentences.zh: 詔九品已上直言極諫，右衛騎曹宋務光上疏曰：

translations.literal: An edict ordered officials of the ninth rank and above to speak frankly with utmost remonstrance; Song Wuguang, cavalry adjutant of the Right Guard, submitted a memorial saying:
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered officials of the ninth rank and above to speak frankly with utmost remonstrance. Song Wuguang, cavalry adjutant of the Right Guard, submitted a memorial saying:

sentences.zh: 疏奏不省。

translations.literal: The memorial was submitted but not heeded.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was submitted but not heeded.

sentences.zh: 右僕射唐休璟以霖雨為害，咎在主司，上表曰：「臣聞天運其工，人代之而為理；

translations.literal: Right Vice Director Tang Xiujing, because prolonged rain was harmful, blamed the chief office and submitted a memorial saying: "Your servant has heard that Heaven operates its craft and humanity replaces it in governing;
translations.idiomatic: Right Vice Director Tang Xiujing, holding that the harm of prolonged rain lay with the chief minister's office, submitted a memorial saying, "Your servant has heard that Heaven operates its craft and humanity takes its place in governing;

sentences.zh: 神行其化，為政資之以和。

translations.literal: the spirits carry out transformation, and governing relies on this for harmony.
translations.idiomatic: the spirits carry out transformation, and good government relies on this for harmony.

sentences.zh: 得其理則陰陽以調，失其和則災沴斯作。

translations.literal: Obtain its principle and yin and yang are regulated; lose its harmony and calamities and harms arise.
translations.idiomatic: When its principle is attained, yin and yang are regulated; when its harmony is lost, calamities and harms arise.

sentences.zh: 故舉才而授，帝唯其難，論道於邦，官不必備。

translations.literal: Therefore in raising talent and conferring office, the emperor finds it difficult; in discussing the Way for the state, offices need not all be filled.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore in raising talent and conferring office, the emperor finds it difficult; in discussing the Way for the state, not every office need be filled.

sentences.zh: 頃自中夏，及乎首秋，郡國水災，屢為人害。

translations.literal: Recently from midsummer until early autumn, commanderies and kingdoms have suffered flood disasters, repeatedly harming the people.
translations.idiomatic: Recently, from midsummer until early autumn, commanderies and kingdoms have suffered flood disasters that have repeatedly harmed the people.

sentences.zh: 夫水，陰氣也，臣實主之。

translations.literal: Water is yin qi, and ministers truly preside over it.
translations.idiomatic: Water is yin qi, and ministers truly preside over it.

sentences.zh: 臣忝職右樞，致此陰沴，不能調理其氣，而乃曠居其官。

translations.literal: Your servant disgraces the office of the right pivot, having brought about this yin harm, unable to regulate its qi, yet idly occupying the post.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant disgraces the office of the right pivot by having brought about this yin harm, unable to regulate its qi, yet idly occupying the post.

sentences.zh: 雖運屬堯年，則無治水之用；

translations.literal: Although the age belongs to the era of Yao, I have no use in controlling waters;
translations.idiomatic: Although the age is one that belongs to the era of Yao, I have no ability to control the waters;

sentences.zh: 位侔殷相，且闕濟川之功。

translations.literal: my rank equals an Yin minister, yet I lack the achievement of crossing the river.
translations.idiomatic: my rank equals that of a Yin minister, yet I lack the achievement of crossing the river.

sentences.zh: 猶負明刑，坐逃皇譴。

translations.literal: I still bear clear punishment, sitting in escape from the imperial reproof.
translations.idiomatic: I still deserve clear punishment for sitting here in escape from the imperial reproof.

sentences.zh: 皇恩不棄，其若天何？

translations.literal: Imperial grace does not abandon me—what am I to do about Heaven?
translations.idiomatic: Imperial grace has not abandoned me—what am I to do before Heaven?

sentences.zh: 昔漢家故事，丞相以天災免職。

translations.literal: In former Han precedent, the chief minister was removed from office because of heavenly calamity.
translations.idiomatic: By former Han precedent, the chief minister was removed from office because of heavenly calamity.

sentences.zh: 臣竊遇聖時，豈敢塤顏居位。

translations.literal: Your servant has encountered a sage age—how dare I thick-facedly hold office?
translations.idiomatic: Your servant has encountered a sage age—how dare I shamelessly hold office?

sentences.zh: 乞解所任，待罪私門，冀移陰咎之征，復免夜行之眚。

translations.literal: I beg to be released from my post and await punishment in my private home, hoping to shift the signs of yin blame and again escape the calamity of walking at night.
translations.idiomatic: I beg to be released from my post and await punishment at home, hoping to shift the signs of yin blame and again escape calamity.

sentences.zh: 三月壬子，洛陽東十里有水影，月餘乃滅。

translations.literal: On renzi day in the third month, ten li east of Luoyang there was a water reflection; after more than a month it vanished.
translations.idiomatic: On a renzi day in the third month, ten li east of Luoyang a watery reflection appeared; after more than a month it vanished.

sentences.zh: 四月，洛水氾濫，壞天津橋，漂流居人廬舍，溺死者數千人。

translations.literal: In the fourth month the Luo River overflowed, destroying the Tianjin Bridge, sweeping away residents' dwellings, and drowning several thousand.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month the Luo River overflowed, destroying the Tianjin Bridge, sweeping away residents' dwellings, and drowning several thousand people.

sentences.zh: 三年夏，山東、河北二十餘州大旱，饑饉死者二千餘人。

translations.literal: In the summer of the third year, more than twenty prefectures in Shandong and Hebei suffered great drought; more than two thousand died of famine.
translations.idiomatic: In the summer of the third year, more than twenty prefectures in Shandong and Hebei suffered great drought, and more than two thousand people died of famine.

sentences.zh: 正月，滄州雨雹，大如雞卵。

translations.literal: In the first month Cang Prefecture had rain and hail as large as chicken eggs.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month Cang Prefecture had rain and hail as large as chicken eggs.

sentences.zh: 六月十四日，鞏縣暴雨連日，山水泛漲，壞郭邑廬舍七百餘家，人死者七十二；

translations.literal: On the fourteenth day of the sixth month, Gong County had violent rain for successive days; mountains and rivers rose and overflowed, destroying more than seven hundred dwellings in the walled city, with seventy-two dead;
translations.idiomatic: On the fourteenth day of the sixth month, Gong County suffered violent rain for successive days. Mountains and rivers rose and overflowed, destroying more than seven hundred dwellings in the walled city and killing seventy-two people;

sentences.zh: 汜水同日漂壞近河百姓二百餘戶。

translations.literal: on the same day Sishui swept away and destroyed more than two hundred households of common people near the river.
translations.idiomatic: on the same day Sishui swept away and destroyed more than two hundred households of common people near the river.

sentences.zh: 八年夏，契丹寇營州，發關中卒援之。

translations.literal: In the summer of the eighth year, the Khitan raided Ying Prefecture, and troops from Guanzhong were dispatched to reinforce them.
translations.idiomatic: In the summer of the eighth year, the Khitan raided Ying Prefecture, and Guanzhong troops were sent to reinforce the garrison.

sentences.zh: 軍次澠池縣之闕門，野營谷水上。

translations.literal: The army halted at Que Gate in Mianchi County and camped in the wild on the Gushui River.
translations.idiomatic: The army halted at Que Gate in Mianchi County and encamped in the open country beside the Gushui River.

sentences.zh: 夜半，山水暴至，二萬餘人皆溺死，唯行網役夫樗蒲，覺水至，獲免逆旅之家，溺死死人漂入苑中如積。

translations.literal: At midnight mountain and river waters suddenly arrived; more than twenty thousand all drowned. Only a conscript laborer on net duty playing chupu noticed the water coming, escaped to an inn, and was spared; the drowned dead drifted into the imperial park piled like heaps.
translations.idiomatic: At midnight a mountain flood suddenly struck, and more than twenty thousand men drowned. Only a conscript hauling nets, gambling at chupu, noticed the water and fled to an inn in time to survive. The dead drifted into the imperial park in heaps.

sentences.zh: 其年六月二十一日夜，暴雨，東都穀、洛溢，入西上陽宮，宮人死者十七八。

translations.literal: That year on the night of the twenty-first day of the sixth month, violent rain caused the Yi and Luo rivers to overflow at the Eastern Capital and enter the Western Shangyang Palace; seven or eight out of ten palace women died.
translations.idiomatic: That year, on the night of the twenty-first day of the sixth month, a violent storm made the Yi and Luo rivers overflow at the Eastern Capital and pour into the Western Shangyang Palace. Seven or eight out of every ten palace women perished.

sentences.zh: 畿內諸縣，田稼廬舍蕩盡。

translations.literal: In all counties within the capital region, fields and dwellings were utterly swept away.
translations.idiomatic: Throughout the counties of the capital region, crops and dwellings were completely washed away.

sentences.zh: 掌關兵士，凡溺死者一千一百四十八人。

translations.literal: Among frontier-garrison soldiers, those who drowned totaled one thousand one hundred forty-eight persons.
translations.idiomatic: Among the frontier-garrison troops, a total of 1,148 men drowned.

sentences.zh: 京城興道坊一夜陷為池，一坊五百餘家俱失。

translations.literal: In the capital's Xingdao Ward, in one night it sank into a pool; more than five hundred households of the whole ward were all lost.
translations.idiomatic: In the capital, Xingdao Ward sank into a pool overnight, and more than five hundred households in the entire ward were lost.

sentences.zh: 其年，鄧州三鴉口大水塞穀，初見二小兒以水相潑，須臾，有大蛇十圍已上，張口向天，人或斫射之，俄而暴雷雨，漂溺數百家。

translations.literal: That year at Sanyakou in Deng Prefecture, a great flood blocked the valley. At first two small boys were seen splashing water at each other; in a moment a great serpent more than ten arm-spans thick appeared, mouth open toward the sky. People chopped and shot at it; shortly a violent thunderstorm came, and hundreds of households were swept away and drowned.
translations.idiomatic: That year at Sanyakou in Deng Prefecture, a great flood dammed the valley. At first two small boys were seen splashing water at each other; then a serpent more than ten arm-spans thick appeared with its mouth open to the sky. People hacked and shot at it, and shortly a violent thunderstorm swept away and drowned hundreds of households.

sentences.zh: 十年二月四日，伊水泛漲，毀都城南龍門天竺、奉先寺，壞羅郭東南角，平地水深六尺已上，入漕河，水次屋舍，樹木蕩盡。

translations.literal: On the fourth day of the second month of the tenth year, the Yi River rose and flooded, destroying the Longmen Tianzhu and Fengxian temples south of the capital city, damaging the southeast corner of the outer wall; water on flat ground was more than six feet deep, entered the canal river, and waterside houses and trees were all swept away.
translations.idiomatic: On the fourth day of the second month of the tenth year, the Yi River overflowed, destroying the Tianzhu and Fengxian temples at Longmen south of the capital and breaching the southeast corner of the outer wall. Water on level ground stood more than six feet deep, poured into the canal, and swept away every house and tree along the banks.

sentences.zh: 河南汝、許、仙、豫、唐、鄧等州，各言大水害秋稼，漂沒居人廬舍。

translations.literal: In Henan, the prefectures of Ru, Xu, Xian, Yu, Tang, Deng, and others each reported great floods harming autumn crops and sweeping away residents' dwellings.
translations.idiomatic: In Henan, Ru, Xu, Xian, Yu, Tang, Deng, and other prefectures each reported great floods that ruined the autumn harvest and swept away people's homes.

sentences.zh: 十四年六月戊午，大風拔木髮屋，端門鴟吻盡落，都城內及寺觀落者約半。

translations.literal: On the wuwu day in the sixth month of the fourteenth year, a great wind uprooted trees and tore off roofs; all ridge ornaments at the Duan Gate fell; within the capital city and at temples and monasteries about half fell.
translations.idiomatic: On a wuwu day in the sixth month of the fourteenth year, a great wind uprooted trees and stripped roofs. Every ridge ornament on the Duan Gate fell, and roughly half of those in the capital and at temples and monasteries were knocked down.

sentences.zh: 七月十四日，瀍水暴漲，流入洛漕，漂沒諸州租船數百艘，溺死者甚眾，漂失楊、壽、光、和、廬、杭、瀛、棣租米一十七萬二千八百九十六石，並錢絹雜物等。

translations.literal: On the fourteenth day of the seventh month, the Chan River suddenly rose, flowing into the Luo canal; it swept away several hundred tax-grain boats from various prefectures; very many drowned; lost were 172,896 shi of tax rice from Yang, Shou, Guang, He, Lu, Hang, Ying, and Di prefectures, along with cash, silk, and miscellaneous goods.
translations.idiomatic: On the fourteenth day of the seventh month the Chan River surged and poured into the Luo canal, sinking several hundred tax-grain boats from many prefectures and drowning a great many people.
