Lost were 172,896 shi of tax rice from Yang, Shou, Guang, He, Lu, Hang, Ying, and Di prefectures, along with cash, silk, and other goods.

sentences.zh: 因開斗門決堰，引水南入洛，漕水燥竭，以搜漉官物，十收四五焉。

translations.literal: Thereupon sluice gates were opened and dikes breached to channel water south into the Luo; when the canal water ran dry, officials searched and salvaged government goods, recovering four or five out of ten.
translations.idiomatic: Sluice gates were then opened and dikes cut to divert water south into the Luo. Once the canal ran dry, officials searched the bed and recovered only four or five tenths of the lost government goods.

sentences.zh: 七月甲子，懷、衛、鄭、滑、汴、濮、許等州澍雨，河及支川皆溢，人皆巢舟以居，死者千計，資產苗稼無孑遺。

translations.literal: On the jiazi day in the seventh month, at Huai, Wei, Zheng, Hua, Bian, Pu, Xu, and other prefectures there was soaking rain; the Yellow River and all tributary streams overflowed; people all lived in boats like nests; dead numbered in the thousands; property, seedlings, and crops left not a survivor.
translations.idiomatic: On a jiazi day in the seventh month, Huai, Wei, Zheng, Hua, Bian, Pu, Xu, and other prefectures were deluged with soaking rain. The Yellow River and its tributaries all overflowed, and people took to living in boats. Thousands died, and property, seedlings, and crops were wiped out entirely.

sentences.zh: 滄州大風，海運船沒者十一二，失平盧軍糧五千餘石，舟人皆死。

translations.literal: At Cang Prefecture a great wind struck; eleven or twelve out of twelve sea-transport ships were lost; lost were more than five thousand shi of Pinglu Army grain; all sailors died.
translations.idiomatic: At Cang Prefecture a great wind struck, sinking eleven or twelve of the sea-transport ships and with them more than five thousand shi of Pinglu Army grain. Every sailor perished.

sentences.zh: 潤州大風從東北，海濤奔上，沒瓜步洲，損居人。

translations.literal: At Run Prefecture a great wind came from the northeast; sea surge rushed up and submerged Guabu islet, harming residents.
translations.idiomatic: At Run Prefecture a great wind blew from the northeast, driving the sea surge inland and submerging Guabu islet, with harm to the local population.

sentences.zh: 是秋，天下八十五州言旱及霜，五十州水，河南、河北尤甚。

translations.literal: That autumn, eighty-five prefectures throughout the empire reported drought and frost; fifty reported floods; Henan and Hebei were especially severe.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn, eighty-five prefectures across the empire reported drought and frost, and fifty reported floods. Henan and Hebei suffered especially badly.

sentences.zh: 十五年七月甲寅，雷震興教門樓兩鴟吻，燒樓柱，良久乃滅。

translations.literal: On the jiayin day in the seventh month of the fifteenth year, thunder struck the two ridge ornaments of the Xingjiao Gate tower, burning the tower pillars; after a long time it extinguished.
translations.idiomatic: On a jiayin day in the seventh month of the fifteenth year, thunder struck both ridge ornaments on the Xingjiao Gate tower and set its pillars ablaze. The fire burned for a long time before it went out.

sentences.zh: 二十日，鄜州雨，洛水溢入州城，平地丈餘，損居人廬舍，溺死者不知其數。

translations.literal: On the twentieth day, at Fu Prefecture rain fell, the Luo River overflowed into the prefecture city, more than ten feet on flat ground, damaging residents' dwellings; drowned dead were beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: On the twentieth day, rain fell at Fu Prefecture and the Luo River overflowed into the city, standing more than ten feet deep on level ground. People's dwellings were damaged and the drowned were beyond counting.

sentences.zh: 二十一日，同州損郭邑及市，毀馮翊縣。

translations.literal: On the twenty-first day, at Tong Prefecture the walled city and markets were damaged and Fengyi County was destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: On the twenty-first day, Tong Prefecture's walled city and markets were damaged and Fengyi County was destroyed.

sentences.zh: 八月八日，澠池縣夜有暴雨，澗水、谷水漲合，毀郭邑百餘家及普門佛寺。

translations.literal: On the eighth day of the eighth month, at Mianchi County there was violent rain at night; stream and valley waters rose and combined, destroying more than one hundred households in the walled city and the Pumen Buddhist temple.
translations.idiomatic: On the eighth day of the eighth month, Mianchi County was hit by a violent night storm. Stream and valley waters rose together and destroyed more than one hundred households in the walled city and the Pumen Buddhist temple.

sentences.zh: 是歲，天下六十三州大水損禾稼、居人廬舍，河北尤甚。

translations.literal: That year, sixty-three prefectures throughout the empire suffered great floods damaging grain crops and residents' dwellings; Hebei was especially severe.
translations.idiomatic: That year, sixty-three prefectures across the empire suffered great floods that ruined crops and people's homes. Hebei was hit hardest.

sentences.zh: 十八年六月乙丑，東都瀍水暴漲，漂損揚、楚、淄、德等州租船。

translations.literal: On the yichou day in the sixth month of the eighteenth year, the Chan River at the Eastern Capital suddenly rose, sweeping and damaging tax-grain boats from Yang, Chu, Zi, and De prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: On a yichou day in the sixth month of the eighteenth year, the Chan River at the Eastern Capital surged and damaged tax-grain boats from Yang, Chu, Zi, and De prefectures.

sentences.zh: 壬午，東都洛水泛漲，壞天津、永濟二橋及漕渠斗門，漂損提象門外助鋪及仗舍，又損居人廬舍千餘家。

translations.literal: On the renwu day, the Luo River at the Eastern Capital overflowed, destroying the Tianjin and Yongji bridges and sluice gates of the canal channel; it swept and damaged supply depots and armory quarters outside the Tixiang Gate, and also damaged more than a thousand dwellings of common people.
translations.idiomatic: On a renwu day the Luo River at the Eastern Capital overflowed, destroying the Tianjin and Yongji bridges and the canal sluice gates. It also damaged supply depots and armory quarters outside the Tixiang Gate and more than a thousand private dwellings.

sentences.zh: 二十七年八月，東京改作明堂，訛言官取小兒埋於明堂下，以為厭勝。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the twenty-seventh year, the Eastern Capital was being rebuilt as the Bright Hall; a rumor spread that officials were taking small children to bury beneath the Bright Hall as apotropaic magic.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of the twenty-seventh year, the Eastern Capital was rebuilding the Bright Hall. A rumor spread that officials were burying small children beneath it as apotropaic magic.

sentences.zh: 村邑童兒藏於山谷，都城騷然，或言兵至。

translations.literal: Village children hid in mountain valleys; the capital was in uproar, some saying troops had arrived.
translations.idiomatic: Village children hid in the hills, the capital fell into uproar, and some said troops were coming.

sentences.zh: 玄宗惡之，遣主客郎中王佶往東都及諸州宣慰百姓，久之乃定。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuanzong deplored it and dispatched Supervising Secretary of the Hosts Bureau Wang Ji to the Eastern Capital and various prefectures to announce reassurances and comfort the common people; after a long time it subsided.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuanzong deplored the panic and sent Supervising Secretary of the Hosts Bureau Wang Ji to the Eastern Capital and other prefectures to reassure the people. Only after a long while did order return.

sentences.zh: 二十九年，暴水，伊、洛及支川皆溢，損居人廬舍，秋稼無遺，壞東都天津橋及東西漕；

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year, violent floods caused the Yi, Luo, and tributary streams all to overflow, damaging residents' dwellings, leaving no autumn crops, destroying the Tianjin Bridge and east-west canals at the Eastern Capital;
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-ninth year violent floods made the Yi, Luo, and their tributaries overflow, destroying people's homes and wiping out the autumn harvest. The Tianjin Bridge and the east-west canals at the Eastern Capital were ruined;

sentences.zh: 河南北諸州，皆多漂溺。

translations.literal: north and south of Henan, all had many swept away and drowned.
translations.idiomatic: and north and south of Henan many people were swept away and drowned.

sentences.zh: ，廣陵郡大風架海潮，淪江口大小船數千艘。

translations.literal: at Guangling Prefecture a great wind raised a sea tide and submerged several thousand large and small ships at the river mouth.
translations.idiomatic: At Guangling Prefecture a great wind raised a sea tide and sank several thousand large and small ships at the river mouth.

sentences.zh: 十三載秋，京城連月澍雨，損秋稼。

translations.literal: In the autumn of the thirteenth year, the capital had continuous rain for successive months, damaging autumn crops.
translations.idiomatic: In the autumn of the thirteenth year, the capital was drenched by soaking rain for months on end, ruining the autumn harvest.

sentences.zh: 九月，遣閉坊市北門，蓋井，禁婦人入街市，祭玄冥大社，禜門。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, orders were sent to close the northern gates of wards and markets, cover wells, forbid women from entering the streets and markets, sacrifice to the Great Earth of the Dark Thearch, and perform gate exorcism rituals.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, orders went out to close the northern gates of wards and markets, cover wells, forbid women from entering the streets, sacrifice to the Great Earth of the Dark Thearch, and perform gate exorcism rituals.

sentences.zh: 京城坊市牆宇，崩壞向盡。

translations.literal: Walls and buildings of wards and markets in the capital were nearly all collapsed and ruined.
translations.idiomatic: The walls and buildings of the capital's wards and markets were nearly all collapsed.

sentences.zh: 東方瀍、洛水溢堤穴，沖壞一十九坊。

translations.literal: East of the city the Chan and Luo rivers overflowed dikes and breached holes, destroying nineteen wards.
translations.idiomatic: East of the city the Chan and Luo rivers broke their dikes and breached the embankments, destroying nineteen wards.

sentences.zh: ，京師自七月霖雨，八月盡方止。

translations.literal: in the capital, from the seventh month there was continuous rain; it did not stop until the end of the eighth month.
translations.idiomatic: In the capital, soaking rain began in the seventh month and did not stop until the end of the eighth.

sentences.zh: 京城宮寺廬舍多壞，街市溝渠中漉得小魚。

translations.literal: Many palace temples and dwellings in the capital were ruined; small fish were scooped from streets and ditches.
translations.idiomatic: Many palace temples and dwellings in the capital were ruined, and people scooped small fish from the streets and ditches.

sentences.zh: ，先旱後水。

translations.literal: first drought, then flood.
translations.idiomatic: First came drought, then flood.

sentences.zh: 九月，大雨，平地水數尺，溝河漲溢。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, heavy rain—water on flat ground several feet deep, ditches and rivers swelling and overflowing.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month heavy rain left several feet of water on level ground and made ditches and rivers overflow.

sentences.zh: 時吐蕃寇京畿，以水，自潰而去。

translations.literal: At that time the Tibetans raided the capital region; because of the water, they dispersed and withdrew on their own.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the Tibetans were raiding the capital region, but the floods broke up their forces and they withdrew on their own.

sentences.zh: 二年夏，洛陽大雨，水壞二十餘坊及寺觀廨舍。

translations.literal: In the summer of the second year, Luoyang had heavy rain; water destroyed more than twenty wards and temple and government buildings.
translations.idiomatic: In the summer of the second year, heavy rain in Luoyang destroyed more than twenty wards along with temples, monasteries, and government offices.

sentences.zh: 河南數十州大水。

translations.literal: Dozens of prefectures in Henan had great floods.
translations.idiomatic: Dozens of prefectures in Henan suffered great floods.

sentences.zh: 秋，大雨。

translations.literal: In autumn, heavy rain.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn there was heavy rain.

sentences.zh: 是歲，自四月霖澍，至九月。

translations.literal: That year, from the fourth month of continuous soaking rain until the ninth month.
translations.idiomatic: That year soaking rain continued from the fourth month through the ninth.

sentences.zh: 京師米鬥八百文，官出太倉米賤糶以救饑人。

translations.literal: Rice in the capital was eight hundred cash per dou; the government released granary rice to sell cheaply to save the starving.
translations.idiomatic: Rice in the capital reached eight hundred cash per dou, and the government released grain from the imperial granary to sell cheaply and relieve the starving.

sentences.zh: 京城閉坊市北門，門置土臺，臺上置壇及黃幡以祈晴。

translations.literal: The capital closed the northern gates of wards and markets; at each gate an earthen platform was set up, with an altar and yellow banners upon it to pray for clear weather.
translations.idiomatic: The capital closed the northern gates of its wards and markets, erected earthen platforms at each gate, and set up altars and yellow banners on them to pray for clear skies.

sentences.zh: 秋末方止。

translations.literal: It stopped only at the end of autumn.
translations.idiomatic: The rain did not stop until late autumn.

sentences.zh: 五年夏，復大雨，京城饑，出太倉米減價以救人。

translations.literal: In the summer of the fifth year, heavy rain came again; the capital suffered famine; granary rice was released at reduced price to save people.
translations.idiomatic: In the summer of the fifth year heavy rain returned, famine struck the capital, and the government released imperial granary rice at reduced prices to save the people.

sentences.zh: 十二年秋，大雨。

translations.literal: In the autumn of the twelfth year, heavy rain.
translations.idiomatic: In the autumn of the twelfth year there was heavy rain.

sentences.zh: 是歲，春夏旱，至秋八月雨，河南尤甚，平地深五尺，河決，漂溺田稼。

translations.literal: That year, spring and summer drought until the eighth month in autumn when rain came; Henan was especially severe—flat ground five feet deep, the river broke its banks, crops swept away and drowned.
translations.idiomatic: That year spring and summer brought drought, then rain in the eighth month of autumn. Henan was worst hit: water on level ground stood five feet deep, the river broke its banks, and crops were swept away.

sentences.zh: 夏，京師通衢水深數尺。

translations.literal: In summer, water in the capital's main thoroughfares was several feet deep.
translations.idiomatic: In summer the main thoroughfares of the capital stood several feet deep in water.

sentences.zh: 吏部侍郎崔縱，自崇義里西門為水漂浮行數十步，街鋪卒救之獲免；

translations.literal: Vice Minister of the Ministry of Personnel Cui Zong, from the western gate of Chongyi Ward, was floated along by the water for several tens of steps; market patrol soldiers rescued him and he escaped;
translations.idiomatic: Vice Minister of the Ministry of Personnel Cui Zong was carried by the flood from the western gate of Chongyi Ward for several tens of steps before market patrol soldiers pulled him out and saved him;

sentences.zh: 其日，溺死者甚眾。

translations.literal: That day, very many drowned.
translations.idiomatic: That day a great many people drowned.

sentences.zh: 東都、河南、荊南、淮南江河泛溢，壞人廬舍。

translations.literal: The Eastern Capital, Henan, Jingnan, and Huainan—rivers and streams overflowed, destroying people's dwellings.
translations.idiomatic: At the Eastern Capital and in Henan, Jingnan, and Huainan, rivers and streams overflowed and destroyed people's homes.

sentences.zh: 四年八月，連雨，灞水暴溢，溺殺渡者百餘人。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the fourth year, continuous rain; the Ba River suddenly overflowed, drowning more than a hundred ferry passengers.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of the fourth year continuous rain made the Ba River surge and drown more than a hundred people crossing by ferry.

sentences.zh: 八年秋，大雨，河南、河北、山南、江淮凡四十餘州大水，漂溺死者二萬餘人。

translations.literal: In the autumn of the eighth year, heavy rain; more than forty prefectures in Henan, Hebei, Shannan, and Jianghuai had great floods; more than twenty thousand swept away and drowned.
translations.idiomatic: In the autumn of the eighth year heavy rain brought great floods to more than forty prefectures in Henan, Hebei, Shannan, and Jianghuai, and more than twenty thousand people were swept away and drowned.

sentences.zh: 時幽州七月大雨，平地水深二丈；

translations.literal: At that time You Prefecture in the seventh month had heavy rain; water on flat ground was two zhang deep;
translations.idiomatic: At that time You Prefecture had heavy rain in the seventh month, and water on level ground stood two zhang deep;

sentences.zh: 鄚、涿、薊、檀、平五州，平地水深一丈五尺。

translations.literal: at the five prefectures of Mo, Zhuo, Ji, Tan, and Ping, water on flat ground was one zhang five chi deep.
translations.idiomatic: at Mo, Zhuo, Ji, Tan, and Ping prefectures water on level ground stood one zhang and five chi deep.

sentences.zh: 又徐州奏：自五月二十五日雨，至七月八日方止，平地水深一丈二尺，郭邑廬里屋宇田稼皆盡，百姓皆登丘塚山原以避之。

translations.literal: Moreover Xuz Prefecture reported: from the twenty-fifth day of the fifth month rain until the eighth day of the seventh month it stopped; water on flat ground one zhang two chi deep; walled cities, lanes, dwellings, and crops were all gone; common people all climbed hills and mounds and highlands to escape.
translations.idiomatic: Xuz Prefecture also reported that rain from the twenty-fifth day of the fifth month until the eighth day of the seventh month left level ground one zhang and two chi deep, wiped out cities, lanes, homes, and crops, and drove the people to flee to hills and high ground.

sentences.zh: 正月，振武界黃河溢，毀東受降城。

translations.literal: In the first month, the Yellow River overflowed at the border of Zhenwu, destroying the Eastern Accepting-Surrender City.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month the Yellow River overflowed on the Zhenwu frontier and destroyed the Eastern Accepting-Surrender City.

sentences.zh: 五月，饒、撫、虔、吉、信五州山水暴漲，壞廬舍，虔州尤甚，水深處四丈餘。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, at the five prefectures of Rao, Fu, Qian, Ji, and Xin, mountain and river waters suddenly rose, destroying dwellings; Qian Prefecture was especially severe—at deepest places more than four zhang.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month mountain and river waters surged in Rao, Fu, Qian, Ji, and Xin prefectures and destroyed dwellings. Qian Prefecture was worst hit, with depths of more than four zhang in places.

sentences.zh: 八年五月，許州奏：大雨摧大隗山，水流出，溺死者千餘人。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the eighth year, Xu Prefecture reported: heavy rain demolished Mount Dawei; water burst out and more than a thousand drowned.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the eighth year Xu Prefecture reported that heavy rain had demolished Mount Dawei, unleashing a flood that drowned more than a thousand people.

sentences.zh: 六月庚寅，京師大風雨，毀屋揚瓦，人多壓死。

translations.literal: On the gengyin day in the sixth month, the capital had great wind and rain; houses were destroyed and tiles flew; many were crushed to death.
translations.idiomatic: On a gengyin day in the sixth month a great storm struck the capital, tearing off roofs and hurling tiles. Many people were crushed to death.

sentences.zh: 水積城南，深處丈餘，入明德門，猶漸車輻。

translations.literal: Water pooled south of the city; at deepest places more than a zhang; it entered the Mingde Gate, still reaching to the wheel hubs.
translations.idiomatic: Water pooled south of the city to depths of more than a zhang, flooded in through the Mingde Gate, and still reached to the wheel hubs.

sentences.zh: 辛卯，渭水暴漲，毀三渭橋，南北絕濟者一月。

translations.literal: On the xinmao day, the Wei River suddenly rose, destroying the three Wei bridges; north and south had no crossing for a month.
translations.idiomatic: On a xinmao day the Wei River surged and destroyed all three Wei bridges, cutting off north-south travel for a month.

sentences.zh: 時所在霖雨，百源皆發，川瀆不由故道。

translations.literal: At that time everywhere had continuous rain; a hundred streams all burst forth; rivers and canals did not follow their old courses.
translations.idiomatic: Everywhere there was continuous rain, a hundred streams burst forth at once, and rivers and canals abandoned their old channels.

sentences.zh: 丙申，富平大風，折樹一千二百株。

translations.literal: On the bingshen day, at Fuping a great wind snapped 1,200 trees.
translations.idiomatic: On a bingshen day a great wind at Fuping snapped 1,200 trees.

sentences.zh: 辛丑，出宮人二百車，人得娶納，以水害誡陰盈也。

translations.literal: On the xinchou day, two hundred cartloads of palace women were released; people were allowed to marry them, as admonition against yin excess due to water calamity.
translations.idiomatic: On a xinchou day two hundred cartloads of palace women were released for commoners to marry, as a warning against yin excess in the wake of the flood disaster.

sentences.zh: 九年秋，淮南、宣州大水。

translations.literal: In the autumn of the ninth year, Huainan and Xuan Prefecture had great floods.
translations.idiomatic: In the autumn of the ninth year Huainan and Xuan Prefecture suffered great floods.

sentences.zh: 十一年五月，京畿大雨，害田四萬頃，昭應尤甚，漂溺居人。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the eleventh year, the capital region had heavy rain, harming forty thousand qing of fields; Zhao Prefecture was especially severe; residents swept away and drowned.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the eleventh year heavy rain in the capital region ruined forty thousand qing of fields. Zhao Prefecture was worst hit, and many residents were swept away and drowned.

sentences.zh: 衢州山水湧，深三丈，壞州城，民多溺死。

translations.literal: At Qu Prefecture mountain and river waters surged, three zhang deep, destroying the prefecture city; many common people drowned.
translations.idiomatic: At Qu Prefecture mountain and river waters surged three zhang deep, destroyed the prefecture city, and drowned many of the people.

sentences.zh: 浮梁、樂平溺死者一百七十人，為水漂流不知所在者四千七百戶。

translations.literal: At Fuliang and Leping 170 drowned; swept away by water with whereabouts unknown, 4,700 households.
translations.idiomatic: At Fuliang and Leping 170 people drowned, and 4,700 households were swept away by the water with no trace of where they went.

sentences.zh: 潤、常、湖、陳、許等州各損田萬頃。

translations.literal: The prefectures of Run, Chang, Hu, Chen, and Xu each lost ten thousand qing of fields.
translations.idiomatic: Run, Chang, Hu, Chen, Xu, and other prefectures each lost ten thousand qing of fields.

sentences.zh: 十二年秋，大雨，河南北水，害稼。

translations.literal: In the autumn of the twelfth year, heavy rain; floods north and south of Henan damaged crops.
translations.idiomatic: In the autumn of the twelfth year heavy rain brought floods north and south of Henan and ruined the harvest.

sentences.zh: 其年六月，京師大雨，街市水深三尺，壞廬舍二千家，含元殿一柱陷。

translations.literal: That year in the sixth month, the capital had heavy rain; street water three chi deep; two thousand dwellings destroyed; one pillar of the Hanyuan Hall sank.
translations.idiomatic: That year in the sixth month heavy rain in the capital left streets three chi deep in water, destroyed two thousand dwellings, and sank one pillar of the Hanyuan Hall.

sentences.zh: 十五年九月十一日至十四日，大雨兼雪，街衢禁苑樹無風而摧折、連根而拔者不知其數。

translations.literal: From the eleventh to the fourteenth day of the ninth month of the fifteenth year, heavy rain mixed with snow; trees in streets and the forbidden park without wind were snapped and uprooted beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: From the eleventh to the fourteenth day of the ninth month of the fifteenth year, rain mixed with snow snapped and uprooted countless trees in the streets and the forbidden park, though there was no wind.

sentences.zh: 仍令閉坊市北門以禳之。

translations.literal: Orders were also issued to close the northern gates of wards and markets to perform rituals against it.
translations.idiomatic: Orders were also issued to close the northern gates of wards and markets and perform rituals to avert the calamity.

sentences.zh: 滄州大水。

translations.literal: Cang Prefecture had great flood.
translations.idiomatic: Cang Prefecture suffered a great flood.

sentences.zh: 十月，好畤山水泛漲，漂損居人三百餘家，河南陳、許二州尤甚。

translations.literal: In the tenth month, at Haozhi mountain and river waters rose and overflowed, sweeping and damaging more than three hundred households; Henan Chen and Xu prefectures were especially severe.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month floods at Haozhi swept away more than three hundred households. Chen and Xu prefectures in Henan were hit especially hard.

sentences.zh: 詔賑貸粟五萬石，量人戶家口多少，等第分給。

translations.literal: An edict granted relief grain of fifty thousand shi, apportioned by rank according to each household's population.
translations.idiomatic: An edict granted fifty thousand shi of relief grain, to be distributed by rank according to each household's size.

sentences.zh: 四月，同官暴水，漂沒三百餘家。

translations.literal: In the fourth month, at Tongguan violent flood swept away more than three hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month a sudden flood at Tongguan swept away more than three hundred households.

sentences.zh: 六年，徐州自六月九日大雨至十一日，壞民舍九百家。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, at Xuz Prefecture from the ninth day of the sixth month heavy rain until the eleventh, nine hundred common dwellings were destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year heavy rain at Xuz Prefecture from the ninth to the eleventh day of the sixth month destroyed nine hundred private dwellings.

sentences.zh: 四年夏，鄆、曹、濮雨，壞城郭田廬向盡。

translations.literal: In the summer of the fourth year, at Yan, Cao, and Pu prefectures rain fell, nearly destroying all walled cities, fields, and dwellings.
translations.idiomatic: In the summer of the fourth year rain in Yan, Cao, and Pu prefectures nearly wiped out every walled city, field, and dwelling.

sentences.zh: 蘇、湖二州水，壞六堤，水入郡郭，溺廬井。

translations.literal: Su and Hu prefectures had floods, destroying six dikes; water entered the commandery cities and drowned lanes and wells.
translations.idiomatic: Floods in Su and Hu prefectures destroyed six dikes, poured into the commandery cities, and submerged lanes and wells.

sentences.zh: 許州自五月大雨，水深八尺，壞郡郭居民大半。

translations.literal: At Xu Prefecture from the fifth month heavy rain, water eight chi deep, destroyed more than half the commandery city's residents.
translations.idiomatic: At Xu Prefecture heavy rain from the fifth month left water eight chi deep and destroyed more than half the dwellings in the commandery city.

sentences.zh: 七月，襄州漢水暴溢，壞州郭。

translations.literal: In the seventh month, the Han River at Xiang Prefecture suddenly overflowed, destroying the prefecture walls.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month the Han River at Xiang Prefecture surged and destroyed the prefecture walls.

sentences.zh: 均州亦然。

translations.literal: Jun Prefecture was likewise.
translations.idiomatic: The same happened at Jun Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 則天時，宗秦客以佞幸為內史，受命之日，無雲而雷聲震烈，未周歲而誅。

translations.literal: In Empress Wu's time, Zong Qinke through flattery became chief minister; on the day he received appointment, without clouds thunder sounded violently; before a year had passed he was executed.
translations.idiomatic: During Empress Wu's reign, Zong Qinke rose through flattery to chief minister. On the day he took office thunder crashed though there were no clouds, and before a year had passed he was executed.

sentences.zh: 六月，河南偃師縣之李材村，有霹靂閃入人家，地震裂，闊丈餘，長十五里，測之無底。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, at Licun township in Yanshi County, Henan, lightning flashed into a household; the earth quaked and split—a gap more than a zhang wide and fifteen li long, sounding it had no bottom.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month at Licun in Yanshi County, Henan, lightning struck a house and the earth split open a chasm more than a zhang wide and fifteen li long. When they sounded it, there was no bottom.

sentences.zh: 所裂之處，井廁相通，所沖之塚，棺柩出植平地無損，竟不知其故。

translations.literal: Where it split, wells and privies connected; among tombs it struck, coffins came out planted on flat ground unharmed; in the end no one knew why.
translations.idiomatic: Where the earth split, wells and privies opened into one another. Among the tombs it struck, coffins were thrust out onto level ground unharmed. In the end no one knew why.

sentences.zh: 一月十四日，雨水冰。

translations.literal: On the fourteenth day of the first month, rain froze to ice.
translations.idiomatic: On the fourteenth day of the first month rain froze into ice.

sentences.zh: 七月四日，雷震興教門兩鴟吻，欄檻及柱災。

translations.literal: On the fourth day of the seventh month, thunder struck the two ridge ornaments of Xingjiao Gate; balustrades and pillars were burned.
translations.idiomatic: On the fourth day of the seventh month thunder struck both ridge ornaments on the Xingjiao Gate and set its balustrades and pillars ablaze.

sentences.zh: 二十九年十一月二十二日，雨木冰，凝寒凍冽，數日不解。

translations.literal: On the twenty-second day of the eleventh month of the twenty-ninth year, rain formed ice on trees; cold congealed and froze bitterly for several days without lifting.
translations.idiomatic: On the twenty-second day of the eleventh month of the twenty-ninth year rain coated the trees in ice. Bitter cold set in and lasted several days without lifting.

sentences.zh: 甯王見而歎曰：「諺云『樹稼達官怕』，必有大臣當之。

translations.literal: Prince Ning saw it and sighed: "The proverb says 'When frost coats the trees, high officials fear'—surely a great minister will bear it.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Ning saw it and sighed: "The proverb says, 'When frost coats the trees, high officials tremble'—surely some great minister will bear this omen.

sentences.zh: 」其月王薨。

translations.literal: " That month the Prince died.
translations.idiomatic: " That same month the Prince died.

sentences.zh: 閏四月，大霧，大雨月餘。

translations.literal: In the intercalary fourth month, great fog, heavy rain for more than a month.
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary fourth month there was heavy fog and more than a month of torrential rain.

sentences.zh: 是月，史思明再陷東都，京師米鬥八百文，人相食，殍骸蔽地。

translations.literal: That month, Shi Siming again captured the Eastern Capital; rice in the capital was eight hundred cash per dou; people ate one another; corpses covered the ground.
translations.idiomatic: That month Shi Siming again captured the Eastern Capital. Rice in the capital reached eight hundred cash per dou, people turned to cannibalism, and corpses covered the ground.

sentences.zh: 二月甲子夜，雷電震烈。

translations.literal: On the night of the jiazi day in the second month, thunder and lightning struck violently.
translations.idiomatic: On the night of a jiazi day in the second month thunder and lightning crashed violently.

sentences.zh: 三月，降霜為木冰。

translations.literal: In the third month, descending frost became ice on trees.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month descending frost coated the trees in ice.

sentences.zh: 辛亥，大風拔木。

translations.literal: On the xinhai day, a great wind uprooted trees.
translations.idiomatic: On a xinhai day a great wind uprooted trees.

sentences.zh: 三月辛亥夜，京師大風發屋。

translations.literal: On the night of the xinhai day in the third month, a great wind in the capital tore off roofs.
translations.idiomatic: On the night of a xinhai day in the third month a great wind in the capital tore roofs from houses.

sentences.zh: 十一月，紛霧如雪，草木冰。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, swirling mist was like snow, and grass and trees froze.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month swirling mist fell like snow, coating grass and trees in ice.

sentences.zh: 十年四月甲申夜，大雨雹，暴風拔樹，飄屋瓦，宮寺鴟吻飄失者十五六，人震死者十二，損京畿田稼七縣。

translations.literal: On the night of the jiashen day in the fourth month of the tenth year, heavy hail fell; a violent wind uprooted trees and sent roof tiles flying; fifteen or sixteen ridge ornaments on palace and temple buildings were blown away; twelve people were killed by the strike; crops in seven counties of the capital region were damaged.
translations.idiomatic: On the night of a jiashen day in the fourth month of the tenth year hail crashed down and a violent wind uprooted trees and hurled roof tiles through the air. Fifteen or sixteen ridge ornaments on palace and temple halls were torn away, twelve people were killed by the storm, and crops in seven capital-region counties were ruined.

sentences.zh: 七月己未夜，杭州大風，海水翻潮，飄蕩州郭五千餘家，船千餘只，全家陷溺者百餘戶，死者四百餘人；

translations.literal: On the night of the jiwei day in the seventh month, a great wind struck Hang Prefecture; the sea surged and the tide turned back, sweeping away more than five thousand households in the prefecture city, more than a thousand boats; more than a hundred households were drowned entire families; more than four hundred dead;
translations.idiomatic: On the night of a jiwei day in the seventh month a great wind struck Hang Prefecture. The sea surged and the tide rolled back, sweeping away more than five thousand households in the prefecture city and more than a thousand boats. More than a hundred entire families were drowned, and more than four hundred people died;

sentences.zh: 蘇、湖、越等州亦然。

translations.literal: Su, Hu, Yue, and other prefectures were likewise.
translations.idiomatic: The same happened in Su, Hu, Yue, and other prefectures.

sentences.zh: 正月，大雨雪，平地深尺餘。

translations.literal: In the first month, heavy rain and snow; on level ground more than a chi deep.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month heavy rain and snow left more than a chi of accumulation on level ground.

sentences.zh: 雪上有黃色，狀如浮埃。

translations.literal: On the snow there was yellow color, shaped like floating dust.
translations.idiomatic: The snow bore a yellow tinge, like dust suspended in the air.

sentences.zh: 四年正月，陳留十里許雨木，皆大如指，長寸餘，木有孔通中，所下立者如植。

translations.literal: In the first month of the fourth year, at Chenliu for about ten li wood rained down, all as large as a finger, more than a cun long, the wood having a hole through the center; where it fell it stood upright as if planted.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the fourth year wood rained down over some ten li around Chenliu. Each piece was finger-thick and more than a cun long, pierced through the center, and where it struck the ground it stood upright as though planted.

sentences.zh: 其年，宣州暴雨震電，有物墜地，豬首，手腳各有兩指，執一赤斑蛇食之。

translations.literal: That year, at Xuan Prefecture violent rain and thunder and lightning; a thing fell to earth with a pig's head, hands and feet each having two fingers; it grasped a red-spotted snake and ate it.
translations.idiomatic: That year at Xuan Prefecture a torrential storm broke with thunder and lightning, and a creature fell to earth with a pig's head and two-fingered hands and feet. It seized a red-spotted snake and devoured it.

sentences.zh: 逡巡，黑雲合，不見。

translations.literal: After a little while, black clouds gathered, and it was no longer seen.
translations.idiomatic: Before long black clouds closed in and the creature vanished from sight.

sentences.zh: 八年二月，京師雨土。

translations.literal: In the second month of the eighth year, the capital had a rain of earth.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the eighth year dust rained down on the capital.

sentences.zh: 五月己未，暴風破屋拔樹，太廟屋及諸門寺署壞者不可勝計。

translations.literal: On the jiwei day in the fifth month, a violent wind destroyed houses and uprooted trees; damage to the Grand Ancestral Temple and various gates, temples, and offices was beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: On a jiwei day in the fifth month a violent wind tore houses apart and uprooted trees. Damage to the Grand Ancestral Temple and to gates, temples, and government offices was beyond reckoning.

sentences.zh: 十年六月辛丑晦，有水鳥集于左藏庫。

translations.literal: On the last day of the sixth month, xinchou, of the tenth year, water birds gathered at the Left Treasury.
translations.idiomatic: On the last xinchou day of the sixth month of the tenth year water birds gathered at the Left Treasury.

sentences.zh: 其夜暴雨，大風拔樹十七年二月五日，大雨雹。

translations.literal: That night torrential rain fell and a great wind uprooted trees. In the seventeenth year, on the fifth day of the second month, heavy hail fell.
translations.idiomatic: That night torrential rain fell and a great wind uprooted trees. In the seventeenth year, on the fifth day of the second month, heavy hail fell again.

sentences.zh: 七日，大霜。

translations.literal: On the seventh day, heavy frost.
translations.idiomatic: On the seventh day there was heavy frost.

sentences.zh: 十六夜，大雨，震雷且電。

translations.literal: On the night of the sixteenth, heavy rain, thunder, and lightning.
translations.idiomatic: On the night of the sixteenth heavy rain fell with thunder and lightning.

sentences.zh: 十九日，大雨雪而電。

translations.literal: On the nineteenth day, heavy rain and snow with lightning.
translations.idiomatic: On the nineteenth day heavy rain and snow fell with lightning.

sentences.zh: 四月壬申，大風毀含元殿西闕欄檻二十七間。

translations.literal: On the renshen day in the fourth month, a great wind destroyed twenty-seven bays of balustrades at the western gate-tower of the Hanyuan Hall.
translations.idiomatic: On a renshen day in the fourth month a great wind destroyed twenty-seven bays of balustrades at the western gate-tower of the Hanyuan Hall.

sentences.zh: 八年三月丙子，大風拔崇陵上宮衙殿西鴟尾，並上宮西神門六戟竿折，行牆四十間醿壞。

translations.literal: On the bingzi day in the third month of the eighth year, a great wind tore off the western ridge ornament of the upper palace office hall at Chongling, and also broke the six halberd poles at the western spirit gate of the upper palace; forty bays of corridor wall eaves were destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: On a bingzi day in the third month of the eighth year a great wind tore the western ridge ornament from the upper palace office hall at Chongling, snapped the six halberd poles at the upper palace's western spirit gate, and destroyed the eaves of forty bays of corridor wall.

sentences.zh: 九月壬寅，京師震電，大風雨。

translations.literal: On the renyin day in the ninth month, the capital had thunder and lightning, and a great wind and rain.
translations.idiomatic: On a renyin day in the ninth month thunder and lightning crashed over the capital amid a great wind and rain.

sentences.zh: 四年五月庚辰，大風吹壞延喜、景風二門。

translations.literal: On the gengchen day in the fifth month of the fourth year, a great wind blew down the Yanxi and Jingfeng gates.
translations.idiomatic: On a gengchen day in the fifth month of the fourth year a great wind blew down the Yanxi and Jingfeng gates.

sentences.zh: 六月癸未，暴風雷雨壞長安縣廨及經行寺塔。

translations.literal: On the guiwei day in the sixth month, a violent wind and thunderstorm destroyed the Chang'an County office and the pagoda of Jingxing Temple.
translations.idiomatic: On a guiwei day in the sixth month a violent wind and thunderstorm destroyed the Chang'an County yamen and the pagoda of Jingxing Temple.

sentences.zh: 同、華大旱。

translations.literal: Tong and Hua had severe drought.
translations.idiomatic: Tong and Hua prefectures suffered severe drought.

sentences.zh: 七月辛酉，定陵臺大風雨，震，東廓之下地裂一百三十尺，其深五尺。

translations.literal: On the xinyou day in the seventh month, at Dingling Terrace a great wind and rain fell and the earth quaked; below the eastern corridor the ground split one hundred thirty chi, five chi deep.
translations.idiomatic: On a xinyou day in the seventh month a great wind and rain struck Dingling Terrace and the earth quaked. Below the eastern corridor the ground split open one hundred thirty chi long and five chi deep.

sentences.zh: 詔宗正卿李仍叔啟告修之。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Director of the Imperial Clan Li Rengshu to open rites of announcement and repair it.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered Director of the Imperial Clan Li Rengshu to perform announcement rites and oversee repairs.

sentences.zh: 九年四月二十六日夜，大風，含元殿四鴟吻皆落，拔殿前樹三，壞金吾仗舍，廢樓觀內外城門數處，光化門西城牆壞七十七步。

translations.literal: On the night of the twenty-sixth day of the fourth month of the ninth year, a great wind blew; all four ridge ornaments of the Hanyuan Hall fell; three trees before the hall were uprooted; the Jinwu guard barracks were damaged; gate towers and pavilions at several inner and outer city gates were torn off; the western city wall at the Guanghua Gate was broken for seventy-seven paces.
translations.idiomatic: On the night of the twenty-sixth day of the fourth month of the ninth year a great wind struck. All four ridge ornaments of the Hanyuan Hall fell, three trees before the hall were uprooted, the Jinwu guard barracks were wrecked, gate towers and pavilions at several inner and outer city gates were torn away, and the western city wall at Guanghua Gate was broken for seventy-seven paces.

sentences.zh: 是日，廢長生院，起內道場，取李訓言沙汰僧尼故也。

translations.literal: That day, Changsheng Academy was abolished and an inner dharma altar established, because of Li Xun's proposal to purge monks and nuns.
translations.idiomatic: That same day Changsheng Academy was abolished and an inner dharma altar erected, following Li Xun's proposal to purge monks and nuns.

sentences.zh: 夏六月，鳳翔、麟遊縣暴風雨，飄害九成宮正殿及滋善寺佛舍，壞百姓屋三百間，死者百餘人，牛馬不知其數。

translations.literal: In the summer sixth month, at Fengxiang and Linyou counties a violent wind and rain swept and harmed the main hall of Jiucheng Palace and the Buddha halls of Zishan Temple, destroyed three hundred common dwellings, more than a hundred dead, cattle and horses beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of summer violent wind and rain struck Fengxiang and Linyou counties, damaging the main hall of Jiucheng Palace and the Buddha halls of Zishan Temple, destroying three hundred private dwellings, killing more than a hundred people, and killing cattle and horses beyond count.

sentences.zh: 九月後，霖雨並雪，凡陰一百五十餘日，至正月五日，誅二張，孝和反正，方晴霽。

translations.literal: After the ninth month, continuous rain and also snow—for more than one hundred fifty overcast days; until the fifth day of the first month, when the Two Zhangs were executed and Emperor Xiaohé restored correct rule, only then did skies clear.
translations.idiomatic: After the ninth month rain and snow fell in unbroken succession for more than one hundred fifty overcast days. Not until the fifth day of the first month, when the Two Zhangs were executed and Emperor Xiaohé restored rightful rule, did the skies finally clear.

sentences.zh: 四月，陰，至六月一百餘日，至七月三日，誅竇懷貞等一十七家，方晴。

translations.literal: From the fourth month, overcast—for more than one hundred days until the sixth month; until the third day of the seventh month, when Dou Huaizhen and seventeen other families were executed, only then did it clear.
translations.idiomatic: From the fourth month the skies stayed overcast for more than one hundred days through the sixth month. Not until the third day of the seventh month, when Dou Huaizhen and seventeen other families were executed, did the weather clear.

sentences.zh: 景龍中，東都霖雨百餘日，閉坊市北門，駕車者苦甚汙，街中言曰：「宰相不能調陰陽，致茲恆雨，令我汙行。

translations.literal: In the Jinglong era, the Eastern Capital had continuous rain for more than one hundred days; the northern gate of the ward market was closed; carriage drivers suffered greatly from filth, and people in the streets said: "The chief ministers cannot harmonize yin and yang, causing this constant rain and making us travel in filth.
translations.idiomatic: During the Jinglong era the Eastern Capital endured more than one hundred days of rain. The northern gate of the ward market was closed, and carriage drivers were mired in filth. People in the streets said, "The chief ministers cannot harmonize yin and yang. They bring this endless rain and leave us to travel through the muck.

sentences.zh: 」會中書令楊再思過，謂之曰：「於理則然，亦卿牛劣耳。

translations.literal: " When Chief Minister of the Secretariat Yang Zaosi passed by, he said to them: "In principle that is so, but your ox is inferior too.
translations.idiomatic: " Chief Minister of the Secretariat Yang Zaosi happened to pass by and said to them, "In principle you are right—but your ox is inferior too.

sentences.zh: 」，順宗風疾，叔文用事，連月霖雨不霽。

translations.literal: " Emperor Shunzong had wind disease, Shuwen held power, and for successive months continuous rain did not clear.
translations.idiomatic: " Emperor Shunzong was afflicted with wind disease, Wang Shuwen wielded power, and the skies stayed grey with rain for months on end.

sentences.zh: 乃以憲宗為皇太子，制出日即晴。

translations.literal: Then Emperor Xianzong was made heir apparent; on the day the edict was issued the skies cleared at once.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xianzong was then made heir apparent, and the day the edict was issued the skies cleared at once.

sentences.zh: 《傳》所謂「皇之不極，厥罰恆陰」，皆此數也。

translations.literal: What the Commentary calls "When the sovereign lacks the supreme standard, the penalty is constant overcast"—all these cases are of that number.
translations.idiomatic: These are all instances of what the Commentary calls, "When the sovereign lacks the supreme standard, the penalty is constant overcast."

sentences.zh: 六月，京畿旱，蝗食稼。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, the capital region had drought; locusts ate the crops.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month drought struck the capital region and locusts devoured the crops.

sentences.zh: 太宗在苑中掇蝗，咒之曰：「人以穀為命，而汝害之，是害吾民也。

translations.literal: Emperor Taizong in the park picked up locusts and cursed them, saying: "People take grain as their life, yet you harm it—this is harming my people.
translations.idiomatic: In the imperial park Emperor Taizong picked up locusts and addressed them: "Grain is the life of the people, yet you destroy it. You are destroying my people.

sentences.zh: 百姓有過，在予一人，汝若通靈，但當食我，無害吾民。

translations.literal: If the common people have fault, it rests in me alone. If you have spiritual power, you should only eat me—do not harm my people.
translations.idiomatic: If the people have sinned, the fault is mine alone. If you possess any power, eat me instead—do not harm my people.

sentences.zh: 」將吞之，侍臣恐上致疾，遽諫止之。

translations.literal: " About to swallow them, attendants feared the emperor would fall ill and urgently remonstrated to stop him.
translations.idiomatic: " As he was about to swallow them, his attendants feared he would fall ill and urgently begged him to stop.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「所冀移災朕躬，何疾之避？

translations.literal: The emperor said: "What I hope is to shift the calamity to my own person—why should I avoid illness?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "I mean to take the calamity upon myself. Why should I fear illness?

sentences.zh: 」遂吞之。

translations.literal: " He then swallowed them.
translations.idiomatic: " He swallowed them.

sentences.zh: 是歲蝗不為患。

translations.literal: That year locusts did not become a calamity.
translations.idiomatic: That year the locusts did no harm.

sentences.zh: 五月，山東螟蝗害稼，分遣御史捕而埋之。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, borer-moths and locusts in Shandong harmed the crops; censors were dispatched separately to capture and bury them.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month borer-moths and locusts ravaged the crops in Shandong, and censors were dispatched to capture and bury them.

sentences.zh: 汴州刺史倪若水拒御史，執奏曰：「蝗是天災，自宜修德。

translations.literal: Bian Prefecture governor Ni Ruoshui resisted the censor and submitted a memorial saying: "Locusts are a heaven-sent calamity; one should naturally cultivate virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Bian Prefecture governor Ni Ruoshui blocked the censor and submitted a memorial: "Locusts are a heaven-sent calamity. The proper response is to cultivate virtue.

sentences.zh: 劉聰時，除既不得，為害滋深。

translations.literal: In Liu Cong's time, when extermination did not succeed, the harm grew ever deeper.
translations.idiomatic: In Liu Cong's time extermination failed and the damage only grew worse.

sentences.zh: 」宰相姚崇牒報之曰：「劉聰偽主，德不勝妖；

translations.literal: " Chief minister Yao Chong replied by official dispatch: "Liu Cong was a usurping ruler—virtue did not overcome the portent;
translations.idiomatic: " Chief Minister Yao Chong replied by official dispatch: "Liu Cong was a usurping ruler whose virtue could not overcome the portent;

sentences.zh: 今日聖朝，妖不勝德。

translations.literal: in today's sage dynasty, the portent does not overcome virtue.
translations.idiomatic: in today's sage dynasty the portent cannot overcome virtue.

sentences.zh: 古之良守，蝗蟲避境，若言修德可免，彼豈無德致然。

translations.literal: Ancient good governors had locusts avoid their borders; if cultivating virtue could avert them, were those men without virtue that it happened so?
translations.idiomatic: Locusts avoided the borders of good governors in antiquity. If virtue alone could avert them, were those men without virtue when disaster struck?

sentences.zh: 今坐看食苗，忍而不救，因此饑饉，將何以安？

translations.literal: Now to sit and watch them eat the seedlings, endure it and not rescue—when famine follows from this, how will the realm be settled?
translations.idiomatic: To sit idle while they devour the seedlings and refuse to act—when famine follows, how will the realm be kept at peace?

sentences.zh: 」卒行埋瘞之法，獲蝗一十四萬，乃投之汴河，流者不可勝數。

translations.literal: " In the end they carried out the method of burial; they obtained one hundred forty thousand locusts, then cast them into the Bian River; those carried downstream were beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: " In the end they carried out the burial method, collected one hundred forty thousand locusts, and cast them into the Bian River until the current was thick with them beyond count.

sentences.zh: 朝議喧然，上復以問崇，崇對曰：「凡事有違經而合道，反道而適權者，彼庸儒不足以知之。

translations.literal: Court discussion was clamorous; the emperor again questioned Chong, and Chong replied: "In all matters there are those that violate the classics yet accord with the Way, or oppose the Way yet suit expediency—those mediocre Confucians are not sufficient to understand them.
translations.idiomatic: Court opinion was in an uproar, and the emperor questioned Chong again. Chong replied, "There are times when one must depart from the classics yet follow the Way, or set aside the Way to meet necessity—mediocre scholars cannot grasp that.

sentences.zh: 縱除之不盡，猶勝養之以成災。

translations.literal: Even if extermination is not complete, it is still better than nurturing them until they become a calamity.
translations.idiomatic: Even if we cannot destroy them all, that is still better than letting them breed into catastrophe.

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「殺蟲太多，有傷和氣，公其思之。

translations.literal: " The emperor said: "Killing too many insects harms harmonious qi—Sir, consider this.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor said, "Killing so many insects may harm the harmonious qi of the realm. Consider this carefully.

sentences.zh: 」崇曰：「若救人殺蟲致禍，臣所甘心。

translations.literal: " Chong said: "If saving people by killing insects brings calamity upon me, that is what I willingly accept.
translations.idiomatic: " Chong said, "If saving the people by killing insects brings calamity upon me, I accept it willingly.

sentences.zh: 」八月四日，敕河南、河北檢校捕蝗使狄光嗣、康瓘、敬昭道、高昌、賈彥璿等，宜令待蟲盡而刈禾將畢，即入京奏事。

translations.literal: " On the fourth day of the eighth month, an edict to the locust-inspection commissioners of Henan and Hebei—Di Guangsi, Kang Guan, Jing Zhaodao, Gao Chang, Jia Yanxuan, and others—ordered that they should wait until the insects were gone and the harvest nearly complete, then enter the capital to report affairs.
translations.idiomatic: " On the fourth day of the eighth month an edict instructed the locust-inspection commissioners of Henan and Hebei—Di Guangsi, Kang Guan, Jing Zhaodao, Gao Chang, Jia Yanxuan, and others—to wait until the insects were gone and the harvest nearly finished, then come to the capital to report.

sentences.zh: 諫議大夫韓思復上言曰：「伏聞河北蝗蟲，頃日益熾，經歷之處，苗稼都盡。

translations.literal: Remonstrance Counselor Han Sifu submitted a memorial saying: "I have heard that locusts in Hebei have lately grown daily fiercer; wherever they have passed, seedlings and crops are entirely gone.
translations.idiomatic: Remonstrance Counselor Han Sifu submitted a memorial: "I hear that locusts in Hebei grow fiercer by the day, and wherever they pass the crops are stripped bare.

sentences.zh: 臣望陛下省咎責躬，發使宣慰，損不急之務，去至冗之人。

translations.literal: Your servant hopes Your Majesty will examine faults and blame yourself, dispatch envoys to announce comfort, reduce non-urgent affairs, and remove the most redundant personnel.
translations.idiomatic: I urge Your Majesty to examine your own conduct, send envoys to comfort the people, cut non-urgent business, and dismiss the most redundant officials.

sentences.zh: 上下同心，君臣一德，持此至誠，以答休咎。

translations.literal: Above and below of one mind, ruler and ministers of one virtue—holding this utmost sincerity to answer blessing and calamity.
translations.idiomatic: If ruler and ministers unite in one purpose and one virtue, and meet heaven's judgment with utmost sincerity, blessing and calamity may yet be answered.

sentences.zh: 前後捕蝗使望並停之。

translations.literal: The successive locust-capture commissioners should all be stopped.
translations.idiomatic: All the locust-capture commissioners should be recalled.

sentences.zh: 」上出符疏付中書姚崇，乃令思復往山東檢視蟲災之所，及還，具以聞。

translations.literal: " The emperor produced the talisman memorial and handed it to Chief Minister of the Secretariat Yao Chong, then ordered Sifu to go to Shandong to inspect places of insect calamity; when he returned, he reported fully.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor handed the memorial to Chief Minister Yao Chong and ordered Sifu to inspect the insect disaster in Shandong. When Sifu returned he reported in full.

sentences.zh: 二十五年，貝州蝗食苗，有白鳥數萬，群飛食蝗，一夕而盡。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year, at Bei Prefecture locusts ate the seedlings; tens of thousands of white birds flew in flocks eating locusts, and in one night they were gone.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fifth year locusts devoured the seedlings at Bei Prefecture. Tens of thousands of white birds descended in flocks to eat the locusts, and in a single night they were gone.

sentences.zh: 明年，榆林關有虸蚄食苗，群雀來食，數日而盡。

translations.literal: The next year, at Yulin Pass caterpillars ate the seedlings; flocks of sparrows came to eat them, and in several days they were gone.
translations.idiomatic: The next year caterpillars devoured the seedlings at Yulin Pass. Flocks of sparrows came to feed on them, and within days they were gone.

sentences.zh: ，貴州紫蟲食苗，時有赤鳥群飛，自東北來食之。

translations.literal: at Gui Prefecture purple insects ate the seedlings; at that time flocks of red birds flew from the northeast to eat them.
translations.idiomatic: At Gui Prefecture purple insects devoured the seedlings, and flocks of red birds flew in from the northeast to eat them.

sentences.zh: 秋，虸蚄食苗，關西尤甚，米鬥千錢。

translations.literal: In autumn, caterpillars ate the seedlings; west of the Pass it was especially severe; rice was one thousand cash per dou.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn caterpillars ravaged the seedlings, worst of all west of the Pass, where rice reached one thousand cash per dou.

sentences.zh: 秋，關輔大蝗，田稼食盡，百姓饑，捕蝗為食，蒸曝，去颺足翅而食之。

translations.literal: In autumn, great locusts in the Guanfu region; field crops were entirely eaten; common people were hungry; they captured locusts for food, steamed and dried them, removed wings and legs, and ate them.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn locusts swarmed the Guanfu region until the fields were bare. The people went hungry and turned to eating locusts—steaming and drying them, stripping off wings and legs, and making a meal of what remained.

sentences.zh: 明年夏，蝗尤甚，自東海西盡河、隴，群飛蔽天，旬日不息。

translations.literal: The next summer, locusts were especially severe; from the Eastern Sea west to the He and Long regions, they flew in flocks blotting out the sky for ten days without ceasing.
translations.idiomatic: The next summer the locusts were worse still. From the Eastern Sea west to the He and Long regions they flew in clouds that blotted out the sky for ten days without pause.

sentences.zh: 經行之處，草木牛畜毛，靡有孑遺。

translations.literal: Where they passed, grass, trees, and the hair of cattle and livestock—nothing was left surviving alone.
translations.idiomatic: Where they passed, not a blade of grass, leaf, or hair on cattle and livestock was left untouched.

sentences.zh: 關輔已東，穀大貴，餓饉枕道。

translations.literal: East of the Guanfu region, grain was greatly dear; famine victims lined the roads.
translations.idiomatic: East of the Guanfu region grain prices soared and the starved lay dead along the roads.

sentences.zh: 京師大亂之後，李懷光據河中，諸軍進討，國用罄竭。

translations.literal: After the great disorder in the capital, Li Huaiguang held Hezhong; various armies advanced to attack; state revenues were exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: After the great upheaval in the capital Li Huaiguang held Hezhong while imperial armies marched against him, and the treasury was drained dry.

sentences.zh: 衣冠之家，多有殍殕者。

translations.literal: Among gentry families, many died of starvation.
translations.idiomatic: Even among gentry families many starved to death.

sentences.zh: 旱甚，灞水將竭，井皆無水。

translations.literal: Drought was severe; the Ba River nearly dried up; wells all had no water.
translations.idiomatic: The drought was severe. The Ba River nearly ran dry and the wells were empty.

sentences.zh: 有司奏國用裁可支七旬。

translations.literal: The responsible offices reported that state revenues could barely support seventy days.
translations.idiomatic: The responsible offices reported that state funds would barely last seventy days.

sentences.zh: 德宗減膳，不御正殿。

translations.literal: Emperor Dezong reduced his meals and did not attend the main hall.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Dezong cut his meals and ceased holding court in the main hall.

sentences.zh: 百司不急之費，皆減之。

translations.literal: Among the hundred offices, all non-urgent expenditures were reduced.
translations.idiomatic: Every non-urgent expense across the bureaucracy was cut.

sentences.zh: 夏，鎮、冀蝗，害稼。

translations.literal: In summer, locusts in Zhen and Ji harmed the crops.
translations.idiomatic: In summer locusts ravaged the crops in Zhen and Ji prefectures.

sentences.zh: 秋，洪州旱，螟蝗害稼八萬頃。

translations.literal: In autumn, Hong Prefecture had drought; borer-moths and locusts harmed eighty thousand qing of crops.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn drought struck Hong Prefecture, and borer-moths and locusts destroyed eighty thousand qing of crops.

sentences.zh: 秋，旱，罷選舉。

translations.literal: In autumn, drought; examinations were suspended.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn drought led to the suspension of civil examinations.

sentences.zh: ，河南、河北旱，蝗害稼；

translations.literal: in Henan and Hebei drought; locusts harmed the crops;
translations.idiomatic: In Henan and Hebei there was drought and locusts ravaged the crops;

sentences.zh: 京師旱尤甚，徙市，閉坊南門。

translations.literal: drought in the capital was especially severe; markets were moved; the southern gate of the ward was closed.
translations.idiomatic: the capital suffered worst of all—markets were relocated and the southern ward gate was closed.

sentences.zh: 四年六月，天下旱，蝗食田，禱祈無效，上憂形於色。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the fourth year, the realm had drought; locusts ate the fields; prayers and supplications had no effect; the emperor's worry showed in his countenance.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of the fourth year drought gripped the realm and locusts devoured the fields. Prayers availed nothing, and the emperor's distress showed plainly on his face.

sentences.zh: 宰臣曰：「星官奏天時當爾，乞不過勞聖慮。

translations.literal: The chief ministers said: "The astral officers report that the season should be thus; we beg that Your Majesty not overtax your sacred concern.
translations.idiomatic: The chief ministers said, "The astral officers report that the season is as heaven ordains. We beg Your Majesty not to burden yourself with undue worry.

sentences.zh: 」文宗懍然改容曰：「朕為天下主，無德及人，致此災旱。

translations.literal: " Emperor Wenzong, sternly changing expression, said: "I am sovereign of the realm, yet my virtue has not reached the people, bringing this calamity of drought.
translations.idiomatic: " Emperor Wenzong's face darkened as he said, "I am sovereign of the realm, yet my virtue has not reached the people, and so this drought has come.

sentences.zh: 今又彗星謫見於上，若三日內不雨，當退歸南內，卿等自選賢明之君以安天下。

translations.literal: Now again a banished comet appears above; if within three days there is no rain, I should withdraw to the Southern Palace—you yourselves choose a wise and enlightened ruler to settle the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Now a banished comet appears in the heavens. If it does not rain within three days, I shall withdraw to the Southern Palace, and you must choose a wise ruler to secure the realm.

sentences.zh: 」宰臣嗚咽流涕不能已。

translations.literal: " The chief ministers sobbed and wept, unable to stop.
translations.idiomatic: " The chief ministers sobbed until they could speak no further.

sentences.zh: 是歲，河南府界黑蟲食苗。

translations.literal: That year, within Henan Prefecture black insects ate the seedlings.
translations.idiomatic: That year black insects devoured the seedlings within Henan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 河南、河北蝗，害稼都盡。

translations.literal: In Henan and Hebei, locusts entirely destroyed the crops.
translations.idiomatic: In Henan and Hebei locusts stripped the fields bare.

sentences.zh: 鎮、定等州，田稼既盡，至於野草樹葉細枝亦盡。

translations.literal: In Zhen, Ding, and other prefectures, field crops were already gone—even wild grass, tree leaves, and fine branches were entirely gone.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhen, Ding, and other prefectures the harvest was gone, and even wild grass, tree leaves, and twigs were eaten clean.

sentences.zh: ，山南鄧、唐等州蝗，害稼。

translations.literal: in Shannan, Deng, Tang, and other prefectures locusts harmed the crops.
translations.idiomatic: In Shannan, Deng, Tang, and other prefectures locusts ravaged the crops.

sentences.zh: 四月二十九日，雲陽石燃方丈，晝如炭，夜則光見，投草木於其上則焚，歷年方止。

translations.literal: On the twenty-ninth day of the fourth month, at Yunyang a stone one square zhang burned; by day it was like charcoal, by night light appeared; casting grass and trees upon it caused burning; only after years did it stop.
translations.idiomatic: On the twenty-ninth day of the fourth month a stone one square zhang in size burned at Yunyang. By day it looked like charcoal; by night it glowed. Grass and wood thrown upon it burst into flame, and the fire did not cease for years.

sentences.zh: 證聖元年正月十六日夜，明堂火，延及天堂，京城光照如晝，至曙並為灰燼。

translations.literal: On the night of the sixteenth day of the first month of the first year of Zhengsheng, the Bright Hall caught fire; it spread to the Hall of Paradise; the capital was lit bright as day; by dawn both were ash.
translations.idiomatic: On the night of the sixteenth day of the first month of the first Zhengsheng year the Bright Hall caught fire and the blaze spread to the Hall of Paradise. The capital blazed bright as day, and by dawn both halls were ash.

sentences.zh: 則天欲避殿徹樂，宰相姚璹以為火因麻主，人護不謹，非天災也，不宜貶損。

translations.literal: Empress Wu wished to withdraw from the hall and cease music; chief minister Yao Shuo held that the fire arose because those guarding it had been careless—not a heaven-sent calamity—and one should not demean oneself.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Wu wished to withdraw from court and suspend music, but Chief Minister Yao Shuo argued that careless guarding had caused the fire—it was no heaven-sent calamity, and she should not demean the throne.

sentences.zh: 乃勸則天御端門觀酺，引建章故事，令薛懷義重造明堂以厭勝之。

translations.literal: He then urged Empress Wu to attend the Duan Gate to view the feast; citing the precedent of Jianzhang, he had Xue Huaiyi rebuild the Bright Hall to overcome it by magic.
translations.idiomatic: He urged Empress Wu instead to watch the public feast from the Duan Gate, cited the precedent of Jianzhang Palace, and had Xue Huaiyi rebuild the Bright Hall as apotropaic counter-magic.

sentences.zh: 則天時，建昌王武攸寧置內庫，長五百步，二百餘間，別貯財物以求媚。

translations.literal: In Empress Wu's time, Prince of Jianchang Wu Youning established an inner treasury five hundred paces long, more than two hundred rooms, storing goods separately to seek favor.
translations.idiomatic: During Empress Wu's reign Prince of Jianchang Wu Youning built an inner treasury five hundred paces long with more than two hundred rooms, hoarding valuables apart to curry favor.

sentences.zh: 一夕為天災所燔，玩好並盡。

translations.literal: In one night it was burned by heaven's calamity; curios and treasures were all gone.
translations.idiomatic: In a single night heaven's fire consumed it, and every treasure within was lost.

sentences.zh: 景龍中，東都淩空觀災，火自東北來，其金銅諸像，銷鑠並盡。

translations.literal: In the Jinglong era, the Lingkong Abbey at the Eastern Capital suffered disaster; fire came from the northeast; its gold and bronze images were melted away entirely.
translations.idiomatic: During the Jinglong era fire struck Lingkong Abbey in the Eastern Capital. The blaze came from the northeast and melted every gold and bronze image to nothing.

sentences.zh: ，洪、潭二州災，火延燒郡舍。

translations.literal: at Hong and Tan prefectures disaster; fire spread and burned the commandery offices.
translations.idiomatic: At Hong and Tan prefectures fire spread through the commandery offices.

sentences.zh: 郡人先見火精赤暾暾飛來，旋即火發。

translations.literal: People of the commandery first saw a fire spirit, red and glowing, fly in; immediately fire broke out.
translations.idiomatic: The people first saw a glowing red fire-spirit fly in, and fire broke out at once.

sentences.zh: 十五年，衡州災，火延燒三四百家。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year, Heng Prefecture suffered disaster; fire spread and burned three or four hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year fire at Heng Prefecture spread through three or four hundred households.

sentences.zh: 郡人見物大如甕，赤如燭籠，此物所至，即火發。

translations.literal: People of the commandery saw a thing as large as a jar, red as a candle lantern; wherever this thing went, fire broke out.
translations.idiomatic: The people saw a thing as large as a jar, red as a lantern—wherever it passed, fire followed.

sentences.zh: 十八年二月十八日，大雨雪，俄又雷震，飛龍廄災。

translations.literal: On the eighteenth day of the second month of the eighteenth year, heavy rain and snow; soon thunder struck; the Flying Dragon Stable suffered disaster.
translations.idiomatic: On the eighteenth day of the second month of the eighteenth year heavy rain and snow fell, thunder cracked, and the Flying Dragon Stable caught fire.

sentences.zh: 六月七日，東都應天門觀災，延燒左右延福門，經日不減。

translations.literal: On the seventh day of the sixth month, the Yingtian Gate Abbey at the Eastern Capital suffered disaster; the fire spread to the Yanfu gates left and right; for a whole day it did not diminish.
translations.idiomatic: On the seventh day of the sixth month fire struck Yingtian Gate Abbey in the Eastern Capital and spread to the Yanfu gates on either side. The blaze burned undiminished for a full day.

sentences.zh: 九載三月，華嶽廟災。

translations.literal: In the third month of the ninth year, the Mount Hua shrine suffered disaster.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the ninth Tianbao year fire struck the Mount Hua shrine.

sentences.zh: 十載正月，大風，陝州運船失火，燒二百一十五隻，損米一百萬石，舟人死者六百人，又燒商人船一百隻。

translations.literal: In the first month of the tenth year, great wind; transport boats at Shaan Prefecture caught fire, burning two hundred fifteen vessels, losing one million shi of rice; six hundred boatmen died; also one hundred merchant vessels burned.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the tenth Tianbao year a gale struck. Transport boats at Shaan Prefecture caught fire: two hundred fifteen vessels burned, a million shi of rice were lost, six hundred boatmen perished, and a hundred merchant ships went up in flames.

sentences.zh: 其年八月六日，武庫災，燒二十八間十九架，兵器四十七萬件。

translations.literal: On the sixth day of the eighth month of that year, the armory suffered disaster, burning twenty-eight rooms and nineteen racks, four hundred seventy thousand weapons.
translations.idiomatic: On the sixth day of the eighth month that year the armory burned: twenty-eight rooms and nineteen racks were destroyed, and four hundred seventy thousand weapons were lost.

sentences.zh: 十一月，回紇焚東都宜春院，延及明堂，甲子日而盡。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, the Uyghurs burned the Yichun Court at the Eastern Capital; it spread to the Bright Hall; on the jiazi day it was entirely gone.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month the Uyghurs burned Yichun Court in the Eastern Capital. The fire spread to the Bright Hall and burned itself out on the jiazi day.

sentences.zh: 十二月二十五夜，鄂州失火，燒船三千艘，延及岸上居人二千餘家，死者四五千人。

translations.literal: On the night of the twenty-fifth day of the twelfth month, E Prefecture caught fire, burning three thousand boats; it spread to more than two thousand households of shore dwellers; four or five thousand died.
translations.idiomatic: On the night of the twenty-fifth day of the twelfth month fire broke out at E Prefecture. Three thousand boats burned, the blaze spread to more than two thousand homes along the shore, and four or five thousand people died.

sentences.zh: 二月，莊嚴寺佛圖災。

translations.literal: In the second month, the pagoda of Zhengyan Temple suffered disaster.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month fire struck the pagoda of Zhengyan Temple.

sentences.zh: 初有疾風，震雷薄擊，俄而火從佛圖中出，寺僧數百人急救之，乃止，棟宇無損。

translations.literal: At first there was a fierce wind and thunder striking close; soon fire issued from within the pagoda; several hundred temple monks urgently fought it, and it stopped; the halls and buildings were undamaged.
translations.idiomatic: At first a fierce wind rose and thunder struck close by. Fire then burst from the pagoda itself. Several hundred monks fought it at once and brought it under control before the halls and buildings were harmed.

sentences.zh: ，蘇州火。

translations.literal: fire at Suzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Fire broke out at Suzhou.

sentences.zh: 十九年四月，家令寺火。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the nineteenth year, Jialing Temple caught fire.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the nineteenth year Jialing Temple caught fire.

sentences.zh: 二十年四月，開業寺火。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the twentieth year, Kaiye Temple caught fire.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the twentieth year Kaiye Temple caught fire.

sentences.zh: ，御史臺舍火。

translations.literal: the Censorate offices caught fire.
translations.idiomatic: The Censorate offices caught fire.

sentences.zh: 七年，鎮州甲仗庫一十三間災，節度使王承宗殺主守，坐死者百餘人。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, thirteen rooms of the armor-and-weapons storehouse at Zhen Prefecture suffered disaster; military governor Wang Chengzong executed the chief custodian; more than a hundred were put to death on account of it.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year fire destroyed thirteen rooms of the armor storehouse at Zhen Prefecture. Military Governor Wang Chengzong executed the chief custodian, and more than a hundred others were put to death in connection with the disaster.

sentences.zh: 承宗方拒天軍，而兵仗為災所焚，天意嫉惡也。

translations.literal: Chengzong was just then resisting the imperial army, yet arms and weapons were burned by disaster—Heaven's intent abhorred evil.
translations.idiomatic: Chengzong was then resisting the imperial army, yet his arms and weapons were consumed by fire—a sign that Heaven abhorred his rebellion.

sentences.zh: 十年四月，河陰轉運院火。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the tenth year, the Heyin Transport Office caught fire.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the tenth year the Heyin Transport Office caught fire.

sentences.zh: 十一月，獻陵寢宮永巷火。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, the Eternal Lane of the sleeping palace at Xian Mausoleum caught fire.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month fire broke out in the Eternal Lane of the sleeping palace at Xian Mausoleum.

sentences.zh: 十一年十二月，未央宮及飛龍草場火，皆王承宗、李師道謀撓用兵，陰遣盜縱火也。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of the eleventh year, Weiyang Palace and the Flying Dragon fodder grounds caught fire—both were Wang Chengzong and Li Shidao plotting to obstruct the use of troops, secretly sending thieves to set fires.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month of the eleventh year Weiyang Palace and the Flying Dragon fodder grounds burned. Both fires were set by thieves secretly dispatched by Wang Chengzong and Li Shidao to sabotage the imperial campaign.

sentences.zh: 時李師道於鄆州起宮殿，欲謀僭亂。

translations.literal: At the time Li Shidao was raising palaces at Yan Prefecture, intending to plot usurpation and rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Li Shidao was building palaces at Yan Prefecture, plotting rebellion and usurpation.

sentences.zh: 既成，是歲為災並盡，俄而族滅。

translations.literal: Once completed, that year they were all destroyed by disaster; soon afterward his clan was exterminated.
translations.idiomatic: Once they were finished, fire destroyed them that same year, and soon afterward his entire clan was wiped out.

sentences.zh: 十月甲辰，昭德宮火，延燒至宣政東垣及門下省，至晡方息。

translations.literal: On jiachen day of the tenth month, Zhaode Palace caught fire; the blaze spread to the eastern wall of Xuanzheng and the Secretariat; only at dusk did it cease.
translations.idiomatic: On the jiachen day of the tenth month Zhaode Palace caught fire. The blaze spread to the eastern wall of Xuanzheng Hall and the Secretariat and did not die down until dusk.

sentences.zh: 八年十二月，昭成宮火。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of the eighth year, Zhaocheng Palace caught fire.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month of the eighth year Zhaocheng Palace caught fire.

sentences.zh: 九年六月乙亥朔，西市火。

translations.literal: On the first day, yihai day of the sixth month of the ninth year, the Western Market caught fire.
translations.idiomatic: On the first day of the sixth month of the ninth year, the yihai day, the Western Market caught fire.

sentences.zh: 六月，萬年縣東市火，燒屋宇貨財不知其數。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, the Eastern Market of Wannian County caught fire; buildings and goods burned in numbers beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month fire struck the Eastern Market of Wannian County, destroying buildings and goods beyond count.

sentences.zh: 又西內神龍宮火。

translations.literal: Also the Shenlong Palace within the Western Inner Palace caught fire.
translations.idiomatic: The Shenlong Palace in the Western Inner Palace also caught fire.

sentences.zh: 七月，汴州相國寺佛閣災。

translations.literal: In the seventh month, the Buddha pavilion of Xiangguo Temple at Bian Prefecture suffered disaster.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month fire destroyed the Buddha pavilion of Xiangguo Temple at Bian Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 是日晚，微雨，震電，寺僧見赤塊在三門樓藤網中，周繞一匝而火作。

translations.literal: That evening there was light rain and thunder; temple monks saw a red mass in the vine net of the triple gate tower; it circled once around and fire broke out.
translations.idiomatic: That evening came light rain and thunder. The monks saw a red mass in the vine netting of the triple gate tower. It circled once and burst into flame.

sentences.zh: 良久，赤塊北飛，越前殿飛入佛閣網中，如三門周繞轉而火作。

translations.literal: After a long while the red mass flew north, crossed the front hall and flew into the net of the Buddha pavilion; as at the triple gate it circled around and fire broke out.
translations.idiomatic: After a long while the red mass flew north, passed over the front hall, and entered the netting of the Buddha pavilion. It circled as before and fire broke out again.

sentences.zh: 如是三日不息，訖為灰燼。

translations.literal: Thus for three days it did not cease; in the end it became ash.
translations.idiomatic: The fire burned without ceasing for three days until the pavilion was ash.

sentences.zh: 貞觀初，白鵲巢於殿庭之槐樹，其巢合歡如腰鼓，左右稱賀。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhenguan, a white magpie nested in the pagoda tree of the palace courtyard; its nest was joined like a waist drum; those left and right offered congratulations.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Zhenguan era a white magpie nested in the pagoda tree of the palace courtyard. Its nest was woven tight as a waist drum, and courtiers on either side offered congratulations.

sentences.zh: 太宗曰：「吾常笑隋文帝好言祥端。

translations.literal: Emperor Taizong said: "I have often laughed at Emperor Wen of Sui for loving to speak of auspicious portents.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taizong said, "I have often mocked Emperor Wen of Sui for his fondness for auspicious portents.

sentences.zh: 瑞在得賢，白鵲子何益於事？

translations.literal: Auspiciousness lies in obtaining the worthy—what use to affairs is a white magpie chick?
translations.idiomatic: True auspiciousness lies in finding worthy men. What good is a white magpie chick to the realm?

sentences.zh: 」命掇之，送於野。

translations.literal: " He ordered it taken down and sent to the wild.
translations.idiomatic: " He ordered the nest removed and sent the birds back to the wild.

sentences.zh: 高宗文明後，天下頻奏雌雉化為雄，或半化未化，兼以獻之，則天臨朝之兆。

translations.literal: After Emperor Gaozong's Wenming reign title, throughout the realm reports came repeatedly of hen pheasants turning into cocks, some half-transformed and not yet transformed, and they were presented as tribute—an omen of Empress Wu's holding court.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Gaozong's Wenming era the realm repeatedly reported hen pheasants turning into cocks, some only half changed, and such birds were sent up as tribute—omens of Empress Wu's rise to power.

sentences.zh: ，突厥溫傅等未叛時，有鳴鵽群飛入塞，相繼蔽野，邊人相驚曰：「突厥雀南飛，突厥犯塞之兆也。

translations.literal: before Wen Fu of the Turks and others had rebelled, flocks of calling quail flew south into the frontier passes in succession, covering the fields; border people alarmed one another, saying: "When Turkic quail fly south, it is an omen of Turks violating the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: Before Wen Fu of the Turks and his allies rebelled, flocks of calling quail flew south through the passes in endless waves, darkening the fields. Border folk cried in alarm, "When Turkic quail fly south, the Turks will raid the frontier."

sentences.zh: 」至二年正月，還復北飛，至靈夏已北，悉墜地而死，視之，皆無頭。

translations.literal: " By the first month of the second year they again flew north; reaching Ling and Xia and beyond, all fell to the ground dead; on inspection, all were headless.
translations.idiomatic: " By the first month of the second year they flew north again. Beyond Ling and Xia they all dropped dead to the ground—and every one was headless.

sentences.zh: 裴行儉問右史苗神客曰：「鳥獸之祥，乃應人事，何也？

translations.literal: Pei Xingjian asked Right Scribe Miao Shenke, saying: "Auspicious signs from birds and beasts correspond to human affairs—why is this?
translations.idiomatic: Pei Xingjian asked Right Scribe Miao Shenke, "Bird and beast omens answer to human affairs—why is that?

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「人雖最靈，而稟性含氣，同于萬類，故吉凶兆於彼，而禍福應於此。

translations.literal: " He replied: "Though humans are most spiritual, they receive nature and hold qi, the same as the myriad kinds; therefore good and ill omens appear in them, while fortune and calamity answer here.
translations.idiomatic: " He replied, "Human beings are the most spiritual of creatures, yet we share in nature and qi with all living things. Omens of fortune and disaster appear in them, and blessing or ruin answers in us.

sentences.zh: 聖王受命，龍鳳為嘉瑞者，和氣同也。

translations.literal: When a sage king receives the Mandate, dragon and phoenix become auspicious signs because harmonizing qi is shared.
translations.idiomatic: When a sage king receives the Mandate, dragon and phoenix appear as blessed omens because heaven's harmonious qi flows through all things alike.

sentences.zh: 故漢祖斬蛇而驗秦之必亡，仲尼感麟而知己之將死。

translations.literal: Thus the Han Founder's slaying of the serpent verified that Qin must perish; Zhongni's being moved by the qilin showed that he himself would soon die.
