translations.idiomatic: Thus when the Han Founder slew the serpent, it confirmed Qin's doom; when Confucius was moved by the qilin, he knew his own death was near.

sentences.zh: 夷羊在牧，殷紂已滅。

translations.literal: Barbarian sheep were in the pasture; Zhou of Yin was already destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: Barbarian sheep appeared in the pastures just as Zhou, last king of Yin, was overthrown.

sentences.zh: 鵒來巢，魯昭出奔。

translations.literal: Magpies came to nest; Duke Zhao of Lu fled into exile.
translations.idiomatic: Magpies came to nest in Lu—and Duke Zhao fled into exile.

sentences.zh: 鼠舞端門，燕剌誅死。

translations.literal: Rats danced at the Duan Gate; the Prince of Yan was executed to death.
translations.idiomatic: Rats danced before the Duan Gate—and the Prince of Yan was put to death.

sentences.zh: 大鳥飛集，昌邑以敗。

translations.literal: Great birds flew and gathered; the Prince of Changyi was ruined.
translations.idiomatic: Great birds gathered in flight—and the Prince of Changyi was cast down.

sentences.zh: 是故君子虔恭寅畏，動必思義，雖在幽獨，如承大事，知神明之照臨，懼患難之及己。

translations.literal: Therefore the noble person is reverent and in awe, in every movement necessarily thinking of righteousness; even in hidden solitude, as if undertaking a great affair, knowing that the spirits illuminate and oversee, fearing that calamity may reach oneself.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore the noble person keeps reverent awe in every act and weighs each move by right conduct. Even alone in secret he behaves as though facing a great rite, knowing the spirits watch over him and dreading that disaster may find him.

sentences.zh: 雉升鼎耳，殷宗側身以修德，鵩止坐隅，賈生作賦以敘命。

translations.literal: A pheasant ascended the tripod ear; the Yin sovereign corrected himself to cultivate virtue; an owl stopped in a corner of the seat; Jia Yi composed a fu to narrate fate.
translations.idiomatic: When a pheasant perched on the tripod ear, the Yin sovereign corrected himself and cultivated virtue; when an owl stopped in his corner, Jia Yi wrote a rhapsody on fate.

sentences.zh: 卒以無患者，德勝妖也。

translations.literal: In the end those who remained unharmed did so because virtue overcame portents.
translations.idiomatic: Those who escaped harm did so because virtue triumphs over omens.

sentences.zh: 四月戊申，乾陵上仙觀天尊殿，有雙鵲銜泥及柴，補殿之隙壞，凡十五處。

translations.literal: On wushen day of the fourth month, at the Hall of the Celestial Worthy of Upper Transcendence Abbey at Qian Mausoleum, a pair of magpies carried mud and firewood, repairing gaps and damage in the hall—in all fifteen places.
translations.idiomatic: On the wushen day of the fourth month at the Hall of the Celestial Worthy in Upper Transcendence Abbey at Qian Mausoleum, a pair of magpies carried mud and twigs and mended fifteen damaged spots in the hall.

sentences.zh: 其年九月，大鳥見於武功縣，群鳥隨而噪之。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of that year, a great bird appeared at Wugong County; flocks of birds followed and clamored at it.
translations.idiomatic: That September a great bird appeared in Wugong County, and flocks of smaller birds followed it, shrieking.

sentences.zh: 神策將軍張日芬射得之，肉翅狐首，四足，足有爪，其廣四尺三寸，其毛色赤，形類蝙蝠。

translations.literal: Shence General Zhang Rifen shot and obtained it: fleshy wings and fox head, four feet with claws; its span four chi three cun; its fur red; in form like a bat.
translations.idiomatic: Shence General Zhang Rifen shot it down. It had fleshy wings and a fox's head, four clawed feet, a wingspan of four chi three cun, red fur, and the shape of a bat.

sentences.zh: 十一年，渭州獲赤烏。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year, a red crow was captured at Wei Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year a red crow was captured at Wei Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 十三年五月，左羽林軍鵒乳雀。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the thirteenth year, in the Left Forest Army a magpie nursed a sparrow.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the thirteenth year a magpie was found nursing a sparrow in the Left Forest Army.

sentences.zh: 三月，中書省梧桐樹有鵲以泥為巢。

translations.literal: In the third month, on a parasol tree at the Secretariat a magpie made a nest of mud.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month a magpie built a mud nest in a parasol tree at the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 四年夏，汴、鄭二州群鳥皆飛入田緒、李納境內，銜木為城，高二三尺，方十里。

translations.literal: In the summer of the fourth year, flocks of birds from Bian and Zheng prefectures all flew into the territories of Tian Xu and Li Na, carrying wood to build ramparts two or three chi high, ten li square.
translations.idiomatic: That summer flocks of birds from Bian and Zheng prefectures flew into the domains of Tian Xu and Li Na, carrying twigs to build fortifications two or three chi high and ten li across.

sentences.zh: 緒、納惡之，命焚之，信宿而復，鳥口皆流血。

translations.literal: Xu and Na hated it and ordered the structures burned; after one night's lodging they were rebuilt; the birds' mouths all bled.
translations.idiomatic: Xu and Na loathed the omen and ordered the structures burned, but within a night the birds rebuilt them—and every bird's beak ran with blood.

sentences.zh: 十年四月，有大鳥飛集宮中，食雜骨數日，獲之，不食而死。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the tenth year, a great bird flew and gathered in the palace, eating assorted bones for several days; once captured, it would not eat and died.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the tenth year a great bird alighted in the palace and fed on scraps of bone for days. Once captured it refused food and died.

sentences.zh: 六月辛未晦，水鳥集左藏庫。

translations.literal: On the last day, xinwei day of the sixth month, water birds gathered at the Left Treasury.
translations.idiomatic: On the last xinwei day of the sixth month water birds gathered at the Left Treasury.

sentences.zh: 十四年秋，有鳥色青，類鳩鵲，息于宋郊，所止之處，群鳥翼衛，朝夕嗛稻粱以哺之。

translations.literal: In the autumn of the fourteenth year, there was a bird blue in color, resembling turtledove and magpie; it rested in the outskirts of Song; wherever it stopped, flocks of birds wing-guarded it, morning and evening holding rice and millet in their beaks to feed it.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn a blue bird resembling a turtledove and magpie rested in the outskirts of Song. Wherever it alighted, other birds guarded it on the wing and fed it rice and millet morning and evening.

sentences.zh: 睢陽之人適野聚觀者旬日，人不知其名，郡人李翱見之曰：「此鸞也，鳳之次。

translations.literal: People of Suiyang going to the fields gathered to watch for ten days; people did not know its name; Li Ao of the commandery, seeing it, said: "This is a luan—next in rank to the phoenix.
translations.idiomatic: For ten days the people of Suiyang thronged the fields to watch, for none knew the bird's name. Li Ao of the commandery declared, "This is a luan—the phoenix's nearest kin.

sentences.zh: 」六月，濮州雷澤縣人張憲家榆樹鳥巢，因風墮二雛，別樹鵲引二鳥雛於巢哺之。

translations.literal: " In the sixth month, in a bird nest in a elm tree at the home of Zhang Xian of Leize County, Puzhou, two nestlings fell because of wind; a magpie from another tree led the two fledglings to its nest and nursed them.
translations.idiomatic: " In the sixth month two nestlings fell from a bird's nest in an elm at the home of Zhang Xian of Leize County, Puzhou, when the wind blew. A magpie from another tree took the fledglings to its own nest and fed them.

sentences.zh: 六月，真興門外野鵲巢于古塚。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, outside Zhenxing Gate a wild magpie nested on an ancient tomb.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month a wild magpie nested on an ancient tomb outside Zhenxing Gate.

sentences.zh: 永徽中，黑齒常之戍河源軍，有狼三頭，白晝入軍門，射之斃。

translations.literal: In the Yonghui era, Heichi Changzhi garrisoned Heyuan Army; three wolves in broad daylight entered the army gate; they were shot and killed.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yonghui era, while Heichi Changzhi was garrisoned at Heyuan Army, three wolves entered the camp gate in broad daylight and were shot dead.

sentences.zh: 常之懼，求代。

translations.literal: Changzhi was afraid and sought a replacement.
translations.idiomatic: Changzhi was alarmed and asked to be relieved.

sentences.zh: 將軍李謹代常之軍，月餘卒。

translations.literal: General Li Jin replaced Changzhi's army; after a little more than a month he died.
translations.idiomatic: General Li Jin took over the garrison from Changzhi and died a little over a month later.

sentences.zh: 先天初，洛陽市人牽一羊，左肋下有人手，長尺許，以之乞丐。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xiantian, a Luoyang market man led a sheep with a human hand beneath its left ribs, about a chi long, using it to beg.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Xiantian era a Luoyang market man led about a sheep with a human hand, about a chi long, growing from beneath its left ribs—and used the deformity to beg for alms.

sentences.zh: ，韶州鼠害稼，千萬為群。

translations.literal: at Shaozhou rats harmed the crops, gathering in groups of tens of millions.
translations.idiomatic: At Shaozhou rats ravaged the crops in swarms of tens of millions.

sentences.zh: 三年，有熊白晝入廣陵城，月餘，都督李處鑒卒。

translations.literal: In the third year, a bear in broad daylight entered Guangling city; after a little more than a month, military governor Li Chujian died.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year a bear entered Guangling city in broad daylight. A little over a month later Military Governor Li Chujian died.

sentences.zh: 十一月，乾陵赤兔見。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, a red hare appeared at Qian Mausoleum.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month a red hare was seen at Qian Mausoleum.

sentences.zh: 三月，河中獻玄狐。

translations.literal: In the third month, Hezhong presented a black fox.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month Hezhong presented a black fox.

sentences.zh: 四年九月己卯，虎入京城長壽坊元載私廟，將軍周皓格殺之。

translations.literal: On jimao day of the ninth month of the fourth year, a tiger entered the private ancestral temple of Yuan Zai in Changshou Ward of the capital; General Zhou Hao struck and killed it.
translations.idiomatic: On the jimao day of the ninth month of the fourth year a tiger entered Yuan Zai's private ancestral shrine in Changshou Ward of the capital. General Zhou Hao killed it.

sentences.zh: 六年八月丁丑，太極殿內廓下獲白兔。

translations.literal: On dingchou day of the eighth month of the sixth year, a white hare was captured beneath the inner corridor of Taiji Hall.
translations.idiomatic: On the dingchou day of the eighth month of the sixth year a white hare was caught beneath the inner corridor of Taiji Hall.

sentences.zh: 八年七月，白鼠出內侍。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the eighth year, a white rat appeared from within the palace attendants' quarters.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of the eighth year a white rat appeared in the inner palace attendants' quarters.

sentences.zh: 十二年六月，苑內獲白鼠。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the twelfth year, a white rat was captured within the park.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of the twelfth year a white rat was caught in the imperial park.

sentences.zh: 十三年六月戊戌，隴右汧源縣軍士趙貴家，貓鼠同乳，不相害，節度使朱泚籠之以獻。

translations.literal: On wuxu day of the sixth month of the thirteenth year, at the home of army soldier Zhao Gui of Qianyuan County, Longyou, cat and rat nursed together without harming each other; military governor Zhu Ci caged them and presented them.
translations.idiomatic: On the wuxu day of the sixth month of the thirteenth year at the home of soldier Zhao Gui of Qianyuan County in Longyou, a cat and a rat nursed together without harming each other. Military Governor Zhu Ci caged them and sent them up as tribute.

sentences.zh: 宰相常袞率百僚拜表賀，中書舍人崔祐甫曰：「此物之失性也。

translations.literal: Chief minister Chang Gun led the hundred officials in submitting a congratulatory memorial; Secretariat drafter Cui Youfu said: "This is these creatures' loss of nature.
translations.idiomatic: Chief Minister Chang Gun led the hundred officials in a congratulatory memorial, but Secretariat Drafter Cui Youfu said, "This is a perversion of nature.

sentences.zh: 天生萬物，剛柔有性，聖人因之，垂訓作則。

translations.literal: Heaven generates the myriad things; hard and soft each have their nature; the sage takes this and extends instruction, making norms.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven creates all things, each with its own hard or soft nature, and the sage takes this as a model for instruction and law.

sentences.zh: 禮，迎貓，為食田鼠也。

translations.literal: In ritual, one welcomes the cat because it eats field mice.
translations.idiomatic: In ritual the cat is welcomed because it devours field mice.

sentences.zh: 然貓之食鼠，載在祀典，以其能除害利人，雖微必錄。

translations.literal: Yet the cat's eating of mice is recorded in the sacrificial canon because it can remove harm and benefit people—even the small must be noted.
translations.idiomatic: The cat's hunting of mice is recorded even in the sacrificial canon, for it removes pests and serves the people—so small a merit is still worth noting.

sentences.zh: 今此貓對鼠，何異法吏不勤觸邪，疆吏不勤捍敵？

translations.literal: Now this cat facing a rat—how is it different from legal officers not diligently exposing evil, or frontier officers not diligently repelling the enemy?
translations.idiomatic: Now a cat that will not touch a mouse—what is that but legal officers who fail to expose corruption, or frontier officers who fail to repel the enemy?

sentences.zh: 據禮部式錄三瑞，無貓不食鼠之目。

translations.literal: According to the Ministry of Rites regulations, three auspicious signs are recorded; there is no entry for a cat that will not eat mice.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of Rites registers three kinds of auspicious signs—and nowhere lists a cat that refuses to eat mice.

sentences.zh: 以此稱慶，理所未詳。

translations.literal: To call this a cause for celebration—the reasoning is not yet clear.
translations.idiomatic: To treat this as grounds for celebration makes no sense at all.

sentences.zh: 以劉向《五行傳》言之，恐須申命憲司，察聽貪吏，誡諸邊境，無失儆巡，則貓能致功，鼠不為害。

translations.literal: Speaking by Liu Xiang's "Treatise on the Five Phases," I fear one must proclaim orders to the censorate, investigate and hear out corrupt officials, warn the frontier regions not to neglect patrol and vigilance—then cats can achieve merit and rats will not become harm.
translations.idiomatic: By the logic of Liu Xiang's Treatise on the Five Phases, we ought rather to charge the censorate to investigate corrupt officials and warn the frontiers not to neglect patrol—then cats will do their work and rats will do no harm.

sentences.zh: 」帝深然之。

translations.literal: " The emperor deeply approved of this.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor strongly agreed.

sentences.zh: 五月，滑洲馬生角。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, a horse at Hua Prefecture grew horns.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month a horse at Hua Prefecture sprouted horns.

sentences.zh: 二月，太僕寺郊牛生犢，六足，太僕卿周皓白宰相李泌，請上聞，泌笑而不答。

translations.literal: In the second month, the suburban ox of the Court of the Imperial Stud calved; the calf had six feet; Court of the Imperial Stud director Zhou Hao informed chief minister Li Bi and asked that the emperor be told; Bi smiled and did not reply.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month the suburban ox of the Court of the Imperial Stud bore a calf with six legs. Director Zhou Hao reported it to Chief Minister Li Bi and asked that the emperor be informed. Bi only smiled and said nothing.

sentences.zh: 又京師人家豕生子，兩首四足，有司以白御史中丞竇參，請上聞，參寢而不奏。

translations.literal: Also in the capital a household's sow farrowed; the piglet had two heads and four feet; the responsible office reported to censor-in-chief Dou Can and asked that the emperor be told; Can shelved it and did not memorialize.
translations.idiomatic: In the capital, too, a household sow farrowed a piglet with two heads and four feet. The responsible office reported it to Censor-in-Chief Dou Can and asked that the emperor be told. Can shelved the report and never submitted it.

sentences.zh: 三月癸丑，鹿入京師西市門，眾殺之。

translations.literal: On guichou day of the third month, a deer entered the Western Market Gate of the capital; the crowd killed it.
translations.idiomatic: On the guichou day of the third month a deer entered the Western Market Gate of the capital, and the crowd killed it.

sentences.zh: 十一月，龍州武安川佘田中嘉禾生，有麟食之，復生。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, in the She fields of Wu'an River, Long Prefecture, auspicious grain grew; a qilin ate it, and it grew again.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month auspicious grain sprang up in the She fields along Wu'an River in Long Prefecture. A qilin ate it, and the grain grew again.

sentences.zh: 麟之來，一鹿引之，群鹿隨之，光華不可正視。

translations.literal: When the qilin came, one deer led it; a herd of deer followed; its radiance could not be looked at directly.
translations.idiomatic: When the qilin came, a deer led the way and a herd followed. Its radiance was too dazzling to meet with the eye.

sentences.zh: 使畫工圖麟及嘉禾來獻。

translations.literal: He sent painters to depict the qilin and the auspicious grain and present them.
translations.idiomatic: He had painters depict the qilin and the auspicious grain and sent the pictures up as tribute.

sentences.zh: 八年四月，長安西市門家豕生子，三耳八足，自尾分為二。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the eighth year, at the Western Market Gate of Chang'an a household sow farrowed; the piglet had three ears and eight feet; from the tail it divided into two.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the eighth year a Chang'an sow near the Western Market Gate farrowed a piglet with three ears and eight legs, its body split in two from the tail.

sentences.zh: 八月，易定監軍小將家馬，因飲水吐出寶珠一，獻之。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, at the home of a junior officer of the Yiding army supervisor, a horse while drinking water spat out one precious pearl; it was presented.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month a horse belonging to a junior officer under the Yiding army supervisor drank water and spat out a precious pearl, which was sent up as tribute.

sentences.zh: 貞觀中，汾州言青龍見，吐物在空中，有光明如火。

translations.literal: In the Zhenguan era, Fen Prefecture reported that a blue dragon appeared, spitting something in midair with brightness like fire.
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhenguan era Fen Prefecture reported that a blue dragon appeared and spat something into the air that blazed like fire.

sentences.zh: 墜地，地陷，掘之得玄金，廣尺，長七寸。

translations.literal: It fell to earth; the ground sank; digging, they obtained dark metal one chi wide and seven cun long.
translations.idiomatic: It fell to earth and the ground collapsed. When they dug they found a block of dark metal a foot wide and seven cun long.

sentences.zh: ，虔州別駕得六眼龜，一夕而失。

translations.literal: the assistant prefect of Qian Prefecture obtained a six-eyed tortoise; in one night it was lost.
translations.idiomatic: The assistant prefect of Qian Prefecture obtained a six-eyed tortoise, which vanished overnight.

sentences.zh: 神龍中，渭河有蛤蟆，大如一石鼎，里人聚觀，數日而失。

translations.literal: In the Shenlong era, in the Wei River there was a toad as large as a stone cauldron; village people gathered to watch; after several days it was gone.
translations.idiomatic: During the Shenlong era a toad as large as a stone cauldron appeared in the Wei River. Villagers gathered to stare, and after several days it was gone.

sentences.zh: 是歲，大水漂溺京城數百家，商州水入城門，襄陽水至樹杪。

translations.literal: That year, great water drowned and swept away several hundred households of the capital; at Shang Prefecture water entered the city gates; at Xiangyang water reached the treetops.
translations.idiomatic: That year floods drowned several hundred households in the capital. At Shang Prefecture water poured through the city gates; at Xiangyang it rose to the treetops.

sentences.zh: 六月，西京朝堂磚階，無故自壞。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, the brick steps of the audience hall in the Western Capital collapsed for no reason.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month the brick steps of the audience hall in the Western Capital collapsed without cause.

sentences.zh: 磚下有大蛇長丈餘，蛤蟆大如盤，面目赤如火，相向鬥。

translations.literal: Beneath the bricks was a great serpent more than a zhang long; a toad as large as a tray; their faces red as fire; they faced each other and fought.
translations.idiomatic: Beneath the bricks lay a serpent more than a zhang long and a toad as large as a tray, both with faces red as fire, fighting face to face.

sentences.zh: 俄而蛇入大樹，蛤蟆入於草。

translations.literal: Soon the serpent entered a great tree; the toad entered the grass.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the serpent slipped into a great tree and the toad vanished into the grass.

sentences.zh: 其年七月三日，玄宗誅竇懷貞、岑羲等十七家。

translations.literal: On the third day of the seventh month of that year, Emperor Xuanzong executed seventeen clans including Dou Huaizhen and Cen Xi.
translations.idiomatic: On the third day of the seventh month that year Emperor Xuanzong executed seventeen clans, including those of Dou Huaizhen and Cen Xi.

sentences.zh: 六月，郴州馬嶺山下，有白蛇長六七尺，黑蛇長丈餘。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, below Maling Mountain in Chen Prefecture, there was a white serpent six or seven chi long and a black serpent more than a zhang long.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, below Maling Mountain in Chen Prefecture, a white serpent six or seven chi long and a black serpent more than a zhang long appeared.

sentences.zh: 兩蛇鬥，白蛇吞黑蛇，至粗處，口眼流血，黑蛇頭穿白蛇腹出，俄而俱死。

translations.literal: The two serpents fought; the white serpent swallowed the black serpent; at the thick part mouth and eyes bled; the black serpent's head pierced through the white serpent's belly and emerged; soon both died.
translations.idiomatic: The two serpents fought. The white serpent swallowed the black one, but at its thickest point blood streamed from mouth and eyes as the black serpent's head burst through the white serpent's belly—and in a moment both were dead.

sentences.zh: 旬日內桂陽大雨，山水暴溢，漂五百家，殺三百餘人。

translations.literal: Within ten days Guiyang had heavy rain; mountains and rivers overflowed violently; five hundred households were swept away; more than three hundred people were killed.
translations.idiomatic: Within ten days Guiyang was deluged; mountain streams burst their banks and swept away five hundred households, killing more than three hundred people.

sentences.zh: 天寶中，洛陽有巨蛇，高丈餘，長百尺，出於芒山下。

translations.literal: In the Tianbao era, at Luoyang there was a giant serpent more than a zhang tall and a hundred chi long, emerging from below Mang Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tianbao era a serpent appeared below Mang Mountain near Luoyang—more than a zhang in height and a hundred chi in length.

sentences.zh: 胡僧無畏見之，歎曰：「此欲決水注洛城。

translations.literal: The foreign monk Wuwei saw it and sighed, saying: "This serpent intends to burst water and pour it into Luoyang city.
translations.idiomatic: The foreign monk Wuwei saw it and sighed: "It means to burst the waters and flood Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 」即以天竺法咒之，數日蛇死。

translations.literal: " He then used Indian dharma to curse it; within days the serpent died.
translations.idiomatic: He cast spells in the Indian manner, and within days the serpent was dead.

sentences.zh: 祿山陷洛之兆也。

translations.literal: It was an omen of An Lushan's capture of Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: This foretold An Lushan's seizure of Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 李揆作相前一月，有大蛤蟆如床，見室之中，俄失所在。

translations.literal: One month before Li Kui became chief minister, there was a great toad the size of a bed, appearing in a room; soon it vanished.
translations.idiomatic: A month before Li Kui became chief minister, a toad as large as a bed appeared in a room—and then was gone.

sentences.zh: 占者以為蟆天使也，有福慶之事。

translations.literal: Diviners took it to be the toad angel, a sign of good fortune and celebration.
translations.idiomatic: Diviners declared it the toad angel and a portent of blessing and joy.

sentences.zh: 九月，通州三岡縣放生池中，日氣下照，水騰波湧上，有黃龍躍出，高丈餘，又于龍旁數處，浮出明珠。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, in the Release-Life Pond of Sangang County, Tong Prefecture, sunlight shone down; water surged upward in waves; a yellow dragon leaped out, more than a zhang high; at several places beside the dragon bright pearls floated up.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, at the Release-Life Pond in Sangang County, Tong Prefecture, sunlight struck the water and waves rose up. A yellow dragon leaped forth, more than a zhang tall, and bright pearls surfaced in several places beside it.

sentences.zh: ，京師金天門外水渠獲毛龜。

translations.literal: At the capital, outside the Golden Heaven Gate, a hairy tortoise was obtained from a water channel.
translations.idiomatic: At the capital a hairy tortoise was taken from a canal outside the Golden Heaven Gate.

sentences.zh: ，李納獻毛龜。

translations.literal: Li Na presented a hairy tortoise.
translations.idiomatic: Li Na sent up a hairy tortoise as tribute.

sentences.zh: 四月，舒州桐城縣有黃、青、白三龍各一，翼風雷自梅天陂起，約高二百尺，凡六里，降於浮塘坡。

translations.literal: In the fourth month, in Tongcheng County, Shu Prefecture, there were one each of yellow, green, and white dragons; riding wind and thunder they rose from Meitian Marsh, about two hundred chi high, for six li in all, descending at Futang Slope.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month at Tongcheng County in Shu Prefecture, one yellow, one green, and one white dragon appeared. Riding wind and thunder they rose from Meitian Marsh to a height of some two hundred chi, traveled six li, and descended at Futang Slope.

sentences.zh: 九年四月，道州二青龍見於江中。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the ninth year, two green dragons appeared in the river at Dao Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the ninth year two green dragons were seen in the river at Dao Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 六月七日，密州卑產山北面有龍見。

translations.literal: On the seventh day of the sixth month, a dragon appeared on the north face of Beichan Mountain, Mi Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: On the seventh day of the sixth month a dragon appeared on the north slope of Beichan Mountain in Mi Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 初，赤龍從西來，續有青龍、黃龍從南來，後有白龍、黑龍從山北來，並形狀分明。

translations.literal: At first a red dragon came from the west; then green and yellow dragons followed from the south; afterward white and black dragons came from the north of the mountain—all with clearly distinct forms.
translations.idiomatic: First a red dragon came from the west; then green and yellow dragons from the south; last white and black dragons from the north of the mountain—all plainly visible.

sentences.zh: 自申至戌，方散去。

translations.literal: From the shen hour to the xu hour, they finally dispersed.
translations.idiomatic: From the shen hour until the xu hour they lingered, then at last dispersed.

sentences.zh: 天寶初，臨川郡人李嘉胤所居柱上生芝草，狀如天尊像，太守張景夫拔柱以獻。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Tianbao era, at the residence of Li Jiayin of Linchuan Commandery, lingzhi fungus grew on a pillar, shaped like an image of the Celestial Worthy; Prefect Zhang Jingfu pulled up the pillar and presented it.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Tianbao era lingzhi sprouted on a pillar at the home of Li Jiayin of Linchuan Commandery, shaped like the Celestial Worthy. Prefect Zhang Jingfu uprooted the pillar and sent it up as tribute.

sentences.zh: 七月甲辰，延英殿御座生白芝，一莖三花。

translations.literal: On jiachen day of the seventh month, white lingzhi grew on the imperial throne in the Yanying Hall—one stem, three flowers.
translations.idiomatic: On the jiachen day of the seventh month white lingzhi appeared on the imperial throne in the Yanying Hall: one stem bearing three flowers.

sentences.zh: 肅宗制《玉靈芝詩》三篇，群臣皆賀。

translations.literal: Emperor Suzong composed three poems titled "Jade Lingzhi"; all ministers offered congratulations.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Suzong wrote three "Jade Lingzhi" poems, and the whole court offered congratulations.

sentences.zh: 占曰：「白芝主喪。

translations.literal: The omen readers said: "White lingzhi presages mourning.
translations.idiomatic: The diviners said: "White lingzhi foretells mourning.

sentences.zh: 」明年，上皇、肅宗俱崩。

translations.literal: " The following year, both the Retired Emperor and Emperor Suzong died.
translations.idiomatic: " The next year both the Retired Emperor and Emperor Suzong died.

sentences.zh: 二年九月，含輝院生金芝。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the second year, golden lingzhi grew in Hanhui Academy.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of the second year golden lingzhi appeared in Hanhui Academy.

sentences.zh: 二月，京城槐樹有蟲食葉，其形類蠶。

translations.literal: In the second month, on locust trees in the capital worms ate the leaves; their shape resembled silkworms.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month worms shaped like silkworms devoured the leaves of the capital's locust trees.

sentences.zh: 其年六月，太廟第二室芝草生。

translations.literal: That year in the sixth month, lingzhi grew in the second chamber of the Imperial Ancestral Temple.
translations.idiomatic: That same year, in the sixth month, lingzhi sprouted in the second chamber of the Imperial Ancestral Temple.

sentences.zh: 三月，潤州上元縣芝草生，一莖四葉，高七寸。

translations.literal: In the third month, lingzhi grew in Shangyuan County, Run Prefecture—one stem, four leaves, seven cun high.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month lingzhi appeared in Shangyuan County, Run Prefecture: one stem with four leaves, seven cun tall.

sentences.zh: 八年，廬州廬江縣紫芝生，高一丈五尺。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, purple lingzhi grew in Lujiang County, Lu Prefecture, one zhang five chi high.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year purple lingzhi sprouted in Lujiang County, Lu Prefecture, standing a zhang and five chi tall.

sentences.zh: 九年九月，晉州神山縣慶唐觀檜樹已枯重榮。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the ninth year, at Qingtang Abbey in Shenshan County, Jin Prefecture, a cypress tree that had withered flourished again.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of the ninth year a withered cypress at Qingtang Abbey in Shenshan County, Jin Prefecture, put forth fresh growth.

sentences.zh: 十二年五月甲子，成都府人郭遠，因樵獲瑞木一莖，有文曰「天下太平」四字，其年十一月，蔡州汝陽縣芝草生，紫莖黃蓋。

translations.literal: On jiazi day of the fifth month of the twelfth year, Guo Yuan of Chengdu Prefecture while gathering firewood obtained one stalk of auspicious wood with characters reading "All Under Heaven at Peace"—four characters; that year in the eleventh month lingzhi grew in Ruyang County, Cai Prefecture, with purple stems and yellow caps.
translations.idiomatic: On the jiazi day of the fifth month of the twelfth year Guo Yuan of Chengdu Prefecture, out gathering firewood, found a stalk of auspicious wood inscribed with the four characters "All Under Heaven at Peace." That same year, in the eleventh month, lingzhi with purple stems and yellow caps appeared in Ruyang County, Cai Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 八月，亳州真源縣大空寺僧院李樹，種來十四年，才長一丈八尺，今春枝忽上聳，高六尺，周圍似蓋，九尺餘。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, a plum tree in the monks' courtyard of Dakong Temple in Zhenyuan County, Bo Prefecture, planted fourteen years earlier had grown only one zhang eight chi; this spring the branches suddenly thrust upward six chi high, spreading around like a canopy for more than nine chi.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, at Dakong Temple in Zhenyuan County, Bo Prefecture, a plum tree planted fourteen years before had reached only a zhang and eight chi. That spring its branches suddenly shot up six chi and spread outward like a canopy more than nine chi wide.

sentences.zh: 又先天太后墓槐樹上有靈泉漏出，今年六月，其上有雲氣五色，又黃龍再見於泉上。

translations.literal: Also at the tomb of the Primordial Heavenly Empress a numinous spring leaked out on a locust tree; this year in the sixth month clouds of five colors appeared above it, and a yellow dragon was seen again above the spring.
translations.idiomatic: At the tomb of the Primordial Heavenly Empress a numinous spring had begun to seep from a locust tree. That sixth month five-colored clouds gathered above it, and a yellow dragon appeared once more over the spring.

sentences.zh: 十二月雷，桃李俱花。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month there was thunder; peach and plum trees all bloomed.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month thunder rolled and peach and plum trees burst into bloom.

sentences.zh: 十二月，水不冰，草萌芽，如正二月之候。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month water did not freeze; grass sprouted—like the season of the first and second months.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month the waters did not freeze and grass put forth shoots, as though it were the first or second month of spring.

sentences.zh: 三月，洛陽東七里有水影，側近樹木車馬之影，歷歷見水影中，月餘方滅。

translations.literal: In the third month, seven li east of Luoyang there was a water reflection; the shadows of nearby trees, horses, and carriages were clearly visible in the water reflection; after more than a month it vanished.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, seven li east of Luoyang, a pool of water reflected with perfect clarity the shadows of nearby trees, horses, and carriages. More than a month passed before it disappeared.

sentences.zh: 七月，嵐州合河關黃河水，四十里間，清如井水，經四日而後復。

translations.literal: In the seventh month, at the Yellow River at Hehe Pass, Lan Prefecture, for forty li the water was as clear as well water; after four days it returned to normal.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month the Yellow River at Hehe Pass in Lan Prefecture ran clear as well water for forty li; after four days it turned muddy again.

sentences.zh: 九月甲午，華州至陝州二百餘里，黃河清，澄澈見底。

translations.literal: On jiawu day of the ninth month, for more than two hundred li from Hua Prefecture to Shan Prefecture the Yellow River was clear, transparent to the bottom.
translations.idiomatic: On the jiawu day of the ninth month the Yellow River ran clear for more than two hundred li from Hua Prefecture to Shan Prefecture, so transparent one could see the bottom.

sentences.zh: ，醴泉出櫟陽，愈疾。

translations.literal: Sweet springs appeared at Liyang, curing illness.
translations.idiomatic: Sweet springs appeared at Liyang and cured the sick.

sentences.zh: 七月，自陝州至河陰，河水色如墨，流入汴河，止於汴州城下，一宿而復。

translations.literal: In the seventh month, from Shan Prefecture to Heyin the river water was dark as ink, flowing into the Bian River and stopping below Bian Prefecture city; after one night it returned to normal.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month the river from Shan Prefecture to Heyin turned black as ink, poured into the Bian River, and pooled below Bian Prefecture city; one night later it cleared.

sentences.zh: ，亳州言出聖水愈病。

translations.literal: Bo Prefecture reported that sacred water appeared and cured illness.
translations.idiomatic: Bo Prefecture reported sacred water that healed the sick.

sentences.zh: 江淮已南，遠來奔湊求水。

translations.literal: South of the Yangtze and Huai, people came from afar rushing to seek the water.
translations.idiomatic: From south of the Yangtze and Huai people traveled great distances to crowd in and fetch the water.

sentences.zh: 浙西觀察使李德裕奏論其妖。

translations.literal: Zhedong Circuit Observation Commissioner Li Deyu memorialized discussing its malevolent character.
translations.idiomatic: Li Deyu, observation commissioner of Zhedong Circuit, memorialized that the phenomenon was an evil portent.

sentences.zh: 宰相裴度判汴州所申狀曰：「妖由人興，水不自作。

translations.literal: Chief Minister Pei Du judged the report from Bian Prefecture, saying: "Portents arise from men; water does not stir itself.
translations.idiomatic: Chief Minister Pei Du ruled on Bian Prefecture's report: "Portents are raised by men; water does not move of its own accord.

sentences.zh: 」牒汴州觀察使填塞訖申。

translations.literal: " He dispatched the Bianzhou Observation Commissioner to fill and seal it, then report completion.
translations.idiomatic: " He ordered the observation commissioner of Bianzhou to fill the site in and report when the work was done.

sentences.zh: 玄宗初即位，東都白馬寺鐵像頭無故自落於殿門外。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xuanzong first took the throne, the iron Buddha head at White Horse Temple in the Eastern Capital fell without cause outside the hall gate.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xuanzong first ascended the throne, the iron Buddha's head at White Horse Temple in the Eastern Capital fell for no apparent reason outside the hall gate.

sentences.zh: 後姚崇秉政，以僧惠范附太平亂政，謀汰僧尼，令拜父母，午後不出院，其法頗峻。

translations.literal: Later when Yao Chong held power, because the monk Huifan attached to Taiping and disturbed government, he planned to purge monks and nuns, requiring them to bow to parents and not leave the monastery after noon—the regulations quite strict.
translations.idiomatic: Later, under Yao Chong's administration, the monk Huifan had attached himself to Princess Taiping and meddled in government. Chong sought to purge monks and nuns, requiring them to bow to their parents and forbidding them to leave their monasteries after noon—harsh measures indeed.

sentences.zh: 二月，太僕寺廨有佛堂，堂內小脫空金剛左臂上忽有黑汗滴下，以紙承色，色即血也。

translations.literal: In the second month, at a Buddhist hall in the offices of the Court of the Imperial Stud, on the left arm of a small hollow gilt bronze guardian statue black sweat suddenly dripped; paper was used to catch the color—it was blood.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, in a Buddhist hall within the Court of the Imperial Stud offices, black sweat suddenly dripped from the left arm of a small hollow gilt guardian statue. Paper caught the drops—they were blood.

sentences.zh: 明年五月，代宗崩。

translations.literal: The next year in the fifth month Emperor Daizong died.
translations.idiomatic: The following fifth month Emperor Daizong died.

sentences.zh: ，楚州刺史崔侁獻定國寶十三：一曰玄黃天符，形如笏，長八寸，有孔，辟人間兵疫；

translations.literal: Chuzhou Prefecture Inspector Cui Qian presented thirteen treasures of the realm: first, the Black-and-Yellow Heavenly Talisman, shaped like a tablet, eight cun long, with a hole, warding off war and pestilence among men;
translations.idiomatic: Cui Qian, prefect of Chuzhou, presented thirteen state treasures. First: the Black-and-Yellow Heavenly Talisman, tablet-shaped, eight cun long, pierced with a hole, said to ward off war and pestilence among men;

sentences.zh: 二曰玉雞毛，白玉也，以孝理天下則見；

translations.literal: second, the Jade Cock Feather, of white jade—when the realm is governed by filial piety it appears;
translations.idiomatic: second, the Jade Cock Feather of white jade, which appears when the realm is ruled by filial piety;

sentences.zh: 三曰谷璧，白玉也，粟粒，無雕鐫之跡，王者得之，五穀豐熟；

translations.literal: third, the Grain Disc, of white jade, millet-grain pattern with no trace of carving—when the king obtains it the five grains ripen abundantly;
translations.idiomatic: third, the Grain Disc of white jade, patterned like millet grains with no sign of carving—when a king possesses it the five grains flourish;

sentences.zh: 四曰西王母白環二，所在處外國歸伏；

translations.literal: fourth, two White Rings of the Queen Mother of the West—wherever they are located foreign lands submit;
translations.idiomatic: fourth, two white rings of the Queen Mother of the West—wherever they rest foreign peoples submit;

sentences.zh: 五曰碧色寶，圓而有光；

translations.literal: fifth, the Green Treasure, round and luminous;
translations.idiomatic: fifth, a green gem, round and radiant;

sentences.zh: 六曰如意寶珠，大如雞卵；

translations.literal: sixth, the Wish-Fulfilling Pearl, large as a hen's egg;
translations.idiomatic: sixth, a wish-fulfilling pearl the size of a hen's egg;

sentences.zh: 七曰紅色靺鞨，大如巨栗；

translations.literal: seventh, red mokling, large as a great chestnut;
translations.idiomatic: seventh, a red mokling stone as large as a great chestnut;

sentences.zh: 八曰琅玕珠二；

translations.literal: eighth, two langgan pearls;
translations.idiomatic: eighth, two langgan pearls;

sentences.zh: 九曰玉玦，形如玉環，四分缺一；

translations.literal: ninth, the jade tablet, shaped like a jade ring with one quarter missing;
translations.idiomatic: ninth, a jade tablet shaped like a ring missing a quarter;

sentences.zh: 十曰玉印，大如半手，理如鹿形，陷入印中；

translations.literal: tenth, the jade seal, large as half a hand, its grain like a deer shape sunk into the seal;
translations.idiomatic: tenth, a jade seal half the size of a palm, veined like a deer sunk into the stone;

sentences.zh: 十一曰皇后采桑鉤，如箸，屈其末；

translations.literal: eleventh, the empress's silkworm-gathering hook, like a chopstick, bent at the tip;
translations.idiomatic: eleventh, the empress's silkworm-gathering hook, chopstick-thin with a bent tip;

sentences.zh: 十二曰雷公石斧，無孔；

translations.literal: twelfth, Lord Thunder's stone axe, without a hole;
translations.idiomatic: twelfth, Lord Thunder's stone axe, without a hole;

sentences.zh: 十三缺。

translations.literal: the thirteenth is missing.
translations.idiomatic: the thirteenth is lost.

sentences.zh: 凡十三寶。

translations.literal: In all, thirteen treasures.
translations.idiomatic: Thirteen treasures in all.

sentences.zh: 置之日中，白氣連天。

translations.literal: When placed in the sun, white vapor joined heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Set in the sunlight, they sent white vapor up to the sky.

sentences.zh: 初，楚州有尼曰真如，忽有人接之升天，天帝謂之曰：「下方有災，令第二寶鎮之。

translations.literal: At first, in Chuzhou there was a nun named Zhenru; suddenly someone took her up to heaven; the Heavenly Emperor said to her: "Below there is disaster; let the second treasure suppress it.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, in Chuzhou, there was a nun named Zhenru. Suddenly someone lifted her to heaven, and the Heavenly Emperor told her: "Disaster threatens below; let the second treasure hold it in check.

sentences.zh: 」即以十三寶付真如。

translations.literal: " He then entrusted the thirteen treasures to Zhenru.
translations.idiomatic: " He then entrusted all thirteen treasures to Zhenru.

sentences.zh: 時肅宗方不豫，以為瑞，乃改元寶應，仍傳位皇太子，此近白祥也。

translations.literal: At that time Emperor Suzong was already unwell; taking this as an auspicious sign, he changed the era name to Baoying and still transferred the throne to the crown prince—this was a recent white auspice.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Suzong was then already ill. Taking this as a blessing, he changed the era name to Baoying and abdicated in favor of the crown prince—a recent white portent indeed.

sentences.zh: 五月，神策軍修苑內古漢宮，掘得白玉床，其長六尺，以獻。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, the Shence Army while repairing the ancient Han palace within the imperial park dug up a white jade couch six chi long and presented it.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, while repairing the ancient Han palace in the imperial park, the Shence Army unearthed a white jade couch six chi long and sent it up as tribute.

sentences.zh: 二月，京兆神策昭應婦人張氏，產一男二女。

translations.literal: In the second month, Zhang the woman of Zhaoying in Jingzhao Shence bore one son and two daughters.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month Zhang, a woman of Zhaoying in Jingzhao Shence, gave birth to one son and two daughters.

sentences.zh: 二月，許州人李狗兒持杖上含元殿，擊欄檻，又擊殺所擒卒，誅之。

translations.literal: In the second month, Li Gou'er of Xu Prefecture took a staff, ascended the Hanyuan Hall, struck the railing, and also killed a captured soldier; he was executed.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month Li Gou'er of Xu Prefecture climbed the Hanyuan Hall with a staff, beat the railings, and killed a soldier he had seized. He was put to death.

sentences.zh: 十年四月，巨人跡見常州。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the tenth year, giant footprints appeared at Chang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the tenth year giant footprints were seen at Chang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: ，開紅崖冶役夫將化為虎，眾以水沃之，化而不果。

translations.literal: At Kaihong Cliff ironworks a corvee laborer was about to transform into a tiger; the crowd drenched him with water, and the transformation did not succeed.
translations.idiomatic: At Kaihong Cliff a corvee laborer at the ironworks was turning into a tiger; the crowd poured water over him and the transformation failed.

sentences.zh: 四月十七日，染坊作人張韶與卜者蘇玄明，于柴草車內藏兵仗，入宮作亂，二人對食於清思殿。

translations.literal: On the seventeenth day of the fourth month, the dyeworker Zhang Shao and the diviner Su Xuanming hid weapons in a firewood cart, entered the palace to raise rebellion, and the two dined facing each other in the Qingsi Hall.
translations.idiomatic: On the seventeenth day of the fourth month the dyeworker Zhang Shao and the diviner Su Xuanming concealed weapons in a cart of firewood, entered the palace to rebel, and sat down to eat together in the Qingsi Hall.

sentences.zh: 是日，禁軍誅張韶等三十七人。

translations.literal: That day the palace guard executed Zhang Shao and thirty-six others.
translations.idiomatic: That day the palace guard executed Zhang Shao and thirty-six others.

sentences.zh: 十二月，延州人賀文妻產三男。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, the wife of He Wen of Yan Prefecture gave birth to three sons.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month the wife of He Wen of Yan Prefecture bore three sons.

sentences.zh: ，京師訛言鄭注為主上合金丹，須小兒心肝，密旨捕小兒。

translations.literal: In the capital a rumor spread that Zheng Zhu was compounding elixir pills for the emperor and needed the hearts and livers of small children; a secret order was capturing small children.
translations.idiomatic: In the capital a rumor spread that Zheng Zhu was refining elixir pills for the emperor and required the hearts and livers of small children, and that a secret order had gone out to seize them.

sentences.zh: 或相告云，某處失幾兒。

translations.literal: People told one another, "So many children lost at such and such a place."
translations.idiomatic: People whispered to one another that children had vanished here and there.

sentences.zh: 人家扃鎖小兒甚密。

translations.literal: Households locked their small children very tightly.
translations.idiomatic: Families bolted their doors and kept their children under close guard.

sentences.zh: 上恐，遣中使喻之，乃止。

translations.literal: The emperor was alarmed; he sent palace envoys to explain; only then did it stop.
translations.idiomatic: Alarmed, the emperor sent palace envoys to reassure the people, and the panic subsided.

sentences.zh: 十二月二十八日，狂人劉德廣入含元殿，詔付京兆府杖殺之。

translations.literal: On the twenty-eighth day of the twelfth month, the madman Liu Deguang entered the Hanyuan Hall; an edict entrusted him to the Jingzhao Prefecture to be beaten to death.
translations.idiomatic: On the twenty-eighth day of the twelfth month the madman Liu Deguang entered the Hanyuan Hall. An edict handed him over to Jingzhao Prefecture to be beaten to death.

sentences.zh: 隋末有謠云：「桃李子，洪水繞楊山。

translations.literal: At the end of Sui there was a rhyme: "Peach and Li sons, flood waters encircle Yang Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Sui a rhyme ran: "Peach-and-plum child, floodwaters circle Yang Mountain.

sentences.zh: 」煬帝疑李氏有受命之符，故誅李金才。

translations.literal: " Emperor Yang suspected the Li clan had a mandate token, and therefore executed Li Jincai.
translations.idiomatic: " Emperor Yang suspected the Li clan possessed the token of Heaven's mandate and therefore executed Li Jincai.

sentences.zh: 後李密據洛口倉以應其讖。

translations.literal: Later Li Mi seized Luokou Granary in fulfillment of the prophecy.
translations.idiomatic: Later Li Mi seized Luokou Granary, fulfilling the prophecy.

sentences.zh: 隋文時，自長安故城東南移于唐興村置新都，今西內承天門正當唐興村門。

translations.literal: In Emperor Wen's time, the capital was moved southeast from the old Chang'an city to Tangxing Village to establish the new capital; today the Chengtian Gate of the inner western palace directly faces the gate of Tangxing Village.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Wen the capital was moved southeast from old Chang'an to Tangxing Village to build the new city. Today the Chengtian Gate of the inner western palace stands directly opposite Tangxing Village's gate.

sentences.zh: 今有大槐樹，柯枝森鬱，即村門樹也。

translations.literal: Today there is a great locust tree, its branches dense—this was the village gate tree.
translations.idiomatic: A great locust tree still stands there, its branches thick and dark—the tree that once marked the village gate.

sentences.zh: 有司以行列不正，將去之，文帝曰：「高祖嘗坐此樹下，不可去也。

translations.literal: The relevant office, because its row alignment was incorrect, was about to remove it; Emperor Wen said: "Grandfather once sat beneath this tree—it cannot be removed.
translations.idiomatic: Because the tree stood out of line, the authorities meant to cut it down. Emperor Wen said: "Our Grandfather once sat beneath this tree. It must not be removed.

sentences.zh: 」調露中，高宗欲封嵩山，累草儀注，有事不行。

translations.literal: " In the Diaolu era Emperor Gaozong wished to perform the feng and shan rites at Mount Song; he repeatedly drafted ritual protocols but the matter was not carried out.
translations.idiomatic: " During the Diaolu era Emperor Gaozong wished to perform the feng and shan rites on Mount Song. He drafted ritual protocols again and again, but the ceremony never took place.

sentences.zh: 有謠曰：「不畏登不得，但恐不得登。

translations.literal: There was a rhyme: "Not afraid of being unable to ascend—only afraid of being unable to finish the ascent.
translations.idiomatic: A rhyme said: "Not afraid you cannot climb—only afraid you cannot finish the climb.

sentences.zh: 三度徵兵馬，旁道打騰騰。

translations.literal: Three times conscripting troops and horses, and beating tengteng on the side road.
translations.idiomatic: Three times conscripting troops and horses, and beating tengteng drums on the side road.

sentences.zh: 」高宗至山下遘疾，還宮而崩。

translations.literal: " When Gaozong reached the foot of the mountain he fell ill, returned to the palace, and died.
translations.idiomatic: " Gaozong reached the foot of the mountain, fell ill, returned to the palace, and died.

sentences.zh: 永徽末，里歌有《桑條韋也》、《女時韋也》樂。

translations.literal: At the end of the Yonghui era, village songs included the tunes "Sangtiao Wei Ye" and "Nüshi Wei Ye."
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Yonghui era village songs included the tunes "Mulberry Branch and Wei" and "When the Girl Wei."

sentences.zh: 及神龍中，韋後用事，鄭愔作《桑條歌》十篇上之。

translations.literal: During the Shenlong era Empress Wei held power; Zheng Yin composed ten "Sangtiao Songs" and presented them.
translations.idiomatic: During the Shenlong era, when Empress Wei held power, Zheng Yin composed ten "Mulberry Branch Songs" and presented them to the court.

sentences.zh: 龍朔中，俗中飲酒令，曰：「子母去離，連臺龍抝倒。

translations.literal: In the Longshuo era, among drinking games in popular custom was: "Mother and child part, overturn the connected platform dragon.
translations.idiomatic: In the Longshuo era a popular drinking game ran: "Mother and child part ways; overturn the linked platform dragon.

sentences.zh: 」俗謂杯盤為子母，又名盤為臺，即中宗廢于房州之應也。

translations.literal: " Popular speech called cup and plate mother and child, and also called the plate a platform—this answered to Zhongzong's deposition to Fang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: " People called cup and plate "mother and child," and also called the plate a "platform"—a prophecy fulfilled when Zhongzong was deposed to Fang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 時里歌有《突厥鹽》，及則天遣尚書閻知微送武延秀，立知微為可汗，挾之入寇。

translations.literal: At the time village songs had "Turkic Salt"; then Empress Wu dispatched Minister Yan Zhiwei to escort Wu Yanxiu and installed Zhiwei as khan, leading them in invasion.
translations.idiomatic: Village songs then included "Turkic Salt." Later Empress Wu sent Minister Yan Zhiwei to escort Wu Yanxiu, installed Zhiwei as khan, and led them in raiding the borders.

sentences.zh: 如意初，里歌云：「黃麞黃麞草裏藏，彎弓射爾傷。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Ruyi era a village song said: "Yellow stag, yellow stag hiding in the grass, bend the bow and shoot you wounded.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Ruyi era a village song ran: "Yellow stag, yellow stag hiding in the grass—bend the bow and shoot you down wounded.

sentences.zh: 」後契丹李萬榮叛，陷營州，則天令總管曹仁師、王孝傑等將兵百萬討之，大敗于黃麞穀，契丹乘勝至趙郡。

translations.literal: " Later the Khitan Li Wanrong rebelled and captured Ying Prefecture; Empress Wu ordered generals Cao Renshi, Wang Xiaojie, and others to lead a million troops against him; they suffered great defeat at Yellow Stag Valley; the Khitan pressed the victory to Zhao Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: " Later the Khitan Li Wanrong rebelled and seized Ying Prefecture. Empress Wu ordered Generals Cao Renshi, Wang Xiaojie, and others to march a million men against him. They were routed at Yellow Stag Valley, and the Khitan pressed their victory as far as Zhao Commandery.

sentences.zh: 垂拱已後，東都有《契苾兒歌》，皆淫豔之詞。

translations.literal: After Chuigong, in the Eastern Capital there was the "Qibi Song"—all licentious words.
translations.idiomatic: After the Chuigong era the Eastern Capital had the "Qibi Song," full of licentious verses.

sentences.zh: 後張易之兄弟有內嬖，易之小字契苾。

translations.literal: Later Zhang Yizhi and his brothers had imperial favor; Yizhi's childhood name was Qibi.
translations.idiomatic: Later Zhang Yizhi and his brothers became imperial favorites; Yizhi's childhood name was Qibi.

sentences.zh: 元和小兒謠云：「打麥打麥三三三」，乃轉身曰：「舞了也。

translations.literal: In the Yuanhe era a children's rhyme said: "Thresh wheat, thresh wheat, three three three"—then turning around: "The dance is done.
translations.idiomatic: In the Yuanhe era children chanted: "Thresh wheat, thresh wheat, three-three-three"—then, turning around: "The dance is done.

sentences.zh: 」及武元衡為盜所害，是六月三日。

translations.literal: " When Wu Yuanheng was killed by bandits, it was on the third day of the sixth month.
translations.idiomatic: " Wu Yuanheng was murdered by bandits on the third day of the sixth month.

sentences.zh: 《五行傳》所謂詩妖，皆此類也。

translations.literal: What the Treatise on the Five Phases calls "poetry portents" are all of this kind.
translations.idiomatic: These are all examples of what the Treatise on the Five Phases calls "poetry portents."

sentences.zh: 上元中為服令，九品已上佩刀礪等袋，紛帨為魚形，結帛作之，為魚像鯉，強之意也。

translations.literal: In the Shangyuan era a dress regulation was made: officials of the ninth rank and above wore bags for knife, whetstone, and the like; the sash ends were made in fish shape, knotted from silk, the fish resembling carp—meaning strength.
translations.idiomatic: In the Shangyuan era a dress regulation required officials of the ninth rank and above to wear bags for knife and whetstone. The sash ends were knotted from silk in the shape of fish resembling carp, symbolizing strength.

sentences.zh: 則天時此制遂絕，景雲後又佩之。

translations.literal: In Empress Wu's time this regulation ceased; after the Jingyun era it was worn again.
translations.idiomatic: During Empress Wu's reign this regulation lapsed; after the Jingyun era it was worn again.

sentences.zh: 張易之為母阿臧為七寶帳，有魚龍鸞鳳之形，仍為象床、犀簟。

translations.literal: Zhang Yizhi made for his mother Azang a canopy of the seven treasures with forms of fish, dragons, luan birds, and phoenixes, and also an ivory bed and rhinoceros mat.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yizhi had made for his mother Azang a canopy of the seven treasures adorned with fish, dragons, luan birds, and phoenixes, along with an ivory bed and a rhinoceros-horn mat.

sentences.zh: 則天令鳳閣侍郎李迥秀妻之，迥秀不獲已，然心惡其老，薄之。

translations.literal: Empress Wu ordered Fengge Vice Minister Li Jiongxiu to marry her; Jiongxiu could not refuse, yet in his heart he detested her age and treated her coldly.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Wu ordered Fengge Vice Minister Li Jiongxiu to marry her. Jiongxiu could not refuse, yet he resented her age in his heart and treated her coldly.

sentences.zh: 阿臧怒，出迥秀為定州刺史。

translations.literal: Azang was enraged and had Jiongxiu sent out as prefect of Ding Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Azang was enraged and had Jiongxiu posted out as prefect of Ding Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 中宗女安樂公主，有尚方織成毛裙，合百鳥毛，正看為一色，旁看為一色，日中為一色，影中為一色，百鳥之狀，並見裙中。

translations.literal: Emperor Zhongzong's daughter Princess Anle had a feather skirt woven by the Palace Workshops, combining the feathers of a hundred birds: viewed straight on it was one color, viewed from the side another, in sunlight one color, in shadow another—the forms of all the birds appeared together in the skirt.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Zhongzong's daughter, Princess Anle, owned a feather skirt woven by the Palace Workshops from the plumage of a hundred birds. Viewed straight on it showed one color, from the side another, in sunlight one hue, in shadow another—the forms of all the birds could be seen together in the skirt.

sentences.zh: 凡造兩腰，一獻韋氏，計價百萬。

translations.literal: Two were made in all; one was presented to the Wei clan, priced at a million.
translations.idiomatic: Two were made in all; one was presented to the Wei clan, at a cost of a million cash.

sentences.zh: 又令尚方取百獸毛為韉面，視之各見本獸形。

translations.literal: She also ordered the Palace Workshops to take the fur of a hundred beasts for saddle flaps; viewed closely, each showed the form of its beast.
translations.idiomatic: She also ordered the Palace Workshops to make saddle flaps from the fur of a hundred beasts; viewed closely, each showed the form of its original animal.

sentences.zh: 韋後又集鳥毛為韉面。

translations.literal: Empress Wei in turn gathered bird feathers for saddle flaps.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Wei in turn had saddle flaps made from gathered bird feathers.

sentences.zh: 安樂初出降武延秀，蜀川獻單絲碧羅籠裙，縷金為花鳥，細如絲髮，鳥子大如黍米，眼鼻嘴甲俱成，明目者方見之。

translations.literal: When Anle was first married to Wu Yanxiu, Shu presented a cage-skirt of single-thread green gauze; gold filigree formed flowers and birds fine as silk hair, the birds the size of millet grains, eyes, nose, beak, and claws all complete—only those with sharp sight could see them.
translations.idiomatic: When Anle was first married to Wu Yanxiu, Shu presented a cage-skirt of single-thread green gauze with gold filigree flowers and birds fine as silk hair. The birds were the size of millet grains, with eyes, nose, beak, and claws all complete—only those with sharp sight could make them out.

sentences.zh: 自安樂公主作毛裙，百官之家多效之。

translations.literal: From the time Princess Anle made feather skirts, many officials' households imitated her.
translations.idiomatic: After Princess Anle made feather skirts, many officials' households followed her example.

sentences.zh: 江嶺奇禽異獸毛羽，采之殆盡。

translations.literal: The feathers and pelts of rare birds and beasts in the Jiang ranges and Ling mountains were gathered nearly to exhaustion.
translations.idiomatic: The feathers and pelts of rare birds and beasts in the Jiang ranges and Ling mountains were gathered nearly to exhaustion.

sentences.zh: 開元初，姚、宋執政，屢以奢靡為諫，玄宗悉命宮中出奇服，焚之於殿廷，不許士庶服錦繡珠翠之服。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Kaiyuan, Yao and Song held power and repeatedly remonstrated about extravagance; Emperor Xuanzong ordered all extraordinary garments brought out from the palace and burned in the court hall, forbidding gentry and commoners to wear brocade, embroidery, pearls, and jade adornment.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Kaiyuan, Yao Chong and Song Jing held power and repeatedly remonstrated against extravagance. Emperor Xuanzong ordered all extraordinary garments brought out from the palace and burned in the court hall, forbidding gentry and commoners to wear brocade, embroidery, pearls, and jade adornment.

sentences.zh: 自是採捕漸息，風教日淳。

translations.literal: From this gathering and hunting gradually ceased, and customs daily grew pure.
translations.idiomatic: From this time gathering and hunting gradually ceased, and customs grew purer day by day.

sentences.zh: 韋庶人妹七姨，嫁將軍馮太和，權傾人主，嘗為豹頭枕以辟邪，白澤枕以辟魅，伏熊枕以宜男。

translations.literal: The seventh aunt of Empress Wei the commoner, who married General Feng Taihe, wielded power rivaling the ruler; she once had a leopard-head pillow to ward off evil, a white-unicorn pillow to ward off demons, and a crouching-bear pillow to favor sons.
translations.idiomatic: The seventh aunt of Empress Wei, who married General Feng Taihe, wielded power rivaling the sovereign. She once used a leopard-head pillow to ward off evil, a white-unicorn pillow to ward off demons, and a crouching-bear pillow to favor the birth of sons.

sentences.zh: 太和死。

translations.literal: Taihe died.
translations.idiomatic: Taihe died.

sentences.zh: 再嫁嗣虢王。

translations.literal: She remarried the heir to the Prince of Guo.
translations.idiomatic: She remarried the heir to the Prince of Guo.

sentences.zh: 及玄宗誅韋後，虢王斬七姨首以獻。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xuanzong executed Empress Wei, the Prince of Guo beheaded the seventh aunt and presented her head.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xuanzong executed Empress Wei, the Prince of Guo beheaded the seventh aunt and presented her head.
